Kong does currently like to jump up so a family with experience around large breeds would be beneficial. Kong is a sweet boy and always greets staff in the morning with a blanket in his mouth and a very waggy tail!

Kong came into our care as a stray from another kennels so we don’t have any history on him or know if he has lived in a home before. Due to this and his size, Kong is best to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Kong has interacted well with friendly dogs whilst in our care but can be very boisterous and over the top. He will need continuous socialisation to help train him to react appropriately around dogs. He could potentially be rehomed with another dog that has a calm and friendly temperament but it is preferred for him to be the only dog in the home so that he can get all of the attention to help with his training. This would be subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Ziggy
description:
Ziggy is full of life  and energy as he is a young boy. He is a super friendly boy, with a big personality and absolutely loves playing in our enclosed area chasing balls around. At times Ziggy can get a little mouthy and will need his new family to continue helping him learn manners. With Ziggy still being young and high energy, he would need an active home who are able to give him the exercise he needs along with mental stimulation.

Whilst in our care Ziggy has socialised really well with other dogs and often enjoys his daily walks alongside them. For this reason, we do believe he could potentially live with another dog, able to keep up with his high energy levels – subject to a successful meet.

Ziggy wouldn’t be suitable to live with cat or any small animals.

Due to Ziggy coming into our care as a stray, we don’t have any previous history on him. Ziggy would be best suited to an experienced home, ideally having knowledge of his breed, with children no younger than 16 years old – subject to a successful meet.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Duke
description:
This lovely boy is Duke!  He is looking for a patient and understanding home where he can truly thrive.  When he first came into us he was very nervous, but given the time and space to build trust his friendly and affectionate nature shines through.  He can be quite vocal and will bark to let you know when he’d like some attention.  When he gets over excited or over stimulated he can become a little mouthy, so he will need owners who can calmly redirect this behaviour and continue his training and socialisation.  He already knows some basic commands and is eager to engage.  Being a large, strong boy, he does pull on the lead, so he will benefit from ongoing lead training and someone confident enough to manage his strength.  He is currently unsure around other dogs and would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where his new adopter can continue his socialisation with other dogs in a controlled environment with lots of positive reinforcement.  This handsome lad is looking for an active home, that can provide patience, consistency and plenty of exercise and mental enrichment.  He will need a private secure garden.

As he came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Raven
description:
Raven is a gentle, sweet-natured girl looking for a patient and understanding home where she can build her confidence at her own pace.

She has been no trouble in our care and has no issues with feeding or cleaning. When she first arrived, she was extremely nervous and wouldn’t approach for attention. By day five she had made small steps, coming over for a sniff, but she is still very worried about being stroked and is understandably wary of new people, often keeping her tail tucked between her legs.

As Raven came into our care as a stray, we don’t know what she may have experienced in the past, but it’s clear she will need kind, committed owners who are willing to give her the time, patience and reassurance she needs to flourish.

Although she has coped around other dogs in our environment, she is very unsure of them and would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where she can have her own space and settle without added pressure.

With time, patience and plenty of love, Raven has every chance of growing in confidence and becoming a wonderful, loyal companion.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, he has a submissive nature around other dogs. We believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Jasper
description:
Jasper is an ex-racing greyhound that has spent all of his life in kennels. Jasper is now ready for a comfortable and cosy forever home to call his own. Jasper is a friendly and loveable boy who likes attention and a cuddle. Jasper has a high prey drive still so does pull when he sees ducks, birds and wildlife when out on walks. Jasper has never lived in a home before so he will need time to settle and get used to unfamiliar sounds and objects.

Jasper has interacted well with dogs and is currently paired with another greyhound so we believe that he can be rehomed with another dog of a similar size – Subject to a successful meet.

Jasper is a sweet boy so can potentially be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Dakota
description:
Dakota is looking for her forever home, and she has so much love to give.  She’s an incredibly sweet, friendly girl who absolutely adores people.  If you’re happy to give her plenty of fuss, she’ll be in her element!  Despite her size, she is a gentle soul with a lovely nature and enjoys spending time with her favourite humans.  She already knows some basic commands and is very eager to please so would benefit from further training.  Being a young, strong dog, she can be powerful on the lead, so her new adopter will need to be confident and committed to continue her lead training.  Because of this, she will be best suited to an active home where she can enjoy plenty of exercise, adventures and mental stimulation.  If you are looking for a loyal, affectionate companion with a heart as big as she is, this lovely girl could be the one for you.  She will need a private secure garden.

She has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, and is very playful and can be too much for other dogs as she does get in their face so for this reason we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can continue to learn manners and boundaries around other dogs will the full support of her new adopter with lots of positive reinforcement.

As Dakota came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Jax
description:
This stunning boy is Jax! we are looking for an experienced home for this fantastic lad.  He is a friendly and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and enjoys a good fuss.  He has a wonderful nature and is always happy to spend time with his people. This clever lad is exceptionally well behaved at the vets, taking examinations and handling in his stride, which is a testament to his temperament and trainability.  Like many dogs, he has his own little quirks – one of his favourites is enthusiastically ragging his blankets and rearranging them to his liking!  As a typical Belgian Malinois, he is highly intelligent, energetic and thrives on both physical exercise and mental stimulation.  He loves charging around our compound and would be happiest in a home where he has plenty of opportunities to stay active and engaged.  Because of his breed traits, he will need an owner who has previous experience with Belgian Malinois and understands their needs.  He is not a dog that will be content with a short walk around the block, he requires ongoing training, enrichment and a lifestyle that allows him to use both his body and brain.  He will need a private secure garden.

Jax was rehomed but sadly has been returned to us as his prey drive was too much for his new owners. He cannot be rehomed with cats or small furries.  He will need an owner that has previous experience with large breed high prey dogs.

He has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could possibly be rehomed with another dog (similar size) following a successful meet and greet.

As Jax came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Daisy
description:
Daisy was previously a racing greyhound who has been brought up in kennels. She is a smaller girl in comparison to a typical greyhound but still does have quite a high prey drive. She makes up for her size with her big personality, she is a very sweet and loving girl but can be a little cheeky at times. As like most greyhounds, Daisy enjoys a good walk and sniff in the woods, with the occasional time off lead in an enclosed area to burn off energy but will equally spend lots time relaxing on a comfy cosy bed. Daisy is after someone that is looking to give a dog lots of love and companionship, which she hasn’t previously had in her life. She in return will give you unconditional love.

Daisy can be a little nippy at times so we feel that it would be best for her to be rehomed with children who are 14 years or older – subject to a successful meet.

Daisy is currently paired and used to living with another greyhound in kennels. She has also interacted well with other dogs whilst on walks so we believe that she could be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and temperament – again subject to a successful meet.

Due to Daisy being an ex-racer it wouldn’t be suitable for him to be rehomed with cats or small furries.

name: Ivan
description:
This handsome lad is Ivan!  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a big personality and an even bigger heart.  Full of energy and enthusiasm, he’s always ready for fun and loves nothing more than chasing after tennis balls.  He’s a very excitable and giddy dog who doesn’t always realise his own size, so he can jump up when greeting people or when he’s excited.  He is also quite vocal at times, especially when he wants your attention.   He knows his basic commands and is eager to interact with people, but he will need continued training and guidance, particularly when out walking as he is very strong on the lead.  Due to his size and strength, he would benefit from an experienced and active owner who can continue his training and provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation.  Ivan would benefit from a private secure garden where he can safely have off lead time to play fetch with his tennis balls.

Ivan has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he potentially could be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet.

As Ivan came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Buddy
description:
This loveable boy is Buddy! He is the perfect mix of playful energy and affectionate companionship. He’s a friendly, easy-going lad who absolutely adores people and loves being the centre of attention.  Full of character, he’s excitable, giddy and always ready to make you smile.  Whether it’s cuddles on the sofa or a game in the garden, he just wants to be involved in everything you do.  He is bursting with energy and would thrive in an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, playtime and mental stimulation.  Fetch is one of his favourite games, and he will happily keep you entertained for hours chasing after a ball.  Buddy is incredibly affectionate and loves a fuss, he will make a loyal, loving companion.  One thing to note : He is quite the escape artist, so he will need a private secure garden and owners who are mindful of doors, gates and fencing.  When Buddy came into us he had an Entropian (an eye condition) which has now been repaired and he is healing nicely.

Buddy has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care so we feel he could potentially live with another high energy dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Buddy came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Mercy
description:
Mercy came into our care as a stray, very shut down and scared. With time and patience staff managed to win her round and she slowly came out of her shell. Little by little we are seeing her lovely personality shine through. With those she trusts, Mercy has shown to be very affectionate and sweet lady.

She is still a little unsure, especially around men. However, this is something we are currently helping her with, and her new family must be willing to continue this.

With Mercy being nervous and unsure she is looking for a very patient and understanding adult only home, where she can develop and settle in at her own pace. Her new family must have the time to be able to come and meet her multiple times so she can get to know you before she goes home.

Mercy is currently also having socialisation training around dogs to build up her confidence. She is still unsure of other dogs so needs to be the only dog in the home.

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, she came in as a stray so we don’t know much about her history. It has taken a lot of time and patience for Cali to show us her excitable, bubbly personality. Due to this we are after an experienced home that has the time to get to know Cali here before she goes home. Once Cali gets to know you she loves a fuss and attention.  She loves going out for woodland walks and gets very giddy for her lead, she pulls a little on the lead, due to her size, so would benefit from some on going training. Cali enjoys an offlead run in the enclosed compound where she can chase after a tennis ball.

Cali will need to live in an Adult only home with an enclosed garden where she has space to roam about at her leisure.  She used to be a little nervous and unsure around certain dogs, we have been working with her on this and introducing her to dogs which is helping her social interactions. She is now a friendly girl with most of the dogs on site and can say a lovely face to face hello and even tries to play with others. She will need continued training to help with her socialisation. We still feel that Cali will need to be the only dog in the house.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Arlo
description:
Arlo is a very giddy boy who will always bring you a toy when you greet him and just wants to play! He is super friendly and loves everyone that he meets! He is always wagging his tail and wiggling his body when you go to say hello! He loves to explore the woodland area on his walks and will sniff everything along the way. He also adores going into the secure compound area where he can be let off the lead and have as many zoomies as he wants! Arlo will need an active family that is happy to be outside with him a lot.

Arlo can be very vocal when he sees other dogs, but he is capable of interacting well with calm, friendly dogs when introductions are managed appropriately. He would benefit from continued socialisation and training to help him develop better manners and build his confidence around other dogs. Arlo can be powerful on the lead and will pull enthusiastically towards other dogs, so he is looking for a confident owner who is comfortable handling large, strong dogs and is committed to continuing his training. Due to this Arlo needs to be the only dog in the home.

Arlo needs to be in an adult only home with no regular visiting children.

Arlo would benefit from a house with a very secure large garden in a quiet area that doesn’t have much footfall going past as he gets easily overwhelmed with noises. Arlo is a sweet young dog looking for a patient and loving home where he can continue to learn and thrive. With consistent training, guidance, and plenty of opportunities to channel his natural instincts in positive, appropriate ways, he’s sure to grow into a wonderful companion.

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Mabel
description:
Mabel came in to our care as an ex racer, meaning she does have quite a high prey drive when out on her walks! She does walk beautifully until she sees a squirrel and then she’s off! She is a very chilled out girl in her kennel and does love to give you a scare when she’s under a blanket hiding!

This lovely girl is looking for a home where she can relax and enjoy her retirement years curled up in a bed or sprawled out on a couch! We do feel she could live in a home with another dog as she has interacted well with other dogs whilst being in our care. This would be subject to a successful meet. However shecannotlive in home with small animals such as cats, due to her high prey drive. We also feel she could potentially live in a home with a family where children are 12 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Although Mabel does love being in her beds, she really does enjoy being out and about on her walks with her greyhound pals! So she would appreciate a home that would give her the best of both worlds – a lovely walk followed by snuggles with her favourite people! Please apply today to give her a forever home that she deserves so much!

name: Shadow
description:
Shadow is a very cheeky boy has been super friendly to our staff and volunteers since he came in to our care. With him being an ex racer, he does have a high prey drive so can try to chase squirrels whilst out for his walks! He was paired in his kennel prior to her going home and will walk well with other greyhounds. He does seem unsure around other breeds of dogs, especially smaller breeds and will be quite vocal towards them. The staff and volunteers have been doing socialisation training with him here and he is improving slowly, his new family would need to continue this to help with improve further.

Shadow will have spent most of his life in kennels with his racing background, so he may feel a little nervous going in to a home environment. We also do not know if he is house trained or toilet trained due to this. He loves to lie in his comfy beds after his walks – we sometimes catch him upside down showing his belly off!

We think Shadow would prefer to be the only dog in the home, with him being a little unsure around other dogs at moment. However, he could potentially live with another greyhound if a meet and greet with him went well and depending on the other dogs temperament. He could also potentially live with children 12 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Shadow would love a home where he could relax and enjoy his retirement years and rest on a comfy bed (or couch) of his own!

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Todd
description:
Todd is a super friendly, but very energetic boy! He can be quite vocal towards other dogs whilst out on his walks due to wanting to play so would benefit from further training and socialisation. He enjoys treats and toys and loves a good play around with the staff in his kennel and on walks. Todd is the happiest when he is outside in our enclosed compound area off lead and running around with his toys. He would happily stay there all day! We think that Todd needs a reasonably sized fully enclosed garden that he can spend a lot of time in burning off all of his energy in between walks. Todd needs a family that is around a lot so he isn’t alone in the house for too long. His new family will need to have the time to ensure he is getting a lot of exercise every day and be able to take him to extra activities such as agility or scent work to help engage his brain and keep it stimulated.

We believe that Todd needs to be the only dog in the home so that he has all of the focus on him whilst he still needs extra training. Todd loves other dogs but can be very over the top whilst out on walks.

Additionally, we think that Todd needs to be in an adult only home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Enfys
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I would like to be the only dog in the home!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I'm making progress but need gentle encouragement.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

Enfys is a wonderful lady who has come to us from a breeder and has settled so well as she has grown to trust us. As she has settled in, her true and wonderful personality has begun to shine, and she has grown so much in confidence. As she begins to trust you, the more animated she becomes, giving us little glimpses of the happy girl she has the potential to become.

Enfys would prefer to be the only dog in the home as she enjoys her space and would prefer all of the attention on her. Her adopters would need to have experience with rescue dogs and be confident in helping her continue to build her confidence. She can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeding dogs to better understand her needs.

As Enfys has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a completely new way of living. Enfys has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she does need some encouragement and reassurance. With continued patience and positive experiences, we are sure she will become more confident and enjoy exploring the world with her new family.

Enfys is a lovely girl who is already showing us little flashes of her personality. She has so much potential, and we know that with the right experienced home, she will continue to blossom.

Enfys arrived overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home. She also has a Grade 1 patella luxation in her right hind leg, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle.

Enfys is also being treated for a skin rash and has some areas of alopecia. Our veterinary team will continue to monitor her progress and ensure she receives any care she needs..

Enfys has been given the Gift of Life by Ruth Butterworth

I’ve now been looking Enfys for two weeks, and what difference those two weeks have made.

When Enfys first came onto my section, she was a very nervous girl! It was very clear that she has never really been show love, and didn’t know how to take us humans. Fast forward two weeks and Enfys is a completely different dog!

Enfys is now walking beautifully on a harness, sometimes she will freeze but with encouragement she gets up and starts toddling along.

Enfys has also grown in so much confidence I now think she would be able to be an only dog in the home as long as her adopters were experienced enough.

Enfys really is a beautiful girl, and I really hope she isn’t waiting too long for her people!

Enfys is a wonderful lady who has come to us from a breeder and has settled so well the more she begins to trust us. As she has settled in, her true and wonderful personality has began to shine and she has grown so much in confidence. As she begins to trust you, the more she becomes animated, giving us little glimpses of the happy girl she has the potential to become.

Enfys gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she can live with a kind resident dog in her new home, or she can live as an only dog in a home that has rescue experience and can help continue to build her confidence. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

As Enfys has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a completely new way of living. Enfys walks well on a lead and would love to continue this in her new home, so that she can go on plenty of adventures. Enfys is a lovely girl who is already showing us little flashes of her personality.

Enfys has arrived overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home. She also has a Grade 1 patella luxation in her right hind leg, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle.

Enfys is also being treated for a skin rash and has some areas of alopecia. Our veterinary team will continue to monitor her progress and ensure she receives any care she needs.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Rosie
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can live with others dogs or be an only dog.

I'd like a secure garden to excercise and play safely in.

I'm a little unsettled at the moment, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home!

31-07-26 Rosie is the sweetest lady who has arrived all the way from Romania in search of her forever home. Despite her long journey, she is already trying so hard to be brave.

She will happily approach us with a wiggly bum, and if we spend a little time sitting quietly with her, she soon starts to relax. Before long, she'll lie down beside us and happily accept some gentle bum scratches. Rosie is still quite worried by sudden movements and loud noises, which is completely understandable given how much change she has been through.

Rosie is currently kennelled with other dogs and really enjoys their company. She gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends but is so people oriented that she could be an only dog in the right home with experienced adopters, or live with kind resident dogs who don't mind sharing their space, with this happy-go-lucky lady! She does prefer calmer dogs, so if she were to be homed with a resident dog, she would like for them to be on the calmer and understanding side. Rosie's adopters will need to have experience with rescue dogs and understanding that it may take time for them to decompress and settle in.

Rosie has recently been introduced to lead walking and is taking her learning at a slow pace, but with continued training and gentle encouragements she should pick this up. As Rosie has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and allow her to adjust at her own pace. Rosie can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who understand that she will need time to settle in. She cannot live with cats or small furries.

Rosie is a gentle, affectionate girl with a lovely nature. She is already showing us that she wants to trust people, and with a calm home, a confident canine friend, and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the comforts of family life.

Rosie has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

07-07-26 Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

name: Nanook
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and will enjoy going on adventures with my new family!

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

02-08-26 Please meet the very handsome Nanook, a truly special older gentleman who has come into our care through no fault of his own. We were contacted by a veterinary practice after his owners sadly no longer wanted him and asked to have him put to sleep. Thankfully, the kind vets knew Nanook deserved another chance and reached out to us, and we're so grateful they did. We are told that he is a Staffordshire Bull Terrier x Alaskan Malamute.

Nanook is the sweetest, most loving boy who wears his heart on his sleeve. He absolutely adores people and wants nothing more than to be by your side, soaking up all the fuss and affection you can give him. He has so much love to offer and gives his whole heart to everyone he meets and will even shower you with kisses. He's simply a joy to be around.

Understandably, Nanook is finding kennel life quite stressful. After living in a home, the busy kennel environment is a big adjustment for him, and we would love nothing more than to see him settled into a loving forever home as soon as possible. As Nanook has previously lived in a home, he should be house trained, although we can never guarantee this in a new environment. He walks nicely on a lead and will enjoy exploring on walks with his new family before heading home for plenty of cuddles. He can pull slightly on the lead when passing dogs who bark at him and can sometimes be reactive in return, so his adopters will need to work on this with him.

Nanook could happily be homed as an only dog, where he can enjoy all the love and attention to himself, but he could also be homed with another calm and gentle resident dog. His ideal home would be with someone who is around for most of the day, as he truly loves human company and will make a wonderfully loyal companion. We would consider homing him with teenagers ages 16+, as although he has been the perfect gentleman with everyone he has met here, we have no prior history and he has never met children.

If you're looking for a gentle, affectionate best friend who will repay your kindness with endless love and devotion, then Nanook could be the perfect addition to your family.

Nanook does have some arthritis in his hind end and is currently on a joint supplement to help this but he would also benefit from building up some muscle.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Milly
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teenagers, age 16+ who allow me time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

18-08-26 Milly is a shy and worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed by all the changes in her life and is in need of plenty of TLC, patience and understanding while she learns that she is safe. Although she is initially nervous, once she gets to know you she loves to have a gentle fuss.

Milly will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to settle in at her own pace. She will also need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her learn about all the good things that life in a home can offer. We would consider homing her with older, dog-savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

Milly has never lived in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life, including new skills like house training and walking on a lead. These things will be completely new to her, so she will need lots of gentle encouragement and reassurance.

Milly has arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, as well as an old break in her tail. She also arrived with a micro eye on the left side, which was quite sore and had to be removed by our vets to help her feel more comfortable. She also had an entropion repaired in her right eye. Milly is recovering well and we hope she will be feeling better very soon.

Milly is a gentle little soul who has had a difficult start in life, but we hope that with the right home, a kind canine friend and lots of love and patience, she will slowly begin to relax and discover just how wonderful being someone's beloved companion can be.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Lily May
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a male resident dog in my new home and I am fine with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am being treated for a ear infection.

Lily May has come to us from a breeder and is now hoping to find her own special forever home. When she first arrived, she was a very worried little girl who was feeling quite overwhelmed by her new surroundings. Its clear she hasn’t had much socialisation before, so she will need lots of love and TLC as she settles into her new life.

Lily May did move briefly to a foster home, where she began to find her paws and settle into home life. Unfortunately she didn't get on with one of the female resident dogs in her foster home so she has had to come back to the rescue where she has settled back in well. She has since shown that she can be picky with which female dogs she likes to share her space with and so for this reason she will now be looking for a home with a male resident dog as she much prefers the company of male dogs. She was in foster with a cat and so could possibly be homed with a dog savvy cat.

Lily May will be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will help her settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

She is still very timid, but is taking everything gently in her stride. She can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area when she is settled in.

She meets other dogs well on walks and is even getting comfortable greeting their owners as well, showing just how brave she is!

As she has had limited experience in a home, Lily May will need patient and understanding adopters to gently introduce her to everyday routines. She will need support with learning about house training, however, she was already starting to do really well with this in her foster home.

She remains sensitive to everyday noises and movements, but is beginning to cope better with gentle reassurance and support. Lily May does tolerate being handled, and this will continue to improve as her trust develops.

Lily May is a sweet little girl who simply needs patience, love and reassurance. With the right family by her side, she will continue to grow in confidence and become a devoted and loving companion.

She has been treated for an ear infection, and has followed up with the vets that have said it has cleared up now.

Lily May is growing in confidence every day. She will happily come over to say hello and really enjoys a gentle fuss and being handled. She's doing well with her harness training and is making great progress on her walks.

Lily May loves spending time with her kennel mummies, and one of the sweetest parts of her day is greeting them with a happy, wagging tail whenever they come into her kennel. It's been wonderful to watch her confidence blossom, and she's becoming more affectionate every day.

I have seen Lily May make wonderful progress during her time with us. She is an incredibly sweet-natured dog who has formed a lovely bond with her kennel companion, Coan, and clearly enjoys his company.

Lily can be dominant around other dogs at times and would be best suited to a home with a compatible male dog. She walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, making her a pleasure to take out and about. She also loves attention, affection, and treats, which makes building a bond with her very rewarding.

Overall, Lily May is an absolute superstar. She is a lovely dog with so much to offer and can be handled when needed, continuing to show what a wonderful companion she will make in the right home.

Lily May has arrived in her foster home and is beginning to find her paws as she settles into her new surroundings. She is currently a very timid little girl, but is taking things gently in her stride. She has already accepted a harness well, and we will now slowly begin introducing lead walking at her own pace, which we hope will help build her confidence and support her ongoing progress with sensitivity.

Lily May would be best suited to a calm and quiet household where she can continue to build her confidence without pressure. She will need to live with another kind and confident, male dog, who will help reassure her and show her the way as she adjusts to home life.

She is still sensitive to everyday noises and movements, but is learning to cope with gentle support and reassurance. Lily May does tolerate being handled, and this will continue to improve as her trust grows.

She is also currently living happily with a cat in her foster home.

Lily May has come to us from a breeder and is now hoping to find her own special forever home. Lily May is a very worried girl who is feeling rather overwhelmed at the moment. She clearly hasn't had much socialisation before and so will need lots of love and TLC as she settles in to her new life.

Lily May will be looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing, but this dog would need to be male as she doesn't want to share her space with a female dog.

As she has never lived in a home before, Lily May will need kind and understanding adopters who can gently introduce her to everyday life. She will need support with learning all about house training and will need to practice walking on a lead in the safety of the garden before she is ready to explore further afield.

Lily May is a sweet little girl who simply needs patience, love and reassurance. With the right family by her side, she will grow in confidence and become a devoted and loving companion.

She is currently being treated for a ear infection.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Tinkerbell
description:
I need an adult-only home with ex-breeder experience that can show me love.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe but I haven’t met cats yet so I'm not sure

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and has never lived in a home before, so she is understandably unsure and very sensitive to touch. She can go into panic mode if handled too quickly and may try to nip out of fear, as she is simply terrified and trying to protect herself. The initial handling is what scares her most, so patience and slow, gentle introductions are essential.

Recently, Tinkerbell has made wonderful progress and is beginning to show us just how much potential she has. While she is still worried by touch and may move away if approached, she is becoming much more comfortable around the people she knows. She will now approach her kennel mummy to sniff fingers, gently take treats, offer little kisses, and happily relax nearby. Recently, she has even started jumping up onto the bench beside her favourite carer at lunchtime, eagerly hoping for a tasty treat. It has become their own little routine and is a lovely sign of the trust she is beginning to build.

Tinkerbell has also made fantastic progress with handling. Although being picked up can still worry her initially, once she feels secure she settles well. One particularly special moment came when she chose to stay sitting on her kennel mummy's lap for several minutes while being gently stroked, despite not being held in place. For a dog who once found human touch so frightening, this was a huge milestone and shows just how far she has come.

She has also continued her harness training and is now happy wearing a harness with a lead trailing behind her, which many worried dogs find frightening. She is still nervous when gentle lead pressure is introduced, so this will need to continue at her own pace with patient, positive training. With dogs as frightened as Tinkerbell, building confidence is far more important than rushing the end result.

Tinkerbell will need a very experienced, adult-only home with people who understand extremely worried ex-breeding dogs. She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to guide her and help her feel safe. Her adopters will need to appreciate that she may never be a dog who constantly seeks cuddles, but with time, patience and kindness, she can form an incredibly special bond.

As she has never experienced home life, Tinkerbell will need support with house training and all the usual household routines. Calm garden time and gentle introductions to the world will help her confidence continue to grow.

Tinkerbell will also need regular grooming to keep her coat comfortable. She initially found grooming very stressful, but she is making lovely progress through gentle, positive handling and regular visits to our grooming room. Her adopters should be prepared to continue this patiently and work with an experienced, understanding groomer.

Tinkerbell is a truly special little girl who has already overcome so much. The progress she has made since arriving with us is incredible, and we truly believe she is ready for someone to take a chance on her. In the right home, with patience, understanding and love, she has every opportunity to continue blossoming into a wonderful companion.

In the past month I’ve seen more progress in Tinkerbell than ever, and it makes me sooooo happy and proud!!! A little while ago, out of nowhere, she jumped up onto the bench next to me and then quickly jumped back down. It was as if she was thinking “oh gosh, what did I just do!?” … but then she kept doing it again, and again. And now it’s like a little ritual that we have! I eat my lunch with her kennel in the yard nearly every day and because she’s so foodie, she jumps up next to me and waits to see what I have to share. It may or may not be the favourite part of my days!

Another big step for Tinkerbell is that we’ve moved forward with her harness training. I’ve started attaching a lead to it when she’s in the play yard so it trails behind her. A lot of scared dogs get freaked out by this, but it doesn’t seem to bother Tinks at all. I have attempted to pick the lead up twice to essentially ‘walk’ her, and she did panic at the tension, so I’m going to have to ease into it slowly. With dogs as frightened as Tinks, harness training is a huge step, so in my opinion it doesn’t matter how long it takes to get there. What matters is how we get there … slowly, gently, kindly.The last “win” in the past month came a couple of weeks ago. I picked her up in the back of the kennel to put her harness on (which she is not a fan of), and I put her down on my lap to make it easier for me to clip it up. For the first time ever, she just stayed put. She stayed sitting on my lap for about 2 or 3 minutes while I gently stroked her, not holding her in any way - she chose to stay. This made me SO happy and it was such a lovely moment to share with her.Tinks may still be against human touch, but the progress she’s made since her arrival is quite incredible. She really needs someone to take a chance on her now. She deserves it so much.

This week at the rescue we’ve had a big heatwave which resulted in a lot of our dogs needing to be shaved, including my beautiful Tinkerbell as she started to struggle having quite a thick coat. She has the most beautiful fur and she keeps herself so clean and dry, but it had to come off for her comfort. She was taken into the vets to be sedated again, but only because the weather has been so warm.. it would have been too hot to put her through the stress of shaving her all off with no sedation. I have been taking her into the grooming room regularly to brush her and trim the hair around her eyes, and she does definitely get better and better each time, so this is a good sign!! The next time she’s due a shave, I will try again without taking her into the vets to see how she does.

Even though Tinks is still a nervous girl, especially around people she doesn’t know, she is still progressing slowly and steadily. She’s still very reliant on other dogs and tends to copy them a lot of the time, so this has been good for her learning to trust me. She’s watched so many other dogs come up to me for a fuss, take treats from me, and just be comfortable in general being around me, and she is following suit.. just at her own pace. And that’s okay!

She is SUCH a sweet girl who has clearly been through a lot, and it’s not her fault she has such a strong guard up. I absolutely adore working with her and I understand and accept her for who she is. Seeing her get excited over toys and treats, and greeting me with a waggy tail in the mornings really makes me smile, and it gives me hope for her future. She deserves adopters who will love and cherish her the way she always should have been, regardless of if the feelings are mutual.. but I do think she is capable of loving and trusting.. she just needs to find herself with the right people.

Over the last few weeks, our lovely Tinks has reached a huge milestone. After seeing how well she has been progressing with her handling, we felt it was time to take the next step — harness training.

For a dog who finds handling so worrying, we knew there was a strong chance she might not accept wearing a harness. But unless we try, we’ll never know.

Tinks’ other kennel mummy and I took her into the grooming room, where we carefully introduced and fitted her harness. As expected, she was a little unsure and understandably a bit overwhelmed, but she made us both incredibly proud with how she coped. The next step was returning her to her kennel to see how she would manage wearing it throughout the day. Many of our more worried dogs will freeze or refuse to move in this situation, but not our Tinks. She carried on with her day as normal, moving around comfortably with the harness on.

To some, this might not seem like a huge achievement, but for Tinkerbell, it is a massive step in the right direction. Over the coming weeks, we will continue to build on this by practicing daily, with the hope that we can eventually begin introducing a lead in the yard.

With a dog like Tinkerbell, progress takes time, patience, and understanding. Thankfully, she has all of that in abundance, and we will never give up on her.

Tinkerbell has settled into my routine at the rescue beautifully now, so I’m finally starting to see glimpses of the real her. Her guard is definitely still up, but it has dropped slightly and I can tell she’s a lot more comfortable being around me than she used to be. She still won’t allow me to touch her and will bolt away if I go towards her, but she’s approaching me to sniff my fingers, sometimes give me kisses, and taking treats from me every single day now. She also feels content enough to lay near me when I’m sat in the yard eating my lunch, often with her back towards me which I guess is a sign that she does trust me!

One thing she has improved massively with is being picked up. I mentioned in my last update I still had to use a thick blanket and she would still sometimes try to bite (just not as often), but that’s even better again now. This week I was able to pick her up with no blanket, which is HUGE for Tinks!!

Because of how much better she had gotten, I thought I would attempt a full groom - going into it with absolutely no expectations. She allowed me to shave her back, but that’s as far as we could get. She started to get more and more stressed and I really didn’t want to push her and ruin the work we’ve done, so I took her into the vets so she could be sedated to complete the groom. So, she’s now shaved (minus her INCREDIBLE eyelashes), and I think she looks absolutely beautiful. Now that we’ve started fresh with her coat, I’m going to start taking her into the grooming room just once a week or so, and gently brush her etc to get her more used to it all.

Tinkerbell has made slow and steady progress since she’s been on my section and I’m so proud of how brave she’s trying to be. I can tell she wants to come out of her shell a bit more and join in with the rest of the dogs, but she’s not there just quite yet. Something big did happen last week though!! During dinner time I was hand feeding one of her friends, and Tinks came over and started licking the food off my hand for the first time!!!! I was absolutely over the moon and so happy that she felt comfortable enough to do that. Since then she’s done it nearly every day and has also started to take treats from me too if they’re yummy enough. I know this probably won’t sound like a lot to most people, but for a dog like Tinberbell it’s huge. For me, taking food from my hand is usually the first step in earning trust with my scared dogs, so I think we’re heading in the right direction.

We have also made a small amount of progress with Tinkerbell’s fear of being picked up. She still doesn’t like it - at all - but she’s not panicking as much any more and definitely doesn’t try to bite me as much as she did before. I still have to use a thick blanket and be very slow and calm with her, but I think she is starting to slowly realise that I’m not going to hurt her. I trimmed her fringe again a few days ago as her hair seems to grow quite quickly, so I took this opportunity to stroke her head gently for a little while once I was done. She actually started to close her eyes after a minute or so and I think she may have been enjoying it, or at least I hope she was.I adore this little lady and I’m going to do everything I can to show her what love and kindness is. I just hope a special someone will come along and feel the same way about her soon.

Tinkerbell has recently been moved to my section, as she struggles a great deal with being touched and handled by us humans. At present, she goes into complete panic mode whenever I go to pick her up, and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all; she’s literally just so scared she will do anything she can to stop it happening. Once I have her comfortably in my arms, she will actually settle really well and will allow me to do things such as give her a gentle fuss and trim the hair on her face. I think the initial picking up is what scares her the most so this is what we’ll work on slowly together.

Tinkerbell is going to need a very experienced home with people who have had terrified dogs before. She’s going to need a lot of work and TLC put into her, and also a lot of understanding. Her adopters will need to accept the fact that she may never be a normal dog, and she may never be a dog who wants fusses or cuddles, but love her anyway. She’s a very special girl, and she needs a home equally as special to help her and give her what she needs.

I’m going to work as closely as I can with her over the next couple of weeks, and hopefully I can earn her trust and prove to her that she doesn’t need to be afraid of me. I’ll keep you all updated!

Tinkerbell has come to us from a breeder and can be a little unsure at first. She is touch-sensitive and may need time to feel comfortable, but once she calms down, she begins to show her gentle, sweet side. Tinkerbell will need an adult-only home that can handle her sassy personality and provide the patience she needs to settle in at her own pace.

She will also need a kind and confident resident dog to guide her and take her under their wing as she adjusts. Tinkerbell is looking for someone to teach her about trust, companionship, and the joys of home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be gentle and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Starting with a few gentle garden sniffs will be perfect for her confidence as she begins to explore her new world.

Tinkerbell is a little gem who, with time and love, will grow into a devoted and affectionate companion.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Cloe
description:
I need an adult only home that understands ex-breeders.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I am learning to walk on a harness but may need more time as I heal.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 7 teeth extracted and an inguinal hernia repaired. Read below for more!

Cloe is a very worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still learning that people can be kind. It is clear she has had very little positive experience with humans in the past, and as a result she finds trust incredibly difficult. She can be flighty when worried and may choose to protect herself if she feels pressured or uncomfortable.

Cloe is a sweet but complex girl who has already shown us that, once she truly trusts someone, she has a wonderfully affectionate side. Although progress has been slow, it has also been incredibly rewarding. She now greets her favourite carers every morning with an excited waggy tail and is trying her absolute hardest to be brave around the people she trusts.

She has made lovely progress with handling and has recently enjoyed a full groom. Cloe was an absolute angel throughout, allowing herself to be groomed beautifully. She has also recently been bathed and gently dried, taking it all in her stride. These may seem like small achievements, but for a little dog who once found human contact so frightening, they are huge milestones.

We have also discovered that being picked up is only scary for Cloe at first. Once she is safely in someone's arms, she relaxes completely and allows herself to be handled without fuss. We truly believe that, with continued patience and positive experiences, this fear will continue to fade and she will become even more confident.

Cloe has also recently started her harness training. Although she is still a little too timid to venture out on walks just yet, she is making a fantastic start and we are confident that, with a little more time and encouragement, she will soon be ready to begin exploring the world beyond the rescue.

Cloe will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children and adopters who have experience of very worried ex-breeding dogs. Her new family will need to understand that building a relationship with her will take time and that the best way to win her trust is to allow her to approach on her own terms, without rushing or placing expectations on her.

She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home. Having a canine friend gives her comfort and reassurance and will help guide her as she learns about life beyond the rescue. We have also discovered that Cloe is not comfortable around cats and can become quite fixated by them, so she will need a cat-free home.

As she has never lived in a home before, Cloe's adopters will need to be patient as she learns about house training and everyday routines. Progress with Cloe may never be fast, but she proves time and time again that she is willing to try for the people she trusts.

We are incredibly hopeful for Cloe's future. She has already come so much further than we ever imagined possible in the rescue environment, and we truly believe she will flourish in a patient, understanding home. She simply needs someone willing to take a chance on her, give her all the time she needs, and let her discover that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

Cloe has had seven teeth extracted at the time of her spay, as well as an inguinal hernia repaired. She also had a lump removed from her right upper eyelid.

Cloe has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

So Cloe has been with me for about 3 months now and I can happily say I’m finally starting to see the light as the end of the tunnel with her. I think she finally has trust in me and knows that I’m not going to hurt her, and she’s trying her absolute hardest to be brave around me. She still gets really excited to see me every morning and it always instantly brightens my days.

She’s had a busy few weeks since my last update and I really couldn’t be prouder of her. To start with, she had a full groom with our incredible resident groomer who is perfect with our scared dogs, and she was an ANGEL through the whole thing. We were both so proud of her and now she looks absolutely beautiful. I of course had to pick her up to take her into the grooming room and I was a little worried she’d hold a grudge against me, but she didn’t. She was happy when I went to get her and still had a waggy tail at me when I put her back down in her kennel. We decided not to bath her that same day as it would have been too much for her, so I bathed and dried her myself yesterday. Again, she was amazing. She was so good in the bath and let me give her a good shampoo all over. She was more scared of the dryer so I was as gentle as I could have been, and I didn’t dry her completely as I didn’t want to push it. Again, no grudges were held!!!

What I’ve come to learn about Cloe is that she’s only worried and panicky with being picked up initially. As soon as I’ve got her comfortably in my arms, she no longer stresses or fusses and lets me handle her with no issues. I really believe she’ll get over her fear of being picked up in time, and when she does, I think she’ll drop all her guards.

I am truly, truly hopeful for Cloe’s future and I really do think someone just needs to take a chance on her. Even though progress here at the rescue has been slow, it’s still progress, and that is difficult to achieve for dogs like Cloe in such a busy environment. She needs a home, so PLEASE don’t keep her waiting too much longer!!

Progress with Cloe is still very slow, but it is there and it is happening, so that’s all that matters. Since my last update she has opened herself up to me ever so slightly, and now gets very excited to see me everything morning and will run up to me and sniff my fingers with a waggy tail. I know that may not sound like a lot to most, but for a dog like Cloe it’s a big step forward.

I mentioned in my last update that I had to take her into the vets a few times and it made her more frightened of me, so since then I’ve completely left her be as I felt as though we needed to reset. I’ve spent a lot of time with her, just sitting down and being present, but no touching (until today). She wasn’t happy about me picking her up and was trying to bite the blanket I was holding, but she put up way less of a fight than she did a few weeks ago … so I’m taking that as a win!! I took her outside of her kennel just to try and take some nice photos of her and she coped really well. When we were finished and I put her back in her kennel, I got down on the floor and wiggled my fingers at her to see if she was still my friend, and thankfully she did come over with a waggy tail, so that made me happy.

Over the next few weeks I’m going to continue some gentle handling like today, every so often so that she gets more used to it, but it also won’t overwhelm her. I’ll listen to her and what she’s telling me .. stop if it’s too much, and do a little more if she’s ready.I really love Cloe and I’m understanding her more and more each day, and I think she feels the same way about me. I’m starting to feel hopeful!!

Cloe is a sweet but complex little girl who has clearly been through a great deal in her life. She has major trust issues with humans and so far only trusts one person out of all the staff that work here. At the rescue we see 2 sides of her. One side is a happy, excitable girl who enjoys a little fuss and is fine to be picked up (by her favourite person), and the other side is a scared girl who would rather be left alone (by everyone else). Her favourite person here is the first person that worked with her when she first arrived, so I think she sees him as her ‘rescuer’ which is very sweet. She definitely trusts him and it’s quite shocking to see the difference in her when she’s around him - in a good way! With everyone else, she’s still very standoffish and doesn’t tolerate being touched or handled at all. She will nip to protect herself, but this doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog at all .. she’s simply just that scared.I’ve been working with Cloe for about a month now and even though she’s a lot more comfortable around me now than she used to be, she definitely still doesn’t trust me. I think it’s because I had to take her into the vets a couple of times when she first came over to my section, and it’s definitely stunted our relationship. Normally with dogs like Cloe, I won’t handle them for a good while until I establish some form of bond with them, but I couldn’t do this with Cloe as she had to see the vet. Since then, I’ve been leaving her to her own devises and trying to win her over from afar. Although she still hardly approaches me, she’s more relaxed in my presence now .. so at least we are making progress.I think in Cloe’s case, the best way to work with her is to just leave her come to you first. If she can work out by herself that you’re kind and not a threat, you’re heading in the right direction!! And then when she trusts you, she’ll drop her guard with you and become a little sweetheart like she is with her favourite staff member here. In a home where she has all the time in the world to bond with her new parents, I think she will absolutely blossom!!! But it may take a little while to get there, so her future adopters will need to be very understanding and patient with her. It will be SO worth it though, I promise!

Cloe is a very worried little lady who has come to us from a breeding environment and is not yet comfortable with being handled. It’s clear she has had very little experience of kindness, so she can be quite flighty and may panic if approached too quickly and can choose to make the wrong decision if pushed out of her comfort zone.

Cloe settles quickly once she feels safe and has already begun making lovely progress. With her favourite member of staff she is already showing her funny and affectionate side and is happy to approach him, kiss his fingers and will even do a little excited dance. With patient, understanding adopters who can appreciate why she may feel scared or defensive and support her as she builds trust, we believe she will settle in and start to come out of her shell.

She will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children and with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her the patience, kindness, and time she needs to truly thrive.

Cloe is already starting to approach you slowly on her own terms and so will need plenty of time, gentle encouragement, and extra TLC to continue building her confidence. She absolutely loves the company of other dogs and will need a kind, calm, and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she adjusts to home life.

As she has never lived in a home before, Cloe's adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice around the home and garden once she is more comfortable with being handled.

Cloe has had 7 teeth extracted at the time of her spay as well as an inguinal hernia repaired. She had a lump on her right upper eye lid that has been removed.
