name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who was understandably overwhelmed when she first arrived and desperately needed kindness, patience and TLC as she began to settle and learn that the world could be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialled on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a typical dog.

Since moving to a new section of the rescue, Nora has made huge leaps in her confidence. She is now harness trained and happily wears her harness throughout the day. She has become much more comfortable with handling and confidently walks on her harness to and from the exercise yard. Although she is not yet ready to venture out on walks beyond the rescue, she is making steady progress and becoming braver every day. Another wonderful milestone is that she now chooses to sit at the front of her kennel, curiously watching people and dogs come and go, rather than hiding away at the back as she once did.

Since arriving with us, Nora has slowly begun to show glimpses of the gentle and affectionate dog she has the potential to become. Like many nervous dogs, she can be vocal when she feels unsure, and her deep, defensive howl is very much in keeping with her Beagle heritage. However, with patience and a calm approach, she soon settles and begins to reveal her softer side.

Although Nora is still learning to feel comfortable around people, she is making wonderful progress. She is beginning to choose to settle near her carers and, once she has had time to relax, becomes much more accepting of gentle interaction. In these quieter moments she happily allows us to stroke and handle her, which is a huge achievement for a dog who once found every interaction so overwhelming.

It is clear that Nora's worries stem not from a dislike of people, but from uncertainty. Having had such limited life experiences, she simply does not yet understand who we are or what to expect from us. As her confidence grows, she becomes increasingly willing to be approached and reassured, and each small step forward is a testament to her resilience.

Nora would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. She will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. We believe that what Nora needs most now is the stability, security and reassurance that only a loving home can provide.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence. While Nora has successfully shared her kennel with smaller dogs, we feel she would be happiest living alongside a dog of a similar size or larger.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She is now comfortable wearing a harness and walking around the rescue grounds, but she is not yet ready to explore the outside world. Her adopters will need to continue building her confidence gradually, beginning with familiar surroundings before introducing new places at a pace she is comfortable with.

Although Nora is still a sensitive and sometimes worried little girl, the progress she has made has been nothing short of remarkable. Beneath her fears is a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a dog like Nora slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences imaginable, and with love, patience and understanding, we know she will continue to blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every step of that journey worthwhile.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Candy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can live with larger, playful resident dogs, or I can be the only dog in the home!

I would like a large, and secure garden that I can settle into.

I walk well on a lead, but I can be strong so my adopters will need to work with this

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home! Read below for more!

13-08-26 Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy can walk on a lead, although she can be quite strong, so her adopters will need to be prepared to continue her training and help her develop her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. As she is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with her breed and understand her needs.

Candy has the confidence to be the only dog in the home, although she could potentially live with another large breed dog following a successful meet and greet. She loves to play and can be quite excitable, so she would not be suitable to live with smaller or more fragile dogs and she will need a home without cats.

Candy is an incredible girl, but she can be sensitive when she is worried or when she feels uncomfortable, for this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

She has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay.

name: Toby
description:
I’d like an active home filled with love and kindness!

I could be an only dog or live with others! I've haven't met cats yet.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy an active lifestyle!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

15-08-26 Toby is a really handsome boy who originally came to us from a home where his owners landlord would not allow him to stay. He was then adopted into a loving home where he spent five happy years, but sadly his owner has since passed away and Toby has found himself back with us.

He is the sweetest boy. He is a little shell-shocked to find himself here but he is taking everything in his stride. He is still quite a shy boy, but once he knows you he will approach you to ask for cuddles and really enjoys some affection. He would benefit from adopters who have experience with rescue dogs.

We are told by his previous owner's family that Toby has good recall and is a very faithful dog who forms strong bonds with his people. He is very good with both dogs and people. Toby has previously lived happily as an only dog and would be very happy to have his new home all to himself, but he is also sharing his kennel well with another dog and could be homed with another kind, well mannered dog.

As Toby has come to us from a home, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. He is house trained and walks well on a lead, so his new family will have a nice head start. We are told that he can bark when visitors come to the home, but if you call him away for a tasty treat he will settle.

Toby is an active boy who needs plenty of exercise. He is used to having one long walk each day, usually lasting around an hour to an hour and a half, as well as another half-hour walk in the evening. Even after all of that, he can still have plenty of energy! His new home will need to be able to offer him a similar level of exercise and plenty of opportunities to get out and enjoy the world.

Toby would love a home where there are lots of walks and adventures to be had. He is a Collie cross and will need adopters who can keep his mind and body busy, but in return he has so much love and loyalty to give.

Toby could share his home with dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

More than anything, Toby just wants to be back in a home with someone to love and who will love him in return. After already losing his owner and finding himself back in kennels, we hope his next home will be his forever one. He really is a lovely boy who would be very happy to have a person of his own again.

name: Molly Moo
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I would prefer to be an only dog, but could be homed with a large, laid back dog.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have had 5 teeth extracted and a mammary lump removed.

12-08-26 Molly Moo is a sweet lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a lovely girl who is happy to be handled and enjoys a gentle fuss and we think with love and TLC she is going to adore being someones special girl.

At the moment, we feel that Molly Moo would prefer to be homed as the only dog, where she can get all the love and attention to herself. We would consider homing her with another large, laid back dog in the right circumstances. She does get along well with other dogs when socialising, but wouldn't want to share her space with them.

Molly Moo does show signs of resource guarding food when around other dogs, so should she be homed with another dog, they would need to be fed separately and she will need adopters who are happy to manage this. Due to this, any children in the home would need to be 16+.

As Molly Moo has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Molly Moo can already walk on a lead, so once she is settled, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area.

Molly Moo has arrived slightly overweight, so she will need a good diet and gentle exercise to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Molly Moo has had five teeth removed at the time of her spay. She also arrived with a mammary lump, which our vets removed during her spay. Our vets will continue to monitor her recovery and make sure she is comfortable.

Molly Moo is a lovely, easy-going girl who has lots of love to give. We hope she soon finds a family who will enjoy having her around and give her the happy home she deserves.

name: Mash
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need an extra secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

06-08-26 Mash is an extremely sensitive lady who has come to us from a breeder and is finding the world a little overwhelming. She is still wary of us humans and isn't ready to be approached or handled just yet, choosing instead to take things at her own pace. She can be extremely nervous and extra precaution will need to be taken to ensure her safety in the home.

Mash will need a calm, understanding home that can offer her plenty of love, patience and reassurance as she begins to learn about trust. She will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog that she can look to for guidance and comfort as she settles into home life. She will need an adult-only home, that has experience with ex-breeders and can understand her needs, and that she may take time to come around.

As Mash has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient while she learns about house training and all the routines that come with family life. Going for walks may feel too frightening at first, so gentle potters and sniffing around a secure garden will be the perfect way for her to build her confidence before venturing any further. She will need an extra-secure garden to keep her safe as she is nervous and can be flighty.

Mash is a truly sweet girl who is simply overwhelmed by everything that is new to her. Given the time, patience and understanding she deserves, we are sure she will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Mash has a been given the Gift of Life by Jade Mitchell

name: Yoshi
description:
I will need an understanding home, that will allow me to come out of my shell.

I need a resident dog, of the same size to help me settle in and no cats please!

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I am harness training and would like to continue this in my new home!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

18-07-26 Yoshi is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is friendly but understandably nervous and is looking for a patient, understanding family who can help her come out of her shell at her own pace.

Yoshi loves to snuggle up with her kennel friends and takes a lot of comfort from being around other dogs. Because of this, she will need a home with at least one kind, confident smaller resident dog of similar size, who can help her feel safe as she continues to build her confidence and learn to trust but she cannot live with cats.

She can be a little worried when exploring the play yard and new environments, so her adopters will need to be patient and allow her to take things at her own speed. She has never lived in a home before so will need to learn all about life in a home, including house training, so her new family should be prepared to support her through this with kindness and consistency.

Yoshi is a tiny, gentle, inquisitive little lady with so much potential. With time, patience, and the reassurance of a canine companion, we're sure she will blossom into a wonderful, loving companion.

name: Olive
description:
I'd like a calm and quiet, adult only home.

I could be the only dog or live with a male resident dog. I can't live with cats.

I would like a secure garden that I can explore.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

Olive originally came to us from Romania as a puppy with her siblings and was quickly adopted. Sadly, she was recently returned as she was finding life in a busy city and busy household too overwhelming.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace. We feel she would really benefit from adopters with experience of Romanian dogs. Since being back with us, Olive has shown us just how sociable she is with other dogs. She happily shares her kennel with a lovely male dog called Cooper, and the two get along brilliantly. She also regularly enjoys play dates with numerous other dogs and absolutely loves being part of a group! We now feel Olive could happily live with another friendly, well-matched male dog, although she can also be homed as the only dog.

Olive can be a little hit and miss around food with other dogs, but this is easily managed. She can happily be fed alongside other dogs when everyone has their own bowl, and she is also comfortable taking treats around her canine friends. Her adopters will simply need to continue giving her appropriate space and managing mealtimes sensibly. She cannot share her home with cats or small furries.

Olive can struggle with busy environments and traffic, so we feel she would be much happier in a quieter area where she can enjoy more rural walks. She can also bark at loud noises and strangers visiting the home, so this is something her adopters will need to be willing to work on with her. Her adopters will need to be patient, calm and consistent, helping her gradually build confidence and feel secure in her new environment.

Olive is house trained but may need gentle reminders as she adjusts to a new routine. She walks nicely on the lead and would love an active home where she can enjoy plenty of walks and adventures. She is a clever girl who already knows basic commands such assitandpaw. Olive is a very sweet girl who enjoys being close to her people, happily sitting beside you, although she isn't overly fond of cuddles.

When Olive first arrived back with us, she was quite nervous and wouldn't approach us, but she has grown enormously in confidence during her time here. She now eagerly greets her kennel mummy every morning and has become an absolute joy to care for. She loves going out for walks with our volunteers, which has really helped her confidence continue to blossom, and she absolutely adores chasing balls around our big play yard. She is often at the centre of our larger play groups, encouraging all of the other dogs to run around and play with her. Watching Olive run freely and enjoy herself is truly heartwarming.

After spending the last seven weeks getting to know Olive, we can honestly say she has been an absolute angel. She has settled beautifully into kennel life, but it breaks our hearts knowing she has experienced the comforts of a home and is now waiting for another family to find her. She deserves so much more than kennel life and has so much love to give.

With time, love and TLC, we know Olive will blossom into the most wonderful companion. She really will make one very lucky family complete, so please don't leave this special girl waiting any longer.

Olive has tested negative for Brucella Canis.

Olive can show a little guarding behaviours around food time when it comes to other dogs, but as long as she is fed at distance she is absolutely fine!

Olive deserves so much more than kennel life, she will really make your life’s complete!

Olive will make the most perfect companion for someone, please don’t leave her waiting much longer.

description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved to a foster home and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through. Crispin lives alongside two cats in his foster home and he is not bothered by their presence.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Toby
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog and no cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead but can be reactive to bikes.

I was born with deformed toes which have been amputated and I have a luxating patella

Toby is a handsome Cocker Spaniel who has been through a lot in his young life and is now looking for a special someone to help him write his next chapter. Originally coming to us from a breeder at just three months old, Toby was a very scared little puppy who found the world overwhelming. Although he found a loving home, he was sadly returned to our care after his adopters felt unable to manage some of his behaviours.

Toby is still a sensitive soul and will need a calm, adult-only home with no visiting children. His new family should have experience with worried or complex dogs and be confident in helping him feel safe. He will need a home without cats as he has met them at the rescue and was too interested. While Toby had previously shown some resource guarding tendencies in his home, we have not seen any guarding behaviour from him while he has been with us. He has spent time in the office with staff members and has been completely comfortable with people coming in and out, which has been lovely to see.

Toby does enjoy playing with tennis balls and can be reluctant to drop them, but this is not a guarding issue. If we offer him a tasty treat in exchange, he is more than happy to swap his ball!

Since returning to us, Toby has come out of his shell beautifully. He greets staff with a wagging tail and absolutely loves attention, affection and food – especially food! Those who work with him absolutely adore him and think he is the most special and wonderful boy.

Toby will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog. He did live with another dog previously and while they got along, he could sometimes guard his adopter's attention, so for this reason he is best suited to being homed as an only dog.

Out and about, Toby enjoys his walks and is lovely on and off the lead. He has good recall and mixes well with other dogs, although he can be reactive to bicycles, so should only be let off lead in safe, secure areas away from the public.

Toby was born with some deformed toes that were later amputated. He has always had a slightly unusual gait due to this, but our vets have noted that he also has a luxating patella, although it may improve with gentle exercise. He also has a naturally short tail, which just adds to his unique charm.

Toby is a sweet, loving boy who truly wants to connect. He has already won the hearts of everyone here, and we're all rooting for him to find a calm, understanding home where he can feel safe, build trust and thrive. If you have the time, patience and experience to offer Toby the gentle guidance he needs, he will reward you with loyalty, love and plenty of cuddles.

Tobywill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

This week, Toby’s kennel mum celebrated his 1 year anniversary by breaking him out of the rescue for a couple of hours of fun!!Toby travelled good as gold in the car, and happily climbed into the back of the car and had his seatbelt harness fitted with no issues at all.He travelled to Pupstars Paddock with his kennel mum and another staff member who was new to him. He was absolutely brilliant with that staff member who could only sing his praises!!Toby absolutely LOVED the secure field, his tail did not stop wagging, he followed his kennel mum around everywhere and was (very gently) taking treats of both staff members.Once Toby bonds with you, he is the most loyal boy in the world. His circle of trust is only getting bigger, with more and more staff members falling in love with him as time goes on. He may have a stricter criteria than most, but it just means he is just an incredibly special boy in need of a special home. He is such a darling and we wish more people would be able to see it!

Toby’s one year anniversary with us is slowly approaching, and it honestly breaks my heart every day knowing he’s still not curled up on a sofa in a home of his own.

Toby is literally such an amazing dog when he knows you, all he wants to do is spend time with you, whether that be sitting with you, or going out for a gentle stroll!

Recently, I’ve been working on Toby’s lead reactivity, and he’s been doing incredibly well. He’s making such good progress, and I’m so proud of how far he’s come!

I really hope this is the last update I have to write about toby, hopefully his next updates will be coming from his new pawrents, showing us him blossoming in a home and how truly special he really is!

I’ve had the absolute joy of working with Toby for a couple of months now, and he truly is one of my more sensitive, special boys!

Once Toby gets to know you, he turns into the happiest, most affectionate little soul you could ever meet! He absolutely loves zooming around our big play yard, or heading out for a calm, gentle stroll along the lanes taking everything in at his own pace, Toby can be reactive towards passing cars or other dogs, it is something we are currently working on with him!

With the weather getting nicer, I decided it was the perfect day for a little adventure down to the river! To get there, we walk through a huge open field, so I popped Toby on a long line to give him some extra freedom to explore.I don’t think I’ve ever seen a dog so happy he spent most of his time rolling around on his back in the grass with the biggest grin on his face!

When we reached the river, Toby was a little unsure at first. He sat at the edge, watching the water. But after a few minutes of building up his courage, he dipped his paws in and that was it, he was happily paddling back and forth, enjoying every second. It was such a special moment to watch.

I truly adore Toby with my whole heart, he’s one of those dogs who just stays with you, always on your mind.

He can still feel a bit unsure when meeting new people and might bark or back away at first, but give him a little time and patience, and he’ll become your most loyal, loving best friend.

I honestly can’t believe Toby is still waiting for his forever home. He is such a gentle, beautiful soul who deserves the absolute best life has to offer!

Toby is a sweet older gentleman who truly enjoys the quieter side of life. He loves nothing more than snuggling up for a nap and being close to his people.

Toby still has a playful spark and enjoys his daily walks as well as pottering around the yard. He would thrive in a calm, peaceful home and is best suited to a household with no children or cats, where he can relax and enjoy his golden years in comfort.

I love Toby. He is so loved by many of us here at the rescue. He's a confident boy once he knows you, but until he feels comfortable around you he can bark and sometimes be a bit standoffish.

Toby is a big cuddle bunny, he absolutely loves a fuss, and will happily accept butt scratches any time of the day.

He enjoys going out for walks but absolutely loves being off lead and running around the big play yard, when his butt wiggles with happiness and excitement it really doesn't stop, it's super adorable. He likes chasing a tennis ball but he won't bring it back, instead he rolls around with it usually in his mouth and will then lay with it and play with it, he's a comical boy.

Again, once he's comfortable with you he's very easy to handle, I can get a coat or a jumper on him with no problems, I can pick him up and I can brush him with no problems, he had a groom recently and he was no issue at all.

It's a shame he keeps getting overlooked, yes he might have some typical cocker issues such as guarding, but it hasn't been a huge issue since he's been here, I can go in and out of his kennel, pick things up etc and he's been fine. I've also been yarding him with other dogs to try and socialise him more, and although he can be selective of who he likes, once he's found a friend then he just wants to play. He is a beautiful boy inside and out, and in my opinion anyone would be lucky to have him as part of their family.

Also he is kennel clean so house training shouldn't take any time at all.

Please, don't let Toby spend another year in kennels, he truly deserves to find his forever home, as they all do. It's getting colder, it's been snowing, a nice warm, cosy house with a loving family is what he wants, I know his forever home is out there somewhere so please come and find him.

Toby is still doing incredibly well with us here and hasn’t shown any signs of guarding, while this has stopped with us here we still are unsure how he will react in a home environment.

It is an absolute pleasure working with Toby and he always brings a smile to your face throughout the day. Toby is a gentle, loving and happy boy and is desperate to have somebody he can give all his love to.

Toby has definitely come out of his shell since he's been here, he still barks when you first see him but it's a happy bark and his tail doesn't stop, before he would stay for scratches for a little bit, but now he doesn't want to leave you and wants all the attention. He is a very loving dog.

Toby originally came to us from a breeder when he was around 3 months old. He was a terrified puppy who was worried about everything and would even squeak in fear when being handled. He was quickly adopted and found a loving home, but he has sadly been returned to our care as he was displaying some behaviours that his adopters felt unable to cope with.

Toby was homed with another dog and while they got along well, he did show some signs of guarding his adopter from the other dog, for this reason we now think he would be most suited to being homed as an only dog.

Toby can also sometimes grumble if people walk past the sofa or his bed and he is on them, so he will be looking for an adult only home with no visiting children, with adopters who have experience with dogs with similar issues and will be able to work on this with him. He did nip his adopter once around 18 months ago, but that was the only time that resulted in more than a grumble.

Toby is still quite a scared boy in some aspects and certain things will make him extremely nervous, such as the hoover or sometimes even minor things like the sounds of a drawer closing, but with confident owners with experience of scared dogs we do believe he will progress further. He would be best suited to a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and follow a routine.

He enjoys going for walks and is very good both on and off lead. He has good recall and gets along well with other dogs outside of the home. He can be reactive to bikes, so his adopters would need to be mindful of this and keep him on lead in any areas where he may encounter bikes and only let him off lead in secure areas.

As he has lived in a home before, we believe he is house trained, but he may need some reminders.

Toby is a sweet boy at heart and in the right home and with the right adopters we think he will thrive. Since his arrival with us he has been on his best behaviour and already adores all of the staff that work with him and they adore him too. He absolutely loves his food and has a true zest for life which makes us smile each day, so we are so hopeful that his perfect home is out there and will find him soon.

Toby was born with some deformed toes, which have since been amputated but don't seem to bother him, though he does walk with a slightly abnormal gait. He also has a short tail.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Whispy
description:
I need a calm & quiet home, with adopters with experienced of scared ex-breeding dogs

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have not met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 2 mammary lumps removed and 2 teeth extracted.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes grumble or bark, but this has always come from a place of pure fear rather than aggression.

After spending a couple of weeks settling into her kennel routine, it is clear that Whispy has experienced very little kindness in her life. Her fears are deeply ingrained, and she has no understanding of what people's intentions are. When someone enters her kennel, she will often bark and grumble in panic because she is so frightened of what might happen next. Despite this, she allows gentle handling, strokes, and being picked up without any fuss, almost as though she has simply resigned herself to it. It is incredibly sad to see, and all she really needs is someone who will show her that people can be kind.

Whispy takes enormous comfort from other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with her two current kennel companions, who she happily shares everything with. She can be selective about the dogs she befriends and seems to prefer smaller, calm, gentle dogs rather than larger or more boisterous companions. Once she trusts another dog, they become an enormous source of reassurance, so she will need at least one kind, quiet, confident resident dog in her forever home who can help her navigate the world and show her that life doesn't have to be so frightening.

Whispy is looking for a calm, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with very scared ex-breeding dogs and who understand that trust cannot be rushed. As she has never lived in a home before, she will need help learning everything from house training to settling into a routine. Walks are not something she is ready for at the moment, and her adopters must be prepared to let her progress entirely at her own pace. Gentle garden exploration will be much more appropriate until she feels safe enough to take the next steps.

Because Whispy is an older girl and her fears are so deeply rooted, she may never completely lose all of her worries or become the confident dog people often imagine. Her adopters will need to love and accept her exactly as she is, celebrating every tiny step forward without expecting her to become a different dog. For the right family, watching Whispy slowly learn to feel safe will be incredibly rewarding.

Whispy is a very special little lady who has spent far too much of her life living in fear. She deserves a safe place to call home, where she knows nobody will ever hurt or give up on her again. With endless patience, understanding, and unconditional love, we hope she can finally experience the peaceful and happy life she has always deserved.

She has had two mammary lumps removed at the time of her spay and has also had two teeth extracted.

Whispy has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Smith

Whispy has been on my section for a couple of weeks now and oh my goodness is she a heartbreaker. I have no idea what she’s been through in her life, but her fears are deeply ingrained. She has no trust in anything or anyone, apart from a select few dogs at the rescue that she has dropped her guard with. She has absolutely no idea about human kindness, nor what our intentions are. She grumbles and barks when we enter her kennel in pure panic, as she’s so scared of what we’re going to do to her. Even though she may sound a little scary, she lets me stroke her and pick her up absolutely fine .. kind of like she’s just given up. It’s quite sad actually.Whispy currently has 2 kennel friends who she gets on well with and shares everything with. One is a Shih Tzu Cross and one is a Poodle Cross. I have tried quite a few dogs with her and it does seem as though she favours smaller dogs to larger ones. And definitely calmer, quieter ones that don’t get in her face.Whispy will need a very patient and understanding home with adopters who have experience with very scared dogs. Because she’s on the older side, she may never truly lose all of her worries and fears, and may never become a ‘normal’ dog, and this is something her adopters will need to be okay with, and love her and accept her anyway. Things such as going out for walks are not currently in the near future for Whipsy, and it’s going to take a lot of time and gentle guidance to ease her into such things.This poor, sweet girl does not deserve to live her life in fear and panic mode. She deserves to have a safe place to call her own, where she knows nobody is going to hurt her. She deserves to be loved unconditionally, and to not be given up on no matter what.

Whispy has come to us from a breeder and is a truly heartbreaking girl. When she first arrived, she was incredibly shut down, and would bury her face into the wall in the hope that nobody would notice her. She would tremble when approached and could sometimes be a little grumbly, but this was simply because she is so frightened and overwhelmed by her surroundings.

Since then, she has started to settle in and is trying so hard to be brave. She can be vocal with people and is still nervous to approach you but with patience and kind handling she has been joining in on yard times and taking treats, but she still has a ways to go. Whispy has never known the kindness of people so will retreat to a corner when she feels stressed.

Whispy will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who are willing to give her all the time, patience and understanding she needs to settle and learn to trust.

She relies on other dogs for reassurance and so she will need at least one other confident, laid back resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing and provide reassurance as she begins to build confidence. She can be selective over the dogs she enjoys spending time with however once she takes to a friend, she does so well with them and it boosts her confidence. She will need a very placid dog in the home who won’t worry when she is scared. She has had a few grumbles when meeting new dogs but she is just scared and needs time to develop a bond with them.

As she has never lived in a home before, Whispy will need kind and understanding adopters as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will be too overwhelming for her at the moment and once she is more comfortable she can begin learning in a secure garden until she feels brave enough to venture further.

Whispy is a very special lady looking for an equally special home. She has missed out on so much in her life and will need a home who will take things day by day with her and give her the support and love she’s so desperate for.
