name: Toast
description:
I would like a quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me feel safe. I live with a cat in my foster home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in (6ft+)

I'm harness training currently but need to build my confidence around lead walking.

I will need to learn about house training and lead walking

Toast is a delicate little girl who came to us from a breeder and has been slowly finding her confidence in the world. When she first arrived, she was very nervous and overwhelmed by everything around her, often running to hide in her bed.

Since arriving in foster, it has become clear that Toast is an extremely nervous girl and remains very unsure of new situations. She does not enjoy handling and can panic when she feels pressured, so she will need careful, gentle management and time to feel safe.

Toast is currently living with a cat in her foster home and can live with a dog-savvy cat who respects her space.

She will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous ex-breeding dogs and can support her without expectation or pressure. A calm, predictable environment will be essential for her ongoing confidence building.

She has come on in some areas, but handling still needs to be approached very carefully. While she has previously shown some progress with being picked up and having a harness fitted, this must always be done with patience and awareness of her limits, as she can become overwhelmed.

Toast is currently working on her harness training, and does allow her foster mummy to put one on her now, but she is not comfortable on a lead just yet and will need continued support and encouragement to build confidence. She is still learning about house training, and seems to be clean in the home when her foster mummy is around but can have a few accidents when she is left alone. With time and patience, she will begin to pick this up and understand the rules of house training.

She need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and provide reassurance as she adjusts to home life.

Toast arrived with a low-grade luxating patella on her left side, which may improve with gentle exercise. She has also been treated for mucky ears, right-sided otitis, hot spots, and dermatitis, all of which are improving with care. Her general health will need to continue to be monitored in her new home, with any future treatment provided as needed.

Behind her shy beginnings is a sensitive little dog who is still learning to trust the world around her. With patience, understanding, and the right experienced home, Toast will continue to take small steps forward at her own pace.

Toast has arrived in Foster and continues to be a very frightened little girl and can panic easily if anyone tries to pick her up, so she really doesn’t cope well with handling at this stage. Once she is settled in her bed, she is a little more comfortable and will allow gentle strokes and will accept quiet reassurance and talking.

She is extremely nervous overall and will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand how to support a dog like her at her own pace, without pressure. She is also currently living with a cat in her foster home.

I can't believe toast has been here so long that she was due another haircut with me!She has come on tremendously for handling and as long as you're gentle she is content with being picked up, as well as having a harness put on. She is on the journey of learning to walk on a lead and it shouldn't be long before she achieves it.

I've worked with Toast for a while now and I have been able to see how much she's grown over time, especially when it comes to being groomed. The bath is still not her favourite place to be, but she tolerates it, and I think she quite enjoys the warm air of the dryer. She ends up with such a cute haircut because she is so well behaved when it comes to the styling.

This small dog has such a big and beautiful personality and I believe in the right home with another confidence dog she will flourish tremendously.

Toast was such a nervous girl when she came in and she has come on really far since then. I had the pleasure of giving her a much needed groom and although she was nervous she took to it like a champ. She will need grooming upkeep in her forever home to look after her evergrowing locks and I think with a few more pampers she will feel so much more comfortable with it.

She's currently having harness training so she can be more comfortable with the sensation and has gotten much better at being picked up and handled although she can still be a bit jumpy at times but once she's in your arms she's quite calm. She still has a ways to go but I'm so proud of her progress so far and can't wait for when she flourishes with her forever family.

Toast is a delicate little girl who has come to us from a breeder to start her journey towards a brighter future. Right now, the world feels like a very big and scary place to her, and her first instinct is to run and hide in her bed. However, once in your arms, she is easy to handle and accepts gentle reassurance with quiet trust.

Toast will need a calm and understanding home with patient adopters who can give her all the time she needs to find her feet. A kind and confident resident dog will be essential to help guide her, show her that the world can be safe, and give her the courage to explore new experiences.

As she has never lived inside a home before, everything will be new to her, from walking on a lead to learning about house training and family life. Gentle encouragement and plenty of love will help her begin to understand how wonderful it feels to be part of a home.

Toast arrived with a low-grade (Grade 1) luxating patella on the left side, which may improve with gentle exercise. She is also being treated for mucky ears and right-sided otitis as well as dermatitis.

Toast may be shy now, but behind those worried eyes is a sweet girl who just needs the right people to help her shine. With kindness, patience, and a little guidance, she will blossom into a loving and loyal companion.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Snowy
description:
I could live with older dog-savvy teens aged 16+, who respect my space.

I need a laid back dog who is slightly larger than me in my new home.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, but it's still very new for me.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 1 tooth extracted and am being treated for a ear infection.

Snowy is a very sweet little lady who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was quite worried and overwhelmed, but was trying so hard to be brave! She is still feeling quite timid, but once she gets to know she really enjoys having a fuss and is happy to be handled. She is an inquisitive and loving girl and once she's in a home we don’t think it will take long to come out of her shell and show her true personality.

Snowy would love to find a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace and realise what it means to be a loved family member. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers aged 16 and over.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel safe and settled. We have found that she is best suited to living with laid back dogs who are slightly larger than her. She can become a little jealous when other dogs are receiving attention and is more laid back with dogs who are a little bigger than her.

As Snowy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about home life and house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and while this is still very for her, she is doing so well.

With her sweet nature and growing confidence, we are sure it won’t take her long to settle into family life and flourish in a loving home.

Snowy has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay and has prevously been treated for an ear infection.

Snowy has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

This week Snowy has met a few new friends and has been out for her first walk! She took it all in her stride. We were very impressed with how well she has done.

She is a timid lady but really enjoys having a fuss when she gets to know you. She would love a home where she has at least one confident resident dog to help her to settle in. She is currently sharing her kennel with a laid back Scottie dog and gets along well with her, although she ideally needs a friend who is larger than her, she can be quite shy if they are too much larger than her.

She really is a sweetheart who is just looking for her chance at a new and happy life.

Snowy is a wonderful lady who has come to us from a breeder. She is happy to be handled and will shyly approach for fuss and attention, showing that she is trying so hard to be brave and really wants to make friends. Snowy is an inquisitive and loving girl and once she's in a home we don’t think it will take long to come out of her shell and show her true personality.Snowy would love to find a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace and realise what it means to be a loved family member. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers.She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind, calm and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel safe and settled. We have found that she is best suited to living with laid back dogs who are slightly larger than her. She can become a little jealous when other dogs are receiving attention and is more laid back with dogs who are a little bigger than her.As Snowy has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns about house training and walking on a lead. With her sweet nature and growing confidence, we are sure it won’t take her long to settle into family life and flourish in a loving home.Snowy has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay and is being treated for infected ears.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Mika
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

13-08-26 Mika has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is a very shy little lady who prefers to hide away and looks to her canine friends for comfort and reassurance. When left alone, Mika shakes like a leaf, and it is heart-breaking to see just how overwhelmed she can become.

Mika will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that she can lean on as she learns about trust, companionship, and life in a family environment. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to have ex-breeder experience and be patient and understanding as she learns all about house training and settles into a new routine.

Mika does not walk on a lead yet, and venturing out may be too frightening for her initially, so spending time exploring a secure garden and enjoying plenty of sniffing opportunities may be a much better place for her to start. She will need a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace and slowly begin to build her confidence.

Mika has so much potential and so much love to give. She simply needs someone who can see beyond her fears, give her the time she deserves, and help her find her paws in the world.

Mika has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger.

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home! Read below for more!

Maggie is a sweet girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

When Maggie returned to our care, she was a very shy and sensitive girl who was quite worried about meeting new people. Since then she has settled in wonderfully and has well and truly come out of her shell! We would absolutely love to see her back in a home as soon as possible.

Maggie is now confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She could also live with another calm and confident resident dog, but they would need to be her size or larger.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead and will enjoy going for walks with her new family.

Maggie can be particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are ensuring she socialises with males here and she does have a male staff member as part of her care team and has bonded well with him, which is lovely.

Maggie will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in at her own pace. Unfortunately on one occasion, Maggie became tangled in her harness and in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was purely through fear, but due to this, Maggie will be looking for an adult only home.

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and become the most lovely companion.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gabriel
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I cannot live with cats.

I may be shy now, but once I have settled I would love a nice garden I can play in!

I love going for walks, and would love an active home!

I know some tricks & walk well on the lead but will need help with housetraining.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

Gabriel originally came to us from a breeder, and for him the world felt like a very frightening place. He was worried of people, and new environments and unfamiliar experiences left him feeling overwhelmed. Even something as simple as having a lead put on was a huge challenge. He needed time, patience and gentle encouragement to begin to feel safe.

Gabriel was adopted for a short period, but unfortunately it was not the right fit for him. He was returned after displaying unwanted behaviours in the home and making the wrong choices when he felt uncomfortable in a situation, which did result in Gabriel biting. He will need a quiet, adult-only home without resident or visiting children. Gabriel can struggle with visitors coming to the house, so he will need a home without too many visitors and where he can be placed in a separate room when people do come over. His adopters will also need to be willing to meet him multiple times before adoption so that he has the opportunity to develop a bond and build trust with them.

Gabriel requires a highly structured, boundary-focused home with experienced owners who are confident, calm and consistent. He is not a dog who should be allowed on the sofa or encouraged to cuddle up with toys, as we would not want him to be put in situations where he could struggle. Instead, he needs clear rules, his own space and guidance that helps him feel secure and understand what is expected of him. His adopters will need to understand that he has the potential to guard high-value items or sleeping spaces and will need to work with him appropriately. Respecting his boundaries is essential to his wellbeing and success.

Gabriel is muzzle trained and wears his muzzle when out and about, as he has previously redirected when feeling overwhelmed. His adopters will need to be comfortable continuing his muzzle training and using it responsibly as part of his management plan.

Although Gabriel can be nervous and reactive towards strangers, once he has formed a bond with someone, he absolutely loves his people. He forms incredibly strong attachments and becomes deeply loyal once he trusts you. This is one of the things that makes building a relationship with Gabriel so rewarding, but his adopters will need to understand that his affection cannot simply be expected straight away. He needs time to decide that you are someone he can trust.

Gabriel will need both physical and mental stimulation every single day, whatever the weather. Regular walks, enrichment and brain games are a must to keep his active mind engaged and help him remain balanced and settled.

Despite his difficult start, Gabriel has made remarkable progress. These days, he can't wait for his walks and becomes visibly excited when he sees his lead come out. He now happily allows his harness to be put on and walks beautifully, thoroughly enjoying his outdoor adventures.

Gabriel is a very clever boy and a true foodie, which makes training both rewarding and enjoyable. He already knows cues such assitandpawand loves learning new skills. He thrives with clear guidance, consistency and ongoing training, and will do best with an experienced owner who enjoys working with dogs and building a strong, structured relationship.

Gabriel has shown signs of separation anxiety and will need adopters who are home for the majority of the time. He is not suited to being left alone for long periods and will thrive best with someone who can make him a central part of their daily routine. While he is not a dog who seeks constant physical closeness, once a bond is formed he does enjoy affection and gentle fuss in his own way.

He could live as the only dog, enjoying one-to-one attention, or potentially alongside a calm, confident resident dog who respects his space. He will need a home with no cats or small furries.

Gabriel has worked incredibly hard to overcome his fears and has already come so far. He is now searching for a forever home that will offer him understanding, structure, commitment and the chance to live a fulfilled life. For the right, experienced person, Gabriel will be a loyal and incredibly rewarding companion.

Gabrielwill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

This week we’ve had a heatwave which has meant alot of our rescue dogs have needed their ears checked incase they’ve had any mucky build up - Gabriel was one of the unlucky few that have needed some TLC in this area!!We’ve recently had a new meds person who has been visiting Gabriel to do his ear cleans & he has been an absolute angel. He’s even been given the nickname Angel GabrielIt’s just a testament to Gabriel that yes he can be unsure of new people, but once he knows you he truly is such a wonderful boy. He just needs someone to take that chance on him, show him the love he’s desperate to have & he’ll return it tenfold.Gabriel has been waiting such a long time now, and seeing a boy so full of love & hope is heartbreaking when we can’t reassure him that his time will come soon!!!

Today, I worked with Gabriel again for the first time in months. I was a little worried he’d have forgotten, however, it’s safe to say the bond previously made still remains.Gabriel is such an excited little boy. He lives for treats. He’s such a clever and obedient boy when the treats come out. Usually, he’s full of energy and excitement. Once the treats are out, he’s still and sits like the perfect little boy we know he can be.As he can be very busy, I’ve always thought it essential to take him out on walks, the longer the better. As mentioned in a previous update, he loves walks! Once you pull the lead out, you get a similar reaction to the treats.The longer the walk the better. Walks are so good for this gorgeous boy. They keep him stimulated and help shave off the pounds he gains from everyone giving him treats!On the whole, I was so happy to see my boy again. So happy, so loyal, keen to go on walks and he listened so well. I’m so proud of the progress he’s made since I last saw him!Gabriel still can be a challenge and, he does not like everyone. Once you’ve made that bond with him though, it stays. Don’t overlook this boy. He’s such a beautiful, intelligent and fun dog!

This boy has my heart, once you form that special bond with him I do believe it's for life. He is very loving and enjoys a cuddle and a fuss from people he feels comfortable around, as his adopter you'll hopefully get that bond through spending time with him and letting him go at his own pace.Gabriel, as most bockers do, lives for his food and treats, whenever I run him in from being in the yard I always leave a small treat in his bed or somewhere in the back for him to find, and he absolutely loves this he gets so excited knowing he'll get a treat and runs straight to the back of his kennel to find it.He loves his walks and his time in the big yard. He's the curious, adventurous type who just wants to investigate everything, a 10 minute stroll up the road can take us an extra 20-25 minutes to stroll back because he likes to explore, but I don't mind, seeing him happy makes me happy I'd never want to stop him from exploring the world.Gabriel would need an experienced, adult only home (view profile for explanation), he would need someone who is active and can provide him with mental and physical stimulation daily. He is a very smart boy and can pick things up quite quickly which is why, with the help from some treats I think he would pick up toilet training rather quickly.Please don't overlook this handsome guy just because he's not your small and fluffy type dog, Gabriel is a special boy with a lot of love to give, and for that right person/people he would become a true companion and best friend.

Gabriel, a stunning Bocker with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. This handsome boy is full of life and enthusiasm, always ready to embrace whatever the day brings. Gabriel thrives on affection and absolutely loves a good fuss and cuddle — he’s a real people-dog who enjoys being close to those he trusts.

Gabriel is a clever lad with so much potential. He’s already showing us just how intelligent he is as he responds to basic commands! With the right guidance and training , we know he’ll flourish and continue to grow in confidence, not that he lacks any confidence! He also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out on adventures.

Sadly, Gabriel has been returned to us, and we are now searching for the right forever home where he can truly settle and feel secure. Gabriel would be best suited as an only dog, in a calm and quiet home environment. We are looking for a home with minimal visitors and no children, as busy households can feel overwhelming for him.

Gabriel can display guarding behaviours, so he will need experienced owners who understand this and can manage the home environment appropriately to support him. With the right knowledge, structure, and patience, Gabriel will thrive and continue to build trust.

Gabriel has so much love to give to the right person. With understanding, consistency, and kindness, he will make an incredibly loyal and devoted time

Gabriel is a stunning Bocker who is full of life, love, and character! This gorgeous boy is bursting with energy and adores nothing more than a good fuss and a cwtch.He’s incredibly smart, and we just know it wouldn’t take long for him to be trained to a very high standard – he’s already showing us how bright he is every day. Gabriel also walks beautifully on the lead, making him a joy to take out and about.Now all he needs is a forever family who can give him the love, attention, and adventures he deserves. With his brains, energy, and big heart, Gabriel is sure to make someone the most wonderful companion.

Gabriel has come to us from a breeder and has made incredible progress since arriving with us! When he first came, he was nervous around new people and worried about having a lead put on, which made walks and new kennel staff introductions a real challenge. Now, he gets excited for walk time and happily allows us to put on both his lead and harness with no issues.This handsome boy is a true foodie and loves learning new tricks. He already knows “sit” and “paw,” so with trust and patience, teaching him more tricks should be a fun and rewarding experience. Gabriel needs a confident, experienced, owner who will provide clear boundaries and structure, as he can be cheeky if he thinks he’s in charge as well as an adult-only home where he can continue to learn. Gabriel has the confidence to be an only dog in a home with can allow him the dedication and time he needs, or he can be homed with a resident companion that he can continue to learn and grow from, but will need a home with no cats or small furries.Once Gabriel knows and trusts you, he is affectionate, loyal, and loves nothing more than sharing his goofy charm. Underneath his shy moments, he is a beautiful boy with a heart full of love. He is looking for someone who will continue his training, set clear rules, and enjoy all the affection, loyalty, and joy he has to give.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Luca
description:
I'd like an active home and enjoy human company!

I’d like to be the only dog in the home. I can't live with cats or small furries!

I will need a large secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead, although I can pull. I am learning to walk with a muzzle.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home! I have had 1 tooth extracted.

Luca is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. He already knows his name very well, so it would be nice if his adopters kept his name.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and spent most of his life living outdoors, but beneath his impressive appearance is a real softie. He is easy to handle and genuinely enjoys human company, although he understandably found kennel life quite stressful when he first arrived and would often pace his kennel and the exercise yard, struggling to settle.

As Luca has become familiar with the routine, his surroundings and the staff at Many Tears, his confidence has grown enormously. One of the biggest changes we have seen is his newfound love of toys. For the first couple of weeks, he showed no interest in them at all, but now he absolutely adores them! His favourite game is a good game of fetch in the big yard, where he happily charges after his ball with great enthusiasm.

Like many large, playful dogs, Luca can occasionally become overexcited during play. He may jump up to catch the ball or become a little mouthy in his excitement. He is a gentle boy who simply gets carried away when he is having fun. Because of his size and strength, we are helping him learn commands such assit,waitanddrop, as well as encouraging calmer play so he can enjoy himself without becoming overstimulated. This training will be important for his future adopters to continue, as an overexcited Luca could unintentionally knock over someone who is less steady on their feet.

Although he loves chasing a ball, Luca's absolute favourite toys are cuddly toys! He delights in carrying them around and showing off his softer side, which perfectly sums up his character. He really is a big, lovable boy with a wonderfully playful personality.

For now, Luca will need to be the only dog in his home. He has not been kennelled with any other dogs while with us and currently does not mix with them. Luca has had very little basic socialisation with other dogs throughout his life, so we are putting a muzzle-training plan in place with the aim of eventually being able to carefully trial him around other dogs. Until we know more, however, he must remain an only dog and his adopters will need to understand and respect this.

When out walking, Luca can pass other dogs well when they are at a suitable distance, but if another dog barks at him or comes too close, he can become reactive and may get worked up enough to grab at the lead. His future adopters will therefore need to be confident and experienced handlers who are willing to continue his muzzle training and carefully manage his environment. We would consider homing him with dog-savvy older teenagers aged 16+.

Luca is actually very settled when he is in his kennel on his own. He happily lies down in his bed surrounded by his favourite toys and is content to relax, which is a lovely contrast to how unsettled he was when he first arrived.

Luca already walks on a lead, although he can pull initially, so this is something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an active, intelligent boy who would love a home where he can enjoy plenty of adventures, enrichment and quality time with his people. He is also a very strong dog who can jump and even open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who can safely manage his strength.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life, and his adopters will need to be patient and understanding while he learns. With consistency, kindness and plenty of encouragement, we are sure he will adapt well and enjoy discovering all the comforts that a family home has to offer. He is laid-back and loves to relax, so we think he will really enjoy home life.

Luca is an affectionate, loyal and wonderfully characterful boy. Now that he has settled and his playful personality has begun to shine, it has been a joy to watch him embrace life. In the right home, with structure, ongoing training and plenty of love, Luca will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had one tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

Luca has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Before they arrive at Many Tears, many of our dogs have never had toys, and, as strange as it sounds, may not know what to do with them. Fetching, licking, and chewing are important forms of enrichment for dogs and can help to regulate their nervous system and reduce stress, but it can take a while for these dogs to figure out how to use toys in these ways. It's one of the reasons many of our dogs are recommended to have a resident dog at home, as they can learn from each other.

When Luca arrived, he did not engage with toys for the first two weeks or so. He was also very anxious, pacing his kennel and the yard and struggling to settle. However, as he has become used to the routine, surroundings, and staff at Many Tears, Luca has settled very well and discovered a love of all sorts of toys!

We try to give our dogs a mix of toys and enrichment until we know what they like. Luca is not very interested in food-based enrichment like LickiMats or Kongs. He will tug-of-war hesitantly with a rope toy but doesn't really engage with it. However, Luca LOVES a game of fetch down the big yard. He may occasionally jump up to try and get the ball and become over-excited and mouthy, so we are working on balancing his stimulation so he can get his energy out without getting worked up, and on commands like "sit", "wait", and "drop". Luca is incredibly gentle and does not want to hurt anyone, but he is a big boy and could knock a vulnerable person down if he gets too over-excited, so this kind of training is important.

Luca's FAVOURITE type of toy, though, is cuddly toys! It just proves what a big softie he is, as he really loves nothing more than carrying around his stuffed pig toy or cwtching up with his favourite, a string of stuffed Brussels sprouts. It's really lovely to see him relax and enjoy himself this way. Even better when he's doing it on your lap!

Luca is loved by all the staff and volunteers who meet him, but he's definitely ready to be someone's best friend.

Luca is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a fresh start. He already knows his name very well, so his new adopters should keep this the same to avoid confusing him as he settles into his new life.

Luca was previously used as a fake security dog and has spent most of his life living outside, but beneath his big appearance he is a real softie. He is easy to handle and enjoys human company, though he has understandably found kennel life quite stressful and will often plead with us to come back when we have to leave him.

Luca would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where he can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with his new family. He will need adopters who have plenty of time to spend with him and who have experience of the breed or similar breeds. Luca cannot live with cats or small furries and he cannot be around small dogs.

As Luca has spent most of his life outdoors, he will need to learn about house training and the other basics of home life. He will need patient adopters who can help guide him through these new experiences as he adjusts to living in a home environment.

Luca can already walk on a lead, though he does pull at first and so this is something his adopters will need to work on with him. He is a very active boy, so he would love an active household where he can enjoy plenty of adventures and become a loyal companion once he is settled in. He is a strong dog and can both jump and open gates, so he will need a very secure garden and confident handlers who are able to manage his strength safely.

Luca is an intelligent, affectionate, and loyal boy who simply wants to be close to his people. In the right home, with structure, companionship, and plenty of love, he will make an incredibly rewarding companion.

Luca has had 1 tooth extracted at the time of his neuter.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Carys
description:
I need a calm and quiet home, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

24-07-26 Carys is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a larger girl with a typically sweet Cavalier nature. Carys is good with her kennel friends and clearly enjoys having other dogs around. She is easy to handle, although she can be scared when approached and may become submissive while she works out that she is safe.

Carys gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Carys has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and give her time to adjust to her new surroundings.

Carys will need an adult-only home that is calm and quiet as she settles into her new home. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand nervous dogs.

Carys has arrived with sore skin and a thinning coat. She will need a good diet and grrom, and our vets will monitor her to ensure she receives any care she needs. This will need to be continued in her new home.

Carys is a very sweet girl who is still learning that people can be kind. With the support of a friendly dog and a patient family, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy all the comforts of home life.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

name: Rachel
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have had a pea size cyst removed from my right shoulder at the time of spay.

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is understandably overwhelmed by her new surroundings and clearly hasn’t had much socialisation before. However, since being with us, she has slowly started to show small signs of progress as she begins to realise she is safe. Although she still finds being handled very frightening, we are beginning to see small but meaningful improvements in her trust. She is looking for a home with adopters experienced with traumatised ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to continue building her confidence and learning about trust and kindness.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help guide her and provide comfort, as she can still become easily overwhelmed. She takes great reassurance from the presence of other dogs and shares everything beautifully with her kennel companions.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need very patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training, walking on a lead and accepting gentle handling. She follows a daily routine beautifully, happily running out to the exercise yards and returning to her kennel when it is time to come back in. She is not currently 100% kennel clean, but we are confident that she is likely to take to toilet training very well in a home, as she toilets almost immediately when she goes out into the yard. Her adopters will simply need to give her plenty of opportunities to go outside while she learns the new routine.

The big wide world still feels quite scary for Rachel, but she is beginning to show curiosity in safe environments, and gentle time in the garden will be a great way to help her slowly explore and build confidence. She is not yet cat tested, but we feel cats are unlikely to be an issue for her, although this would need to be assessed appropriately.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, but we are continuing to see glimpses of a softer side as she begins to relax in familiar surroundings. Although she still tries her best to avoid being touched and may attempt to bite when she feels frightened, her reactions are already less severe than when she first arrived. She still has the potential to bite if she feels backed into a corner, specifically when she is being picked up or handled, so it is imperative that her adopters fully understand her behaviour and are confident managing her needs.

Recently, Rachel needed to have her thick coat clipped during the warm weather, which unfortunately had to be done under sedation as she is not yet ready to be groomed. Despite how frightening this experience must have been for her, she coped far better than we ever expected, allowing herself to be carried to the vets and held for her injection once she was safely in our arms. We couldn't have been prouder of how brave she was. As her coat grows back, we will continue gently introducing her to grooming so she can slowly learn that being brushed doesn't have to be scary.

Rachel has so much potential and, with time, patience and kindness, we truly believe she will continue to make progress and learn that she is safe and loved. She really is an easy dog to care for in every other aspect – she is wonderful with other dogs, thrives on routine and never puts a paw wrong. She just needs a truly understanding home where she can continue building on the trust she has started to develop and finally blossom into the dog she is meant to be.

Rachel came to us with a pea-sized cyst on her shoulder, which was removed at the time of her spay.

Rachel has been given the Gift of Life by Tracy Davidson

Rachel’s progress continues slowly and steadily and even though she still doesn’t like to be touched, she is so much more content and calm in general. She’s now more than happy to hang out with me and lay down near me, and just this week she actually went to sleep next to me with her tummy exposed!!! I know that may not sound like a lot, but it’s HUGE for a dog like Rachel with such severe trust issues.

The past couple of weeks at the rescue have been extremely warm and Rachel started to struggle a little bit with having such thick fur, so I decided to get it shaved off. Rachel is still not ready to be groomed, so I did have to take her into the vets to be sedated. This is the first time I’ve had to actually pick her up since I started going the crate and touch work with her, but it had to be done. She does still try her very best to get away and she does still try to bite, but it is less severe than what it was when she first came in. Getting her into my arms was the most difficult part, but after I had hold of her I was able to walk over to the vets carrying her, and hold her while she had her injection without a fuss. I was so, so proud of her. She’s now a bit bald, but so much more comfortable and cooler. When her fur starts to grow back I am going to start introducing her to a brush so she can get used to it, as her coat does grow quite fast and it’s very dense which means it gets matted easily. It’s not ideal for a dog like Rachel needing to be groomed regularly, but I’ll try my very best to ease her into it.

Looking after Rachel on a daily basis is very easy. She follows routine beautifully - running to the play yards and back into her kennel when it’s time to come in. She tries her best to be clean with her toileting and I think if she had access to a garden regularly, she would pick it up really quickly. She also shares everything with her kennel friends perfectly and she never puts a paw wrong with other dogs. Aside from hating being touched, she really isn’t a problem at all. I really am hoping that she’ll start to get used to it soon, and I think she will … but being in a home would help massively. So I hope she doesn’t have to wait too much longer for that to happen.

For the past month, Rachel has officially been my “project dog”. This means I’ve been spending a lot more time working directly with her, and I set a goal for both of us when I started. Because Rachel’s biggest fear is human hands, that became my main focus — helping her feel more comfortable with being touched and gently stroked.

In the first week, I wanted to get her used to my touch without her panicking. When Rachel thinks she’s about to be handled, she’ll run around the kennel, jumping from bed to bed to avoid me, and will bite to protect herself if I get too close. I felt that all the running and panic was only reinforcing her fear, making things harder for both of us. So, I introduced a crate to safely contain her in a smaller space, allowing me to begin gentle handling in a more controlled way.

My hope was that she would start to realise that a soft fuss on her head or body isn’t actually that scary — that the anticipation was worse than the reality. Each day for that first week, I set up a crate at the back of her kennel and spent a short session gently touching her, just once a day to ease her into it.

On the first day, it took a little while for her to go into the crate, but she eventually went in with her friend. She was actually very good and allowed me to gently stroke her face for a few minutes, before becoming a little unsettled and starting to nibble my hand. By the second day, she went into the crate much more quickly and again allowed strokes around her head and under her ears. As I carefully moved further down her body, she became uncomfortable and nibbled a bit harder to let me know she’d had enough.

By the third day, she went straight into the crate, and I focused more on her body. She allowed longer strokes before becoming unsettled. The fourth day was very similar, but on the fifth day there was a real breakthrough — she let me stroke her tummy and chest without any nibbles at all.

After every session, I made sure to sit at the front of her kennel for a few minutes and give her treats so we always ended on a positive note (and to make sure she was still my friend!). Rachel is known to hold a grudge, so maintaining that trust was really important, and thankfully this work hasn’t damaged our relationship at all.

In week two, my goal was to remove the crate and see if she would choose to stay settled in a bed while I handled her. I wasn’t sure how it would go, but she absolutely amazed me. On the first day, she settled into a bed at the back of the kennel while I sat on the floor and gently shuffled towards her — and she stayed still, allowing me to stroke her. I kept things consistent over the next few days without pushing her too far.

By the fifth day, I introduced something new: scissors around her head. She needs a fringe trim, so I wanted to begin desensitising her to the sensation and presence of them. She did incredibly well — so well, in fact, that I managed to snip a tiny bit, which I hadn’t even planned to do. Because she was coping so calmly, I took the opportunity, and it paid off.

In week three, I continued trimming her fringe gradually, little by little. After a few days, I was able to clear the hair from around her eyes.

That’s where we are now. There’s still a long way to go, and Rachel will need plenty more time, patience and love, but I’m so pleased with how far she’s come. We’ve definitely made real progress, and I’m excited to keep building on it with her.

Rachel has been at the rescue for just over a month now and in that time she’s gained a lot of inner confidence, and has blossomed into a very cheeky and happy girl who always seems to be up to mischief!! She absolutely loves toys and gets very excited when I put them in her kennel every morning, and she also loves playing with them in the yards. She’s also very partial to starting ‘parties’ AKA getting all the dogs to have a massive game of chase with her, which she finds very amusing. Her favourite thing in the world though … food!!! She is one of the foodiest dogs I’ve ever met and is always at the front of the queue for breakfast, dinner, and treats.Even though Rachel has made progress in many areas, one thing she still simply can’t handle is being touched by us humans in any way. Her fear of our hands is so strong and she will try to bite to protect herself. This doesn’t mean she’s a nasty dog in any way, it’s just complete panic and fear. It’s something I’m trying to de-sensitise her to and I’m working with her as much as I can, but I do think it’s going to take a long time and a lot of consistency. We don’t know what she’s been through in her life that’s made her the way she is, so all we can do now is prove to her that humans can be kind, and hope that one day she’s able to put her past behind her.Rachel will need a very experienced home with people who will be extremely patient with her, understand her, and work with her through her worries and fears. She’ll need at least 1 resident dog to learn from, and absolutely no children. Things that are normal to most dogs such as going for a walk, being brushed/groomed, or even just having a little fuss, are alien to Rachel, so it’s important her adopters take all of this into consideration and be okay with it.

It may be a long and slow road to get Rachel to where she needs to be, but I promise it will be so worth it. There is no better feeling than a dog like her showing you love and trust for the first time!

Rachel is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is a very scared girl at the moment who is quite overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She is looking for a home with adopters with experience of scared ex-breeding dogs who can provide the reassurance and stability she needs to help build her confidence as she learns about safety, trust, and our intentions.

She will need an adult-only home that can offer a calm and predictable environment where she can take things at her own pace. Rachel will also need at least one kind and confident resident dog to help her settle in and take her under their wing, as she can be easily overwhelmed at the moment.

Rachel has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters while she learns about house training and how to walk on a lead. Right now, the big wide world may feel too overwhelming for her, so gentle sniffs in the garden would be a good place to start.

Rachel is only acting out of fear, and we have not yet been able to see the girl she will become once she feels safe. She deserves so much love, she just isn’t sure how to accept it yet and will need a truly understanding home to help her blossom.

Rachel has come to us with a pea sized cyst on her shoulder that has been removed at the time of her spay.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Cuba
description:
I will need a loving and understanding adult-only home!

I'd prefer to be the only dog. I can't live with cats.

I am still unsure about the world, so a secure garden would be ideal.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked, especially by traffic!

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home. Read below for more!

Cuba is a very sensitive and shy boy who is still finding the world quite overwhelming, but who is making lovely progress as his confidence slowly grows. Cuba arrived with very little life experience and can be easily worried by new situations, so he needs a calm, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust.

As he gets to know people, Cuba is becoming increasingly sociable. He may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he trusts you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy quiet, gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby and finds calm strokes very reassuring, often drifting off to sleep while being gently fussed. As his confidence grows, his playful side is beginning to shine. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, giving kisses, and will happily bounce around like a lunatic when he’s feeling safe and excited.

Cuba has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to him. He will need experienced, adult-only adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. Patient guidance will be needed as he learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a harness and lead. He has recently started harness training and is beginning to enjoy it, but this will still need to be continued slowly and positively, starting with gentle practice in the garden. Once out and about, Cuba enjoys taking in the world at his own pace and loves sniffing everything in sight on his walks but he can be spooked by traffic.

Cuba would prefer to be the only dog in the home, so his adopters will need to be around enough to keep him company and provide reassurance as he settles.

He will need a home without cats or small furries as he does have a prey drive.

He is quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character. Beneath his worried exterior, Cuba is a sweet, gentle boy who has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff and is learning that not all people are bad.

Cuba will need a calm and understanding home where his boundaries are respected and he can have his own safe space. With kindness, patience, and the right support, he has the potential to continue blossoming into a truly rewarding companion.

Cuba has had a bilateral entropion repair and is being treated for a ear infection.

Cubawill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Cuba has had quite a busy few weeks at the rescue and has had to put his big boy pants on!! I’ve started taking him into our on site cabin which is similar to being in a home environment. It’s got a sofa, bed, TV etc … so I thought it would be a good idea to start taking him in there to help desensitise him to new things.

Obviously he’s never been in a home before, so everything was completely brand new for him. The first time he was very nervous and really didn’t know what to do at all. He was holding himself low to the floor and hunched, but he was walking around doing little sniffs of things. I was sat on the sofa and he did come over to me a couple of times for reassurance which did help a little, but after about only 5 minutes I took him back to his kennel as I didn’t want to overdo it.

The second time he was still nervous again, but after a little while he did start to drop his guard and became quite curious. He kept coming over to me for a fuss and a treat, so that was a really good sign being brave enough to eat in there. He was fascinated by the TV and didn’t quite know what to think of it. He was a bit scared of it I think, but equally as intrigued. I’m going to keep taking him into the cabin once a week or so just to ease him into it slowly, and then hopefully that will help his transition to home life when he does get adopted.

Cuba has been with me for over 3 months now and I literally love him more and more every day. I’m lucky to have a very close relationship with him and he loves me and trusts me completely, so I see a side to him that not many other people get to see.

He absolutely oozes charisma and character, and he makes me laugh and smile every time we’re together. He’s fiercely loyal, super affectionate, and SO comical. He gives the best of everything. He loves running around the yard with me and playing with toys, but loves a big sit down snuggle equally as much. So much so, he now likes to sprawl across my whole lap and fall into a deep sleep on me (snores and all)! His kennel is filled with plush toys that he loves to carry around in his mouth and sleep with, and he’s SO gentle with them. Isn’t he just the sweetest boy!?

He does still find a lot of things quite challenging, but I do feel as though we’re still making steady progress, and you can’t rush certain things. He’s still very easily spooked by loud noises, cars passing, people trying to approach him etc, so on walks especially I do have to make sure I’m paying complete attention to him. Most of the time he does recover quickly with a bit of reassurance from me, but then sometimes it will ruin his whole walk and he’ll immediately want to turn around and go back to the safety of his kennel. That’s okay though - I always allow it and take him back to make sure he knows he always has a safe place as and when he needs it.

We’ve briefly mentioned in a previous update that Cuba doesn’t like other dogs that much, but I hope this won’t put you off him as he’s not reactive to other dogs out on walks or anything like that - he simply just doesn’t like to share his space with them. I don’t think he was socialised with others apart from his old kennel friend before he came to us, so I think it’s understandable.

If you have the time and the patience to put the work in with Cuba, I can promise you 10 times over that adopting him will be the best decision of your life. Once he settles, he will truly be your best friend and the love of your life. That’s how I feel about him and I’m just his kennel mum!! He is utterly special and he deserves someone equally as special, who will love him as much as he will love them. He has such a big heart and he really does deserve the world and more.

Cuba has come on leaps and bounds over the past few weeks, and I feel so lucky to have been appointed as his “Kennel Auntie,” spending two days a week with this incredibly handsome boy.

Although Cuba can still be wary of strangers, the bond he forms once he trusts you is truly something special. Knowing him from when he first arrived, you honestly wouldn’t recognise him now. He used to hide away at the back of his kennel, wishing we would go away, now he demands to be the centre of attention and absolutely smothers you in kisses. While he may take a little time to warm up to new people, once he feels safe, his affectionate nature shines through.

Cuba has taken some big steps (quite literally!) and is absolutely smashing his harness training. His progress has been incredible, and his confidence grows more each day. He happily trots along on walks, tail wagging, taking in all the exciting new smells he’s never experienced before. Watching him discover so many “firsts” is truly magical.

We’ve found that Cuba isn’t too fussed about other dogs (aside from his kennel friend Chippy), so he would be best suited to a home where he can be the only dog. This will allow him to soak up all the love and attention he thrives on.

I cherish every moment I get to spend with Cuba. He is the sweetest, soppiest boy. He is so full of love, yet not enough people get to see this side of him. He adores playing with toys, cuddling, bouncing around like a lunatic, giving kisses, and sniffing everything in sight on his walks. But most of all, he loves his people.

There isn’t a moment with Cuba where you won’t feel loved. He makes every second count and whoever is lucky enough to adopt him should do the same. He truly is a special boy, and you wouldn’t want to miss out on him.

Cuba has been on my section for a few weeks now and I am just head over heels in love with him. I knew he was a nervous and sensitive boy so I have taken things slow with him and left him be to suss me out and get used to my routine, but it really didn’t take long for him to become quite attached to me. Within a few days he started to trust me, and now I would say he actually trusts me completely. So much so, I’ve been able to start harness training with him, put medication in his eyes after his surgery, and he’s given me his belly a couple of times for fusses!!!

I still haven’t taken him outside of the secure yard on his harness yet, but I do think he’s ready so I’m going to try it really soon. His biggest fear was having any tension on the lead - he would get really spooked by it and panic - but I think we’re just about over that now and he’s gotten used to it.With Cuba, once he gets to know you and forms a bond with you he is an extremely affectionate, happy, and playful boy, but he is still standoffish with people he doesn’t know and he doesn’t trust them to touch him or handle him. This is something his future adopters will need to take into consideration and prepare for. He’ll just need to be given some time, patience and gentleness to begin with. I am certain he’ll come around, but it will need to be in his own time as he can’t be pushed.

Cuba is hilarious and so goofy, and he will make such a great addition to someone’s home in time, but it does need to be the right home to ensure he’s set up for only success. I adore him very much and I just know his future parents will too, so please keep him in mind if you think you could be a good match for him!

Cuba is making lovely progress and is becoming increasingly sociable as his confidence grows. He is still finding walking on a harness quite scary and will need a patient home willing to help him continue this training at his own pace.

Cuba may need a couple of meetings to feel comfortable, but once he knows you, he will happily approach with his tail wagging and enjoy a gentle fuss. He particularly loves relaxing in his bed with trusted company nearby, quietly enjoying being stroked as he drifts off to sleep.

At heart, he is a very sweet and gentle boy who is learning to trust and has already formed strong bonds with familiar staff. He is simply a scared boy who needs a fresh start in a calm, understanding and respectful home where he can continue to blossom.

Cuba is a very nervous and shy boy who is finding the world quite overwhelming at the moment. He needs a slow, gentle approach and plenty of time to build trust, but once he feels safe with someone, he will allow calm, gentle fuss while settled in his bed, which he finds very reassuring. Underneath his worried exterior, Cuba is simply a big, scared baby who needs kindness, patience, and understanding to help him feel secure.

Cuba will need an adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand nervous dogs and are happy to let him settle at his own pace. He has never lived in a home before, so everything will be completely new to him. His adopters will need to be patient and supportive as he learns about home life, including house training and how to walk on a harness and lead. Gentle practice in the garden will be an important starting point before he is ready to venture further afield.

Cuba will also need at least one kind, confident resident dog in the home. He gains comfort and confidence from other dogs and will benefit greatly from having a calm canine role model to help guide him and show him that the world is a safe place. He is not suitable to be an only dog.

Cuba is currently learning to walk on a harness, but this is something he finds very challenging and will require a great deal of time, patience, and dedication. He is also quite fond of using his voice and enjoys a good grumble rather than barking, which is very much part of his character.

Cuba will need a calm, quiet home where he can have his own safe space and plenty of downtime alongside gentle interaction. With love, reassurance, and understanding adopters, he will slowly begin to realise that not all people are bad and that he is finally safe. In the right home, with the right support, Cuba has the potential to blossom into a deeply rewarding companion.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Louise
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home with experienced adopters.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am not ready to learn about lead walking yet. A garden is fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and can still find people and handling very frightening. However, she has made lovely progress since arriving and is showing us more of her cheeky personality every day.

Over the past month, Louise has grown in confidence. While she is still very worried about being touched and picked up, she is no longer as shut down as she was when she first arrived. She is now more than happy to come over for treats and will sit close by while waiting for more. She likes to use her voice to let everyone know how she is feeling, is very partial to chasing flies, and has quite a big personality packed into such a tiny dog. It is wonderful to see her becoming more comfortable in her surroundings.

Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her as she settles into family life.

Louise can be vocal around food and may give a warning growl, but she does not actually do anything and this appears to simply be her way of communicating that she would like some space. She can happily be fed alongside her canine friends as long as each dog has their own bowl and they stick to their own food. She is also absolutely fine taking treats, so this is something her adopters should continue to manage calmly and sensibly.

Louise is slowly becoming more comfortable with being handled, and gentle work has begun to help her get used to being picked up. This is still very worrying for her and she can become wriggly and panic when lifted, but she has never tried to bite during these sessions. With time and patience, we hope she will continue to learn that she is safe and that nobody is going to hurt her.

Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns the basics, including house training. She is not yet ready for harness training, so her future family will need to carefully plan how and when to introduce this once she feels more secure. Everything must happen at Louise's pace so that she can continue building confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Louise is a sensitive little soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her flourish. Every small step she takes is a huge achievement, and she continues to surprise us with just how much she is growing in confidence. With experienced adopters, kind canine companions and lots of love, we truly believe Louise will continue to blossom into the wonderful little dog we know she can become.

Louise has been given the Gift of Life by Ann Winter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.
