Louise has been on my section with me for about a month now, and I’ve definitely seen some positive changes in her. She’s still terrified of being touched and picked up, but her overall confidence is improving daily. She’s now more than happy to come and take treats from me and sit close to me while she’s waiting for more. She’s also nowhere near as shut down as she was when she first arrived and is now turning into quite a cheeky monkey. She does like to use her voice to express her feelings, and she’s also very partial to chasing flies! She’s actually got quite a big personality for such a little girl, and it’s a pleasure to see it emerging as the days go by.I’ve been working slowly on getting Louise used to being picked up, and while she’s definitely still very worried about it, she has calmed down slightly. She’s never tried to bite me, but she does sometimes have little panics and becomes very wriggly when she’s in my arms. I do think this is something that will improve over time. She just needs some more practice and to realise that we’re not hurting her. She obviously hasn’t been handled a lot in her life, so now it’s up to us to prove to her that it’s okay.I love working with Louise, and I can really see the potential in her. She just needs someone to give her a chance and work with her through all her worries and fears. She’s not ready for harness training or conquering the outside world yet, so that’s something her future adopters will need to take into consideration and make a plan for. I do believe she’ll progress faster in a kind home with adopters who have lots of time and patience to give her, so I really hope she won’t have to wait here for much longer.

Louise has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is an extremely worried little girl who has had very little positive human socialisation and currently finds people and handling very frightening. At the moment, Louise feels safest keeping her distance and, if pushed beyond her comfort zone, may make the wrong decision and nip purely out of fear. She is a very scared girl who needs understanding, patience and time.Louise will need a calm and quiet adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who have experience of helping fearful ex-breeding dogs learn to trust. She relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can take her under their wing.Although Louise takes great comfort from other dogs, she can show signs of resource guarding around food. For this reason, she will need to be fed separately from other dogs, and care will need to be taken when giving treats or other high-value food items. Her adopters will need experience of managing this behaviour and the confidence to do so appropriately.Having never lived in a home before, Louise has lots to learn. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to home life and learns new skills such as house training. She is not yet ready to begin learning about lead walking or wearing a harness, as handling is still very worrying for her. These things will need to be introduced gradually and at her pace once she feels more comfortable and secure.Louise is a sensitive soul who will need a dedicated home willing to invest time, patience and understanding into helping her build confidence. We will continue to work with her every day, helping her take small steps forward at a pace she is comfortable with. In the right home, with the support of canine friends and experienced adopters, we hope Louise will slowly learn that people can be kind and that life has so much to offer.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Davina
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I've started harness training but I'm still too scared to walk just yet.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

17-07-26 Davina came to us from a breeder and is now searching for a patient and understanding forever home. We have been told she is a Miniature Doodle (she weighs just under 10kg), but whatever her mix may be, one thing is certain, she's absolutely adorable.

Davina is a very gentle and sensitive little girl who is still finding the world quite overwhelming. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and relies on them for reassurance while she learns that people and new experiences aren't so frightening. Although she is beginning to observe what's going on around her, she is still a very worried girl who needs time to build trust and confidence.

Because of this, Davina is looking for a calm, quiet home with adopters who haveexperience of ex-breeding dogsand understand that confidence cannot be rushed. She will need people who are happy to let her settle entirely at her own pace, allowing her to make progress in her own time without any pressure or expectations.

Davinamust have another kind, confident resident dogin her new home. Having a canine companion is essential for her, providing reassurance, helping her understand home life and giving her the confidence to follow their lead as she discovers the joys of being part of a family.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be completely new to Davina. She will need help with house training, learning household routines and gradually becoming accustomed to everyday sights and sounds. Lead walking will also be something to build slowly, beginning with gentle introductions in the safety of the garden before venturing further afield when she feels ready.

Due to her nervous nature, Davina is looking for anadult-only homewhere she can enjoy a peaceful, predictable environment while she continues to blossom.

Davina is a sweet little soul who simply needs time, patience and understanding. Watching a frightened ex-breeding dog gradually discover that life can be safe and happy is incredibly rewarding, and we have no doubt that, in the right home, Davina will continue to grow in confidence and become a devoted companion.

Davina has been given the Gift of Life by Ceri Mann

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Whimsey
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teens who are sensible and will allow me to settle.

I could live as an only dog, or with a similar sized canine friend. No cats please!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead, but will need guidance in the outside world.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Whimsey came to us from a breeder as a very worried little girl who found the world quite overwhelming. When she first arrived, she was unsettled and skittish, needing plenty of time and reassurance to help her feel safe. Since then, she has made wonderful progress and has really started to show what a special girl she is.

Whimsey has formed a lovely bond with her carers and now greets those she knows and trusts with enthusiastic cuddles and kisses. It has been a joy to watch her confidence grow, and she is becoming more comfortable with the people around her every day.

While Whimsey has come on tremendously, she can still be nervous and unsure around new people. She will need a calm, patient and understanding home that is willing to give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle at her own pace. Once she feels safe, her affectionate and loving personality truly shines through. She could also live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can respect her need for a gentle introduction and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Whimsey walks nicely on a lead, but as she can still be sensitive to new experiences, her adopters will need to continue introducing her to the world gently and at a pace she is comfortable with, helping her build confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Whimsey really enjoys spending time with other dogs and loves socialising with her canine friends in the exercise yards. We now feel she could happily live with another resident dog of a similar size, provided they get along well during a successful meet and greet. Like many dogs, Whimsey can be a little selective about her friendships, so finding the right canine companion will be important. She would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home, where she could soak up all the love and attention from her family while continuing to enjoy opportunities to socialise with other dogs on walks. She cannot live with cats.

Whimsey has such a sweet heart and has already shown just how much progress she can make when given kindness, patience and understanding. With the right home behind her, we know she will continue to blossom into a wonderfully affectionate companion and a much-loved member of the family.

Whimsey arrived with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which has been treated by our veterinary team. Our vets have also noted that she has a fractured canine tooth with no root or nerve exposure. At this stage, no treatment is required, but it should be monitored by her adopters and their own vet. She has also received treatment for a urinary tract infection, which has been successfully managed under veterinary guidance.

Oh, my heart. Whimsey has completely stolen it.

She is honestly one of the most loving, affectionate, and gentle girls I've ever met. The moment I walk into her kennel or sit with her in the yard, she melts into me. All she wants is kisses, cuddles, and to be as close to you as possible. She has so much love to give!

She's doing so well with her dog socialising too and absolutely adores her best friend, Royal.

Whimsey is going to make the most incredible addition to a very lucky family. She deserves so much more than just being someone's dog. She deserves to be a cherished member of the family, included in all of life's little moments, loved unconditionally, and never made to wonder if she's enough again.

I truly can't wait for the day she finds the home she's been waiting for. Whoever gets to call this beautiful girl theirs is going to be incredibly lucky.

Whimsey has come on so well since she first arrived. She’s bonded with me so much and always welcomes me with a big kiss and cuddle.

She can be nervous and unsure around new people, but with time, patience, and understanding, she’s going to make the most wonderful addition to someone’s home.

Although she needs to be the only dog in the home, she can happily socialise with other dogs and loves going down to the big yard with her friends.

Whimsy has come to us from a breeder and is a very worried girl. When she first arrived, she was very unsettled at the moment and could be quite skittish, finding so many of the sights and sounds of the world quite overwhelming. Since arriving she has started to settle in and come out of her shell, but will still need time and TLC as she settles in to her new life. Once she gets to know you, she will quietly approach you and allow a gentle fuss.

Whimsy needs time to learn and to trust, and needs a calm and quiet home home that understands ex-breeding dogs and will allow her the space she needs to learn about trust at her own pace. She will need a calm, patient, and understanding family who are willing to let her take things slowly and gently as she begins to discover the comforts of home life.

She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her home that she can look to and rely on as she learns about home life and settles in. Having a canine companion to guide her will really help build her confidence and show her that the world can be a safe and happy place.

Whimsy does walk well on a lead, but as she can be a bit skittish, her adopters will need to take the outside world at her own pace, allowing her the time she needs to gain confidence in her surroundings without feeling pressured.

Whimsy seems like she has such a sweet heart, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will begin to show her loving and gentle nature. She just needs someone special to help her learn about trust and companionship and to show her that she is safe and loved.

Whimsy has come to us with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which is being treated by the vets. Our vets have noted that she has one fractured canine, but no root or nerve exposure and so it is advised to leave it at this time, but will need monitoring by her adopters and their vet. She is currently being treated for a UTI and will be rechecked once the course of medication has finished.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Trixie
description:
I'll need an adult only home with adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs.

I am looking for a home where I can be the only dog & get all the love and attention.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I walk on a lead but will need my adopters to be extra secure.

I understand toilet training, but will need a reminder in a new home!

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home! Read below for more info!

Trixie is an amazing little lady who came to us from a breeder. She found kennel life quite overwhelming at first and took some time to settle in, but she has gradually grown in confidence and is now beginning to let her wonderful personality shine. Once Trixie learns to trust you, she becomes incredibly affectionate and loves nothing more than being close to her favourite people. She will happily climb into your lap for cuddles and enjoys soaking up as much attention as possible.

Trixie spent some time in a foster home, where she began to experience life in a home environment. This helped to build her confidence and allowed her to start learning that the world isn't such a scary place. Despite the progress she has made, she will still need time to adjust and would much prefer a calm, quiet home without too much hustle and bustle, allowing her to settle at her own pace and build a strong bond with her new family.

Trixie has returned to the rescue after we discovered that she would be happiest as the only dog in the home. Since returning, it has been lovely to see her personality continue to blossom. She enjoys spending time with other dogs in the yard and gets very excited to see her canine friends each day. She is happy to socialise with calm dogs while out and about, but within the home she can become jealous when attention is shared and has occasionally reacted towards other dogs.

For this reason, Trixie will need a home where she is the only pet, with no resident dogs or cats. She will also need an adult-only home with adopters who understand the needs of ex-breeding dogs and can give her the time, patience, and one-to-one attention she truly deserves.

In the garden, she displayed digging behaviours and has previously tried to escape a foster home, so very secure boundaries are essential. Her new home will need to have 6ft minimum fencing height and her new adopters will need to keep her on lead in the garden until she gains confidence outside. Trixie had been mostly clean in the house in her foster home, and seemed to be a star at toilet training. However, she may need some reminders in her new home as she settles in new surroundings. She is walking on a lead and harness, but can still become startled and may try to back out if frightened.

She has had a small lump removed from her left mammary gland and is recovering well.

Trixie has been given the Gift of Life by Tanya Player

Hello, my name is Trixie and I'm living at Many Tears whilst I wait for my forever home to find me.

My perfect home would be with lovely, gentle people, that enjoy a quiet life. I am easily worried by new sounds and loud noises and so I will need lots of time to adjust to my new home and environment. I love a squishy bed to lie on and one of those sofas I hear about sounds perfect to try.

I would be very happy in a secure garden where I won’t be bothered by other people, just my family, sitting with me and a few toys for little plays. Perhaps when I get used to my new people we could go for walks in quiet places together - but I will need time before I’m fully ready to do this.

I enjoy my food, so a good supply of tasty meals would make me very happy. I really don’t want much just a simple, safe and loving home.

Side note from my kennel mum:Trixie is a wonderful loving dog once she feels safe with you. She is a flight risk when startled - and she is easily startled!

If every day was a Trixie day, life would be lovely. Trixie is the sweetest and loveliest of dogs. Her favourite pastimes include tummy rubs and cuddles, and if there’s a home out there with a Trixie-sized spot on the sofa and a human to shower her with fusses, she would be in heaven.

When Trixie is happy, you know it, and she will bounce around you outside for a little play before parking herself next to you for more belly rubs. She loves sitting outside and just relaxing with you.

Trixie does also enjoy a walk (in very quiet areas); however, she can be very, very easily spooked and, if startled, will bolt and has done so previously. Any adopters would need to be very aware of this and work on building her confidence at home before considering outings. Adopters will also need to ensure a very secure setup for her at home, i.e. secure entrances and exits from the house.

Trixie prefers to have a human all to herself and, for this reason, she would like to be the only dog with a human who will be home most of the time.

Trixie truly is a gem of a girl with a heart of gold. A special and sweet lady, who longs for safe hands (and laps) to snuggle into. This super dog needs a little time and a lot of security,  give her that and you will have a bond for life.

Trixie is looking for a home that is quiet, gentle, patient and super secure on a practical level. Trixie is incredibly spooky and even if she trusts you, the slightest of frights in her environment and she will bolt. Because Trixie is a high flight risk she would be suited to a dog experienced home, ideally with knowledge of flighty and/or ex-breeding dogs.

It’s important that her new people have a secure plan for getting her out of the car on arrival home after adoption and are able to keep entrance and exits to the house escape safe. In return for your kindness Trixie will be the cutest of best friends. Trixie is looking to be the only dog and is suited to an adult home with no visiting children.

Trixie has been in foster with me for three weeks now and is settling into our routine fairly well.

When she first arrived, Trixie was very human-oriented and showed signs of jealousy towards other dogs, which led to a few altercations. She would often growl if another dog came close to me, as she wanted all the attention for herself. This is something we’ve been working on, but we still feel it is best if she is homed as an only dog in her new home.

From her interactions with my resident dogs, it’s clear that Trixie isn’t comfortable with small, yappy dogs. She does seem to prefer female human company, although she is continuing to build confidence more generally. She currently sleeps downstairs in an open, covered crate, which she uses as her safe space.

For the first couple of weeks, Trixie has slept downstairs quietly through the night with no accidents. Over the last few nights, she has been a little more unsettled and has had a couple of accidents, which seems to be linked to wanting more human attention.

Trixie is fed on dry Arden Grange and is currently fed separately, as she will try to eat other dogs’ food if given the chance. She was also caught eating poo, so I have started soaking her food in hot water and letting it cool, which she seems to prefer.

In her first week, Trixie did try digging in the garden and looking for ways to escape, but this behaviour has now settled. She clearly recognises me and gets very excited when she sees me, running over happily for fuss and attention.

She has been out on walks and does reasonably well when accompanied by another dog, but she is still quite flighty and easily startled. For now, she should only be walked in secure areas, as she will try to back out of her harness if she feels unsure and has demonstrated this once already.

Trixie can be complex at times, so she will need a calm, experienced adopter who understands nervous, ex-breeding dogs and can handle her with patience and care. It will be important to give her time to settle at home and build trust before introducing too many new experiences, especially.

Trixie absolutely craves human attention and is happiest curled up next to me on the sofa. As her confidence continues to grow and her jealousy is managed, she has all the makings of a very loyal and loving companion who simply wants to feel safe and adored.

Trixie is now in foster and is settling in well. She travelled well and was clean on arrival with no issues noted in the car or on entering the home.

Once in the foster home, Trixie has shown herself to be a very nervous little girl who is still unsure of new environments and needs encouragement to engage with people. She will often hang back and watch, but once she feels a bit more secure she will come forward and seek interaction. On these occasions she has chosen to snuggle close to me and will sit gazing and enjoying contact, although she does need to be gently encouraged each time as confidence doesn’t yet seem consistent.

It has quickly become apparent that Trixie is quite a complex girl in the home. She is very focused on attention and has already shown signs of jealousy when sharing human interaction. On one occasion, when another foster dog came onto the sofa, Trixie reacted strongly and became defensive. She can also be particular about other dogs in general and can be especially reactive to barking dogs, and has shown a clear dislike of a small dachshund in the home. For this reason, she will now be looking for a home as an only dog where she can get all of the attention for herself.

Outside of this, she is an active little girl and has already shown she is a determined digger, having previously managed to dig under fencing and patio areas. This will need careful management going forward with very secure boundaries required.

Overall, Trixie is settling in but is still very much finding her feet.

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I will need to be neutered when I am of age! It's important!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.

name: Flash
description:
I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed. Since then, we’ve watched him grow from a worried boy into a much more confident and affectionate companion, and he continues to make us proud every single day.

Flash is still very much a character, goofy, playful, and full of energy but beneath his bouncy exterior lies a gentle heart that just wants to love and be loved. He can be sensitive in new situations and still finds the world a little overwhelming at times, but with people he trusts, his sweet and loyal nature shines through. Once Flash bonds with you, he is yours for life.

Recently, he’s been showing us more of his loving side. On rainy days when we huddle together out of the downpour, he rolls over for belly rubs, brings his toys for attention, and happily drifts off to sleep during a cuddle. It’s in these quiet moments that his true personality comes out, affectionate, trusting, and eager to please.

Flash’s training is going from strength to strength. He’s mastered “touch” (booping his nose to your hand) and is now learning “place.” He still gets a little mouthy when he’s overexcited, but he’s come a long way since his arrival and continues to improve with patience and consistency. He’ll need his future family to have ex-breeding experience and to continue this gentle guidance in the home so he can keep building on all the progress he’s made.

Being an active breed, Flash loves his walks and enjoys exploring the world at his own pace. He’s happiest in calm, quiet areas where he can relax and take everything in without feeling rushed. He will need to be the only pet in the home, as he prefers human companionship over other animals, and he’s not a fan of pigeons or seagulls either!

Flash has had successful surgery for entropion in both eyes, he received care for mild dermatitis around both eyes, but this has since cleared. He is currently being treated for sore and sensitive ears.

What Flash truly needs now is a calm, understanding, adult-only home with ex-breeding experience and with someone who’s around most of the time, someone who can offer him patience, structure, and all the love he deserves. With time and trust, Flash will repay his person a hundred times over with loyalty, affection, and that special spark that makes him so unforgettable.

Please don’t overlook this beautiful boy. Flash has come so far and is ready to start the next chapter of his life he’s just waiting for that one person to believe in him and bring him home.

Flash will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Flash has officially been waiting for a home for a whole year. After a first few months of (a lot of) patience and training, it's then blossomed into the most incredible remaining months where we’ve really seen Flash’s true heart and soul. This dog is phenomenal in more ways than one, and it’s so sad he’s now become part of the MT furniture, and that the rescue has now become his home.

So for Flash’s 1 year anniversary, I took him off site to the nearby country park for a lovely stroll, followed by a visit to McD’s for some chicken nuggets.

Flash was suuuuuuch a good boy on his walk. He took in all the new smells, and took the new environment in his stride. He was even approached by 3 off lead small dogs, and didn’t react at all. He trotted along the park, with the world at his feet and it was the most amazing thing to see.

He is an absolute darling in the car, so we made a swift visit to McD’s for a box of 20 nuggets to eat together in our on site flat.

It was so nice to see Flash in a home like environment, he jumped straight on the sofa, and wandered around inspecting every room. We sat on the floor together eating our nuggets, and he eventually rested on the raised bed and had a little snooze.

It was heartbreaking putting him back in his kennel, when he seemed so at peace and settled in the flat. I just wish there was someone out there who could see him for everything he is and more!!!

Our beautiful, bonkers Flash has learnt a new trick and we thought we would share.

Flash has also been enjoying the sunshine with lots of walks and plays in the yards this week.

Flash continues to work hard on growing his calmness around new people and he is doing ok. He has now been 10 months here at the rescue and has an increasing fan base amongst the staff but he of course longs for a home and people of his own.

When I first started working with him, I was apprehensive. He was a much larger dog than I was used to working with, and he would mouth you til his hearts content. Not because he is a nasty dog, or means any harm whatsoever, but simply because he has come from a home (just out of puppyhood) and he has become extremely anxious and unsettled being in a kennel environment. On top of that, he has been taught 0 manners which definitely didn’t help with the matter!!! I struggled to bond with him, I struggled to understand why he wouldn’t listen when being told, and why all he wanted to do was treat my arm like a toy…

However I found myself thinking, what has Flash been through in his life that was ever HIS fault? He didn’t ask to spend so much of his life in kennels. He never asked to be put in situations where his anxiety gets the better of him, it was never his decision to not be trained to behave normally. So I decided to buck up my ideas and realise he’s not as scary as he seems, and he’s probably just as anxious being around me as I was him. And from that moment on, our relationship has blossomed…

This boy is truly a superstar in every sense of the word. He is SUCH a goofball, and can have you in fits of laughter within seconds of being with him. His personality is infectious, and as soon as he is comfortable with you and realises you are no threat to him, he shines like the star he is. It’s gutting that Flash doesn’t allow every staff member to see all sides of him. The side that shows his softness, his sweetness, his kindness. But that just makes me so much more grateful that he feels comfortable enough around me to do so.

You can see from his pictures, Flash is muzzle trained. Not because he is an aggressive dog, not because he is a violent dog, it’s simply due to his anxiousness. On one hand, Flash is a super intelligent Poodle but on the other hand, he doesn’t really show it. His anxiety gets the better of him, and he puts himself in uncomfortable positions with new people & then panics whilst he’s in it. It is SUPER important that whoever adopts Flash’s main priority is keeping him safe, and keeping him from making decisions that he feels uncertain about. He wants to make friends with everyone, but also decides halfway through some interactions that he’s not to keen on the thought too!

Among (of course) all of the other precious angels I look after the rescue, Flash is one of the reasons I get excited to go to work. You shouldn’t really have favourites, but Flash does take the cake. I cherish every single moment I get with him. Our lovely strolls up the country lanes, our snuggles in the back of his kennel after a long day, our zoomies down our big play yard. Every single moment & memory I look forward to recreating every single day. Nothing tops being around this dog, nothing else matters when you’re with Flash.

If I was in a position to take him home & work with him through his quirks, I absolutely would, in heartbeat in fact. There is just something so special about him, and I truly envy whoever is fortunate to adopt this incredible young man. And for as long as Flash remains in kennels, I will advocate for him, make him feel safe, comfortable and most of all loved.

Flash has completely changed my mind about Poodles. I am absolutely in love with him. He might not be the sharpest boy in the bunch, but he more than makes up for it with his goofy charm and endless silliness.We are still working on his mouthing when he becomes overexcited. Progress is steady, and every small step forward feels like a real achievement. Flash loves his freedom. We take daily trips to the big yard where he runs around like the happiest whirlwind you have ever seen. He would really benefit from visits to private dog fields where he can safely zoom and explore to his heart’s content.Meeting new people can still be a little tricky for him, but we have a careful plan in place to help him do so safely and comfortably. For those of us who know Flash well, he shows a side many would not expect. Beneath his anxiousness and the need for a muzzle at times is the sweetest, softest boy who adores snuggles and head tickles.He loves to stay close, gently resting his head in your lap until he drifts off to sleep. At the end of each day, we share a quiet moment together, curled up side by side until his eyes close and he is peacefully dreaming.Flash truly is a special boy who deserves a very special home. He needs someone who can offer love, patience, and understanding. In return, he will give unwavering loyalty and companionship for life.

Flash is an absolute character, this boy is full of life and once he knows you he adores you but his introductions to new people always need to be slow as this sensitive boy can be easily overwhelmed.

Flash works well within a routine, he has an abundance of energy and a super inquisitive nature which can sometimes lead to him becoming quite lively, he will often revert to ‘mouthing’ and jumping up when he is uncomfortable or unsure.

Flash has a super inquisitive nature and loves to observe what’s going on at a distance. This boy can also be an absolute cuddle monster and adores a snuggle with his favourite people, and will fall asleep next to us when we have the opportunity to sit quietly with him. One of flash’s unique traits is his love of a pamper session! I have never known a dog who enjoys a bath and hairdryer the way he does and he becomes quite docile under the hair dryer whilst having a gentle brush.

Flash’s ideal home would be a quiet an experienced dog owning home (adults only) with humans that have the patience and time to help grow his confidence and who also understand the need to grow calmness in him. Flash has had a few dog friends at the rescue but his high spirted nature can be a bit much for some dogs and he does not seem to like male dogs, for this reason a home where he is the only pooch would suit him best.

Flash walks well on lead but can become very excited when he sees other dogs, walks in quiet areas would be perfect for him, he loves to be outdoors and often just enjoys sitting in the yard with me watching birds, but he will equally enjoy time spent just hanging out with his humans at home. Flash really is a wonderfully, lovable, giant puppy, looking for kind and understanding humans to provide him with the security and love he deserves.

Flash has had a brilliant few weeks. He celebrated his second Birthday and was treated with his first snow day, which he loved frolicking about in. Unfortunately, he did have to spend his birthday in kennels, but I made sure it was still a very special day for him. We hopped in the car, and I took him for a little walk before heading to the pet shop to pick out some birthday treats. He chose a dinosaur toy and a knuckle bone, which he thoroughly enjoyed. I also bought him some special birthday biscuits to keep him going through the week.

After that, I truly spoiled him, and we decided to go to Burger King for a burger! Flash was quite confused at first, but once he had a taste, he couldn’t get enough.

Flash truly is a special boy and will need a special home to match. He can be very wary of strangers and doesn’t always show clear signs if he’s uncomfortable. For this reason, he is muzzled when out on walks, which I make sure to do whenever we go out.

Flash will need an adult-only home with no visiting children. He cannot live with cats or any small animals

The stunning Flash had a little pamper today, which he absolutely loved. He was as good as gold whilst in the bath and sat very contentedly on the grooming table looking out the window enjoying the warmth of the blowers. I have never known a dog to enjoy bath time as much as he does, he becomes quite sleepy and cuddley, it’s the cutest thing.

After his wash and blow dry he got to open some Christmas treats out in the yard sent in from the lovely folks out there that support Many Tears, Flash particular enjoyed the food presents.

Flash really is the most wonderful boy once you get to know him, and we see improvement every day in his sometimes lively and skittish nature. This fantastic boy will make the most awesome and loyal of friend with the person or couple that are prepared to put the time and love into him he so deserves.

Today, Flash and I went on a little adventure to the local pet shop, finishing off with a much-needed pupcup! He was an absolute angel in the car—he hopped right in, buckled up, and sat calmly for the whole journey. I watched him in the mirror as he gazed out at the world passing by. When we arrived, we popped his muzzle on as a precaution since he can sometimes be wary of strangers. Flash wandered around the shop, taking in all the sights and smells, until he discovered the pick-and-mix treats—which of course we had to get. After choosing his goodies, he rummaged through the plushies and picked out a squeaky monkey to take home.

As we headed toward the till, another dog suddenly rushed around a corner and startled Flash, causing him to react. I managed to whisk him away with a distraction, but he became very on edge and tucked himself into me for comfort. A lovely lady then came around the opposite corner and, despite having seen his reaction, kindly stopped to say hello. She happened to be a previous Many Tears adopter, and her own pup is doing wonderfully. She chose to ignore Flash at first to give him space, and once he settled, he allowed her to gently stroke his head. After wishing us well, we carried on with our day.

We sat outside Costa in the sunshine, and Flash absolutely loved his pupcup, so much so that he managed to get it all over his nose.

I’m incredibly proud of Flash today. It was his first outing since arriving in kennels, and I could really see how scared he can be underneath it all, and how much he relies on his human for reassurance. Flash needs someone devoted, patient, and willing to put time into training and working through his reactivity toward other dogs. He truly is a special boy.

Another bleak day at the rescue with the rain pouring down non-stop, but it meant I got to spend some more quality time with the dogsI’ve never been one for poodles but Flash really has stolen my heartToday I really did see his loving and caring side as we cuddled away from the downpour. He rolled around, brought me his toys and chews before receiving belly rubs and head scratches until he fell asleep

If you’ve been to the rescue I’m usually walking Flash around the reception area in order for him to build his relationship with humans and other dogs but it was nice to just have some one on one time with him today, once you’ve created a bond with this boy he is yours for life.Flash’s’ training is still continuing and has managed to learn ‘touch’ where he boops his nose to the designated hand and is in the midst of learning ‘place’.

In a home will still need some training in order for him to thrive.

Flash is still a little mouthy when he gets super excited but is doing much better to when he first arrived with us.

It's been almost 4 months since Flash arrived here and I feel he has been very much overlooked. Deep down he’s a big cuddle bug and thrives on attention.

I tried spending most of my time with him today as kennel life is very stressful for him. We visited the big yard multiple times, went for a stroll and even met 2 dogs on a walk and greeted them with such kindness. Might I say he walks beautifully alongside you!

We met some new people in the reception area, which can sometimes make Flash a little uneasy but he did fantastically and even accepted some treats. For this he is muzzle trained as he can be mouthy when he’s a little too excited!

The last task of the day was to be groomed. I never thought I would see this boy sit still for more than a few seconds, but he amazed me and hopped up onto the grooming table ready to be pampered! And he now looks so good! Flash really doesn’t mind being groomed which will be helpful for the future.

I absolutely adore this beautiful boy. Flash is best described as an oversized puppy at heart. He has a playful, goofy nature but sometimes forgets his size, which can make him a little overexcited and mouthy, especially if he’s unsure or feeling frustrated.

Flash can be a sensitive soul who is often scared of his own shadow and needs plenty of reassurance and gentle confidence-building when faced with new experiences (like the umbrella he discovered today!). Because of this, kennel life is very tough for him, and I truly believe he will thrive so much more in a loving home.

Once Flash trusts you, he shows his affectionate side. He adores snuggling in for a cuddle and loves being pampered.

Flash’s ideal home would be an adult-only household where he can be the only dog. He isn’t aggressive with other dogs but can become boisterous and overwhelming. A quiet location with a secure, good-sized garden would be perfect, ideally with adopters who enjoy long walks and hikes.

He walks beautifully on the lead, enjoys all weathers, and has the stamina to go for hours. While he may sometimes react to new situations or get excitable around other dogs, his confidence and manners are improving every day. Flash will need adopters who are home most of the time or able to include him in their daily lives, as he finds being left alone difficult and may struggle with separation anxiety.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle who has come to us from a home as his owners no longer had time for him and couldn't offer him the exercise he requires. Although he has lived in a home before, Flash is a worried boy who finds new experiences and people quite daunting. Because of this, Flash is looking for an experienced, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time, patience, and love to give. He needs adopters who won’t give up on him and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace.Initially, Flash can be wary of new people and unsure of their intentions, but once you’ve gained his trust, he begins to show his affectionate and loyal nature. He forms strong bonds with those he feels safe around and shows a deep need for companionship. He does not cope well with being left alone and has shown signs of separation anxiety, getting very worried and anxious when left on his own. He will need an adopter who is able to be with him all of the time and who will work on this with him, slowly building up any time he is left. We are told he was crate trained in his previous home, which may help with this process.Flash is particularly sensitive to loud or sudden noises, which can cause him to panic. He feels safest in quiet, familiar surroundings and finds walks outside of the rescue grounds very difficult at the moment. When taken beyond his comfort zone, he becomes overwhelmed and spins in circles in an attempt to return to safety. While he can walk on a lead, his adopters will need to help him grow in confidence very gradually and may need to begin with simply enjoying time in the garden or short walks in peaceful areas.Flash would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as he can be grumbly when meeting other dogs. This is something his adopters will need to work on with him with patience and positive reinforcement. Because of this, he must only be allowed off lead in secure areas with no other dogs present. He also cannot live with cats or small animals and we are told he isn't a fan of pigeons or seagulls.Flash will be looking for a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and where his adopters will help him settle into a consistent routine so he can feel safe and secure. We are told that he is house trained but he may need some reminders of this in his new homeAlthough he is currently worried about going for walks, he is an active breed who will need to be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. We have been told that he has previously done some agility and scent work, so once his confidence grows this is something he may like to explore again in the future. His previous owners also said he enjoyed being groomed and bathed, though we haven’t yet introduced this at the rescue.This beautiful boy has so much potential in the right hands. If you have the time, experience, and understanding to give Flash the security and stability he needs, he will reward you with trust, loyalty, and love. Please don’t overlook him, he’s waiting for that one special person to believe in him.Flash has an entropion in both eyes, which has been repaired by our vets but does have some dermatitis around his eyes.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I could live with another calm dog, or be the only dog. I haven’t met cats

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, and doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She was a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail has made lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer, happier side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She will happily roll over for a tummy rub, which is a lovely sign of the trust she has developed, although she can still be a little unsure if she feels there is too much fuss or interaction. Her adopters will need to continue reading her body language and allow her to choose when she is ready for affection.

Gail is a happy little girl with plenty of character and a lovely playful side. She particularly enjoys carrying her favourite toys around, and these little glimpses of her personality are wonderful to see as her confidence continues to grow.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. We have also learnt a little more about Gail's feelings towards other dogs. Although she can find some dogs overwhelming, she has shown that she can cope well with a calm canine companion. She is currently sharing her kennel with a Cavalier and has even been spotted happily snuggled up in the same bed with her. This has been a lovely development and suggests that, with the right match, Gail may be able to live with another calm and respectful dog.

Gail's walking has also come on wonderfully. She is much more confident on her walks now, although she is most comfortable walking with the staff members she knows and trusts well. Her adopters will need to understand that she may need time to build the same confidence with them and should continue her training gently and at her own pace.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Her adopters should be prepared for this to be a gradual process and give her plenty of time to feel safe and secure.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who has already come such a long way. She is still learning to trust and can be unsure at times, but beneath her worries is a happy, funny little dog who loves her toys and enjoys the company of those she knows. With the right people, plenty of patience and a gentle approach, we believe Gail will continue to blossom into a wonderfully rewarding companion.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Nimbus
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Nimbus is a beautiful girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was very nervous and found everything quite overwhelming. Since then she has started to settle in and has come out of her shell more each day. Nimbus has now moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the first time.

While she is still nervous, she has settled into her foster home well. She really loves her food and will sleep all night quietly with the resident dog. She has been clean so far in the home, so is doing really well with her toilet training too. She has started learning all about walking on a lead and harness and now loves to go on walks, so we think she will really enjoy going on walks with her new family.

Nimbus will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and take her under their wing. It's clear how much she relies on her canine companions for reassurance.

It's clear that she hasn't been used to much socialisation or handling prior to arrival with us and she is still quite wary of people and isn't keen on being handled, but once in your arms she does begin to relax and settle.

As Nimbus had never lived in a home before moving to foster, her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to settle in and learn all about home life. With patience, kindness, and plenty of reassurance, she will slowly begin to flourish.

Nimbus has been given the Gift of Life by Scott Ferguson

Nimbus or Nell as she is known here in foster, is doing really well. She is house trained and sleeps all night with my dog. She loves her food and will take treats from my hand.

She loves her walks and is fine walking past traffic on quite busy roads, she also enjoys visiting pubs and cafes. Nimbus is fine with all the dogs she meets and is really loves my dog, so she will definitely need a kind confident dog to cuddle up too.

She will let me groom her and check her ears and we have started a little teeth clean, she loves the beef flavoured toothpaste. The only thing Nimbus is still uneasy about is being picked up, but once she settles in your arms she does relax and does enjoy a little cuddle.

Nimbus is a really sweet funny little girl and deserves a forever home where she will make someone a really lovely companion.

Nimbus or Nell as she is known here, has been in foster with us for a week.  Nell is a sweet timid little girl and needs time and patience to help her settle into home life.

She has been clean in the house since she arrived and will now sleep all night with my dog. She loves her food, and is walking on a lead and harness in quiet areas. She really is enjoying her walks and loves meeting other dogs.

She is still wary of people and is not keen on being handled, but once you do pick her up she will settle.

She does rely on my dog and follows him everywhere, so she will need another dog or dogs in her new home, which would need to be a quiet, adult only home.

It will take Nell time to build her confidence, she has done really well so far so hopefully she will find her forever home.

With the recent heatwave, Nimbus has had a much needed and well overdue groom and I think we can all agree she looks absolutely beautiful!

She definitely appreciated being cooler in the hot weather, and it’s allowed her to enjoy the lovely weather the last couple of weeks (within reason of course!!)

Nimbus has been slowly finding her feet here at the rescue, and taking her time with opening up to us. She was incredibly frightened when she first arrived, but with time and patience from her kennel mums and dads, her true personality is slowly coming to the surface.

We find that a lot of our ex-breeders struggle more in the presence of men, but Nimbus is opening up to her kennel dad too. They’re not at the cuddling stage as of yet, but she happily comes up to him and gives him hand kisses so we think with routine, TLC and quality time spent together they’ll get there in no time!

Nimbus is a nervous, flighty little girl who has come to us from a breeder and finds the world quite overwhelming. She is touch-sensitive and clearly hasn’t been used to much handling, so she will need kind, patient adopters who can gently show her that human hands can be kind and reassuring. Despite her worries, once she is in your arms she does begin to relax and settle.

Nimbus relies heavily on the comfort and reassurance of her kennel friends, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide and support her as she learns about life in a home and continues to build her confidence. When she feels unsure, she will often retreat to her bed or a quiet corner where she feels safe.

As Nimbus has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be patient, gentle, and understanding while she learns all about home life and house training. Walking on a lead may feel overwhelming for her at first, so starting with gentle garden sniffs and allowing her to explore at her own pace will help her gain confidence.

Nimbus is looking for a calm and understanding home with adopters who understand the needs of ex-breeding dogs and are willing to give her the time and space she needs to come out of her shell. With patience, kindness, and plenty of reassurance, we are hopeful she will slowly begin to flourish.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, but I have lived with another dog. See more below.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Quiver, Trevor, Clever Trevor, Trev, Piggy, Pig, Squirrel, Egg Nog Dog

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable her wonderful personality starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly lovely girl with a fun, quirky nature and a very affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once she trusts you she is incredibly rewarding to spend time with. She loves being around people she knows and has a gentle, sweet temperament that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels and enjoyed play dates with a variety of canine companions. She is respectful around toys and eats well alongside other dogs, making her an easy companion to have around.

She is now walking on a harness and has made lovely progress, although some things can still make her nervous when out and about. Her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her to feel safe and encouraging her when she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit.
