She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Pop
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who love cuddles, and are active!

I will need to be the only pet in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I would like a secure garden where I can have plenty of play time!

I am very active and will need a home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I may have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

30-07-26 Pop is a fantastic little lady who has come to us from a breeder, although we have been told she has lived in a home previously. She knows her name and responds to "Pop", so her new family will need to keep this name.

Pop is a wonderful little girl who is full of love, character and energy. She can be a little timid when first meeting new people, but it doesn't take her long to warm up. Once she knows you, she absolutely loves cuddles, enjoys giving kisses and thrives on human company. She has a very affectionate, sweet nature and loves being involved in whatever her people are doing.

As an active Jack Russell Terrier x Collie, Pop is looking for a home that can provide plenty of physical exercise as well as mental enrichment to keep her clever little brain busy. She is doing well with her lead walking and enjoys getting out and about, but she will need owners who are committed to continuing her training and helping her build confidence.

Pop will need to be the only dog in her new home. Whilst she can walk past some dogs, she is worried by them and can become reactive on lead, making the wrong choices when she feels overwhelmed. Her adopters will need to be experienced, understanding and willing to continue working on her doggy social skills using positive, reward-based training. We have already started muzzle training with Pop to help build her confidence, with the hope that, in time, she may be able to enjoy controlled walks alongside calm canine companions.

As Pop has previously lived in a home, we think she is likely to know many of the basics, although she may need a few reminders as she settles into a new routine.

She could live with sensible, dog-savvy children aged 13 years and over but will need a home without cats.

Pop is a truly wonderful little dog with so much love to give. With patient, experienced adopters who can provide the active lifestyle and ongoing training she needs, she will make a fantastic, loyal and loving companion.

name: Gary
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home with 4ft boundaries.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am missing my left eye, and I have been castrated & have had 1 tooth removed.

Gary is a very sweet and sensitive boy who has come to us from a breeder. He has now moved into foster and, despite his worries around people, has taken to home life like a duck to water. Everything is exciting to him, and he approaches the world with curiosity, happily exploring every room and taking new sights and sounds in his stride. Household noises don't seem to faze him at all.

Gary has also discovered his playful side and has very much switched into "puppy mode". He is as cute as a button and is always looking for his next adventure. If you turn your back for a few minutes, there's a good chance he'll have found something interesting to carry around! Thankfully, he is happy for his foster carer to gently take items away from him. He enjoys his food and treats, loves playing with toys, appreciates the freedom of the garden, and has quickly decided that sleeping on the family bed is the perfect place to spend the night.

Gary takes enormous comfort from the company of other dogs and is very dependent on his resident canine companions. He has formed a particularly lovely bond with the older male Dachshund in his foster home and is wonderfully determined to persuade him to join in with a game. Because of this, Gary will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his forever home to help guide him, reassure him, and continue building his confidence.

Although Gary has settled brilliantly into home life, he remains extremely frightened of human touch and handling. If he feels pressured or overwhelmed, he may react defensively out of fear. His adopters will need to understand that there will be no quick fix for this. Instead, they must be committed to earning his trust, respecting his boundaries, and allowing him to build confidence at his own pace through gentle, positive experiences. He is already showing what an intelligent and resilient little dog he is, and every small step forward is a huge achievement.

As he is now in a home, he will begin to learn all about house training and lead walking when he is ready, lead walking. A secure garden will be essential, giving him a safe space to explore while he continues to gain confidence.

Due to his sensitive nature, Gary is looking for a calm, adult-only home with experience of ex-breeding dogs, where he can settle without pressure and be accepted for who he is. Gary has come to us missing his left eye, but this doesn't slow him down in the slightest—if anything, it adds to his unique and endearing charm.

Gary is a truly special little boy. He has already shown just how well he can adapt to family life when given patience and understanding. With adopters who are willing to invest the time to earn his trust, we have no doubt that he will grow into an incredibly loyal and rewarding companion and become a wonderful ambassador for his breed.

At the time of his castration, Gary had one tooth removed.

Gary has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Little Gary arrived in foster and has taken to home life like a duck to water. Everything is exciting and is to be explored and conquered, with no household item or sound yet phasing him.

He has turned on his puppy mode, cute as a button but if you turn your back for 5 minutes, he is off with something new in his mouth, but is happy for you to take this away.

He enjoys his food and treats, loves his toys, and very much appreciates the freedom of the garden and the security of sleeping on the family bed at night.

He is very dependent on my resident dogs and has taken a real shine to our older much bigger male dachsie showing great determination in persuading him to play.

Gary does however remain extremely scared of human touch/handling and if you push this, he may act out defensively in fear. There will be no quick fix. Instead this will be a journey of earning his trust, respecting his boundaries and slowly desensitising him to these fears. However this little boy is going to be so worth the investment and in time, will be a credit to the dachsie breed.

Garry is just the funniest little dude, and works hard ever day to become braver with us humans. Thanks to the kindness and perseverance of staff at the rescue Garry slowly grows more confident with us.

Garry has been deeply affected by his rough start in life and arrived terrified of everyone, hating being touched or just being near us. But day by day Garry gets braver and will now allow a little scratch under his chin or take a treat (he loves his food). It’s hard not to fall for Garry there is just something about him and within a patient loving home I believe the true Garry will shine through.

When you seem him playing with his friends in the yard he’s just adorable and happy. Garrys ideal home would be experienced with nervous rescues, have a resident dog and no children, or visiting children.

Gary is a very sweet boy once he gets to know you, although this can take a few meetings. He is very shy and timid in his kennel but will put on a brave front when you're outside it.

Gary is currently undergoing muzzle training as he can be tricky when handled. He is doing really well and is now able to tolerate gentle touches under his chin during his training sessions. Thankfully, Gary is a big foodie, which makes muzzle training much more engaging and rewarding for him.

I’ve been at the rescue for a little while now, and I’ve started to make some two-legged friends. I love the food they give me, especially the squeezy paste in a tube, and I’ll go right up to them now for that tasty treat. Sometimes, when they’re not looking, I’ll creep up behind them and check to see if there’s any in their pockets (but they don’t know I do this, so don’t tell them!).

I prefer it when the two-legged ones move slowly and quietly. It’s very unsettling for me if they rush about, and I’ll find a corner to curl up in and make myself feel safe when they do. On the whole though, they’re okay, and I love it when they let me go out into the big yards. I may be quite tiny, but that doesn’t stop me roaming around for all the good sniffs, and I don’t mind if they sit and chat with me while I go about my business.

Yesterday, one of the two-legged ones sat in the kennel with me. I curled up in my bed and watched them, and I even let them give me a little scratch. I think I would quite like some of these two-legged friends of my own, as long as they’re quiet and gentle (none of the small, bouncy ones!). A cosy bed of my own does sound rather nice, and of course I’ll need a four-legged friend as well.

Perhaps I’ll find some lovely two-legged friends soon… let me know if you hear of any.

Gary is a very sweet and sensitive boy who has come to us from a breeder. He currently finds human interaction quite overwhelming and can be touch-sensitive, so he needs time and patience to build trust. He is very much on the worried side and can react by snapping if he becomes frightened when being picked up, so it’s important that his adopters take a gentle, hands-off approach and allow him to come to them in his own time.

Although he is still nervous, Gary is beginning to take treats from people he knows well and has spent time with, which is a lovely sign of progress and shows his potential to build trusting relationships.

Gary takes great comfort from his kennel friends and has always lived alongside other dogs, so he will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, reassure him, and show him the ropes as he settles in.

As Gary has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be understanding while he learns about house training and walking on a lead. He is not yet used to lead walking, so a secure garden will be essential, giving him a safe space to explore and build confidence at his own pace.

Due to his sensitive nature, Gary is looking for a calm adult-only home with ex-breeding experience, where he can settle in at his own pace without pressure. He will need plenty of time, love, and reassurance, but with patience and consistency, he will continue to make progress and grow in confidence.

Gary has come to us missing his left eye, but this doesn’t slow him down at all, if anything, it adds to his unique and endearing charm.

Gary is a little superstar who is trying his best in a world he finds quite overwhelming. With the right support, he will continue to blossom and form a deep, loyal bond with his future family.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Holiday
description:
I need a quiet adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I’m frightened and will need a secure garden to learn about being outside.

I am too scared to go out for walks right now and will need a careful introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her as the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she came back into our care. Holiday has since moved to a foster home where she is settling beautifully and continuing to learn all about life in a home.

Holiday is a very sensitive girl who had very little socialisation before coming into our care. When she first returned to us, she found people incredibly worrying and was very hand-shy. Her first instinct was always to run away, and she wasn't comfortable being picked up or handled. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could react by nipping out of fear, and she did nip her previous adopter once when she became overwhelmed during handling.

Holiday will still be looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with no visiting children. She will need adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, without pressure or expectations. She relies heavily on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her.

Since moving into foster care, Holiday has made some really lovely progress and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle nearby while her foster family relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where everyone is, often coming to find them and quietly checking in throughout the day.

She is now happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also greets us with a wagging tail and will happily sit and listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as anyone spoke to her, so this has been a huge milestone.

Although Holiday is becoming much more confident, she still isn't ready to be handled much and is not yet comfortable wearing a harness or going for walks. Her adopter will need to be happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace, allowing her to decide when she is ready for each new step.

Minus her brief adoption, Holiday had never lived in a home before, but she has settled brilliantly into foster care. She is now 99% clean in the house and has established a lovely routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs, taking great comfort from them and often following their lead. She enjoys spending time in the garden and small secure field, where she loves exploring, relaxing and watching the world go by. She has also been left at home with the other dogs for a few hours and has coped very well.

Holiday is a very special little girl who has already come such a long way. She is learning that people can be kind and that home life isn't so scary after all. She still has a journey ahead of her, but with plenty of patience, understanding and the support of another dog, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything her new life has to offer.

Holiday has been given the Gift of Life by Ellie Worron

Holiday has made some lovely progress since coming into foster care and is growing in confidence every week. She now happily comes into the sitting room and chooses to settle close by while we relax. She enjoys being part of family life and likes to know where we are, often coming to find us and checking in throughout the day.

She is happily taking treats from our hands and has recently started giving gentle little nose bumps to our hands, which is a wonderful sign that her trust is growing. She also wags her tail when she sees us and will happily listen while we talk to her, maintaining eye contact. When she first arrived, she would run away as soon as we spoke to her, so this is a huge milestone for her.

Holiday is now 99% clean in the house and has settled brilliantly into a routine. She absolutely adores the other dogs and takes great comfort from them, often following their lead. She loves spending time in the garden and our small field, where she enjoys exploring and relaxing.

At the moment, Holiday is not yet ready to wear a harness or go for walks, and she will need an adopter who is happy to continue building her confidence at her own pace. She is making steady progress and, with patience and kindness, continues to blossom.

Holiday is a very gentle, sweet little girl with the softest, kindest eyes. She has such a lovely nature, and it is a privilege to watch her confidence grow a little more each day.

Holiday has settled well into foster care. She is worried about being handled at the moment so we haven’t tried to stroke her or pick her up, we wanted to give her the chance to settle and feel safe first.

She will take treats from our hands, walk through doorways easily, even with us there, and she seeks us out if she doesn’t know where we are. This all indicates that it won’t be long until we can begin gentles strokes etc. When we are fussing our dogs she gets closer to watch and has touched my hand or sniffed my legs. Holiday is not as jumpy as I thought she would be, which is great, and we can walk quite close to her without her moving away.

When we are all settled in the evening, she comes into the sitting room to see where we all are and what we are doing. She isn’t phased by the TV and will often sit on a rug next to my chair.

We have a very small field which most new fosters are a bit scared of as they are not used to big spaces, Holiday loves spending time out there exploring and watching the other dogs play, we’ve even seen her do the odd little sprint!

She has been clean in the house and loves snuggling with the dogs at night in the kitchen, she is left overnight and we can go out for a couple of hours and she is fine as long as the dogs are with her too.

She has the potential to be the best dog and I don’t think it will be long before she is seeking attention and ready to try her harness again. She has very gentle eyes and you can see the sadness ebbing away a little more each day.

This week Holiday has been making lovely progress with lead work. We have been helping her get used to having a lead clipped onto her harness and trailing behind her, and she is becoming much more comfortable with this. Clipping the lead onto her harness is now far less of a concern for her, which is a big step forward, and when she is out in the yard she barely seems aware of it anymore.

She is also doing wonderfully with different people putting her harness on, which is a very significant achievement for Holiday given how sensitive she has been around handling. She is taking these steps in her stride and continues to make really encouraging progress.

Recently, I’ve been spending some dedicated time working with Holiday, and she’s making such lovely progress. She’s beginning to trust me more each day and has even allowed me to gently put a harness on her. Everything is done slowly and at her pace, with plenty of treats and reassurance, but this is a huge milestone for this sensitive girl.

We’ve also been working on gentle touch, always on her terms. When she chooses to come and sit beside me in her bed, we take things one small step at a time, building her confidence with each positive experience (and a few tasty rewards along the way!).

Holiday is starting to show more of her personality now. She’s often one of the first up for a treat and has even begun wagging her tail. It might sound like a small thing, but for Holiday, it’s truly something special.

She’s a wonderful dog who just needs a patient, understanding home where she can continue to grow in confidence and feel safe. Watching her come out of her shell is incredibly rewarding, and she’s so ready for someone to give her the love she deserves.

I am writing this update as someone who has not had much interaction with Holiday although I have worked with her on a few occasions. It is obvious from her previous update that there has been progress in her coming out of her shell and I was surprised to discover that Holiday would accept treats from my hand although when trying to smooth her coat, Holiday swiftly moved out of reach.

She is getting there but slowy and anyone wanting to adopt her will need to go slowly and earn that important trust. Holiday's regular carer can stroke Holiday when she is settled in a bed but only in one place. If a position is changed, Holiday will become scared and move.

It is apparent after speaking with Holiday's regular carer that for Holiday to make that important next step in her progress, it would be better for her to be in a home situation. Holiday is fantastic with other dogs and would definitely need to live with at least one other dog to give her that hope of progress and comfort. There is always someone out there for every dog and vice versa Holiday is waiting.

Holiday originally came to us from a breeder a few months ago. She was adopted and found a lovely home, but sadly it wasn't the right match for her and the resident dog wouldn't accept her, so she is now back in our care.

Holiday is a very scared girl who is very overwhelmed to find herself here and clearly hasn't had much socialisation before. She finds human interaction quite difficult at the moment and is very hand-shy, so she will need a patient and understanding home that can help her come out of her shell at her own pace. Holiday will run away from you when you enter her kennel and isn't keen on being picked up or handled. She finds this so scary, that if she feels like she is being pushed out of her comfort zone she can choose nip or bite, purely through fear. She did bite her previous adopter once when she was being handled as she became so worried.

For this reason, Holiday will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where there are no visiting children. She will need adopters who hav experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will let her settle in slowly at her own pace with no pressure or expectations.

Holiday finds comfort and reassurance from the company of her canine friends and so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing. This dog will need to allow her to snuggle up to them and will need to be happy for her to follow them around. A kind resident dog will be an important source of reassurance and companionship for her as she adjusts to her new life.

Although she spent some time in foster and was adopted for a short period, she had never lived in a home before this, so Holiday will still need to learn all about home life and new skills like house training. She will also need to learn to walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice wearing these around the home and garden, once her confidence with handling has grown a little more. She will then need to practice walking around the garden until she is confident enough to venture further.

Since arriving back with us, Holiday has started to make some more progress and will now take a treat from our hands as long as she has a doggy friend next to her for support. With time, love and patience she will start to leave her past behind her and will truly start to blossom. Holiday's journey won't be a short one, but it will be so worth it when you see her tail wag for the first time or when she first willingly accepts some fuss and attention. In the right home, she will thrive, so please don't keep her waiting too long.

name: Lollipop
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a grade 2 luxating patella and have had 7 teeth extracted. Read below for more

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment and relies heavily on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles into family life and finds her paws.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.

Lollipop has been given the Gift of Life by Jodie Stanley

name: Swanny
description:
I could live with dog savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with a larger male dog. I cannot live with cats.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I do my best to keep my kennel clean, but may need help in a home!

Swanny is a truly lovely little lady who has come to us from a breeder and has been quietly stealing hearts ever since. With her unmistakable Beagle nose, Swanny loves to explore her surroundings and see what’s going on around her. While she can still have a slightly shy side, her confidence has blossomed beautifully during her time with us, and her sweet, gentle nature really shines through. She has become very people orientated and now absolutely loves some fuss and attention!

Over the past few weeks, Swanny has made wonderful progress. She is now walking beautifully on the lead and thoroughly enjoys heading out for walks or having a run around our big yard, where she shows her playful and inquisitive side. She also does her best to keep her kennel clean during the day, which suggests that house training in a home environment should be very straightforward with a little routine and patience.

Swanny has made friends with some larger male dogs here at the rescue and loves to go on play dates in our play yard with them. She can be quite picky with which male dogs she likes and can also be too enthusiastic and doesn't always read other dogs' signals, so she would only be suited to living with a calm, larger male dog who is very tolerant of her. Slow, sensible introductions would be essential. Thanks to her growing confidence, we now feel that Swanny could also live as an only dog in the right, understanding home where she can continue to thrive at her own pace or she can live with a larger, calm male dog. She cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Swanny has never lived in a home before, she will need kind and patient adopters who can help her learn the routines of family life. She could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in. With gentle guidance, consistency, and love, she is sure to settle quickly and become a devoted and affectionate companion. An active family who enjoy getting out and about would be ideal, as Swanny loves having both her mind and body kept busy.

Swanny has cataracts in both eyes, which do not appear to bother her at all. She has had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay, along with two teeth extractions. She also has one fractured pre-molar, which our vets have advised leaving for now, though it may need monitoring in the future. Swanny also has a travel document in place.

Swanny is an absolute delight to care for here at the rescue, and we truly believe that whoever opens their heart and home to her will be gaining a very special little dog who has so much love to give.

Swanny is the perfect dog, suitable to be an only dog. She would thrive in a home with owners who love cuddles and walking. She's the right balance of cuddly and active and an absolute pleasure to work with! She's been enjoying her enrichment toys with her treats and adores anyone who she comes in contact with!

She's honestly perfect and I can't understand how she hasn't found a beagle loving home yet!

Over the last couple of months, we’ve introduced Swanny to many larger male dogs at the rescue in attempt to find her an ideal playmate. Swanny is an absolutely comical girl, and no matter the size of the male dog, she will not hold back!!

Swanny’s main buddy is our Standard Poodle Flash, and every single day they have play dates. She is incredibly tolerant with his exuberant and playful nature, but also gives it as good as she gets. They have such a good balance between them, and once Swanny has had enough she will just take herself away from playing and have a good sniff around our big play yard, or steal some fusses off the first human in sight!

She has also had a play date with Charlie (a Great Dane X Mastiff) and his size did not phase her one bit, he was probably 3-4x bigger than her, but Swanny’s playfulness definitely trumped his size!!!

Swanny is not only an absolute delight to look after, but just being in her presence would make your entire day. She is as sweet as anything, she is kind, gentle, and loving. She is not built for kennels, she is build for sofa snuggles, big adventures, and endless love.

How Swanny has not been adopted yet is a mystery to me .

Perhaps it's her demeanor when meeting new people? Swanny can be a little shy at first but soon makes a connection and there's nothing wrong with being cautious.

Swanny walks beautifully on a lead and loves to sniff and smell the grass.

As Swanny does have enough confidence, she can live as the only dog in the house or equally she would be happy living with a larger male dog.

I would say, to see the true Swanny, you need to meet her, walk her and give her a little time to show affection. It really is rewarding when it happens.

Beagles are really pretty dogs and Swanny is no exception, so if you would like a beautiful beagle in your life, Swanny is ready to be the one.

Swanny is the sweetest angel, and it truly is a privilege to care for her five days a week. She has the most gentle and loving nature.

Swanny can be a little nervous when meeting new people, which is completely understandable, but with a bit of patience and kindness, she soon begins to show her true self.

Once you’ve built that special bond with Swanny, she becomes the most loyal companion you could ever ask for. She loves to  be close to you and will happily follow you around like you’re shadow!

Like a true beagle, Swanny absolutely loves her walks. The moment she’s outside, her nose is straight to the ground, exploring every scent along her way. Watching her take in the world through her nose is such a lovely reminder of how much joy the simple things can bring.

Swanny really is the most perfect dog in her own unique way. With the right family who can give her patience, reassurance, and lots of love, she will truly flourish.

She has so much to offer and would make the most wonderful addition to a caring and understanding home.

Swanny is such a sweet girl who is blossoming in confidence every single day!

Swanny has made so much progress over the last few weeks, I now believe she can be an only dog in the right circumstances.

Swanny does get on with larger male dogs absolutely fine, but prefers dogs who aren’t in the her face and give her the space she needs.

During her time here so far swanny has had a few disagreements with the male dogs she has shared kennels with when they get to much in her space.

Swanny is now walking beautifully on lead, and enjoys spending time going out for walks, or running freely down our big yard!

Swanny also tries to keep her kennel clean during the days, so house training should be a breeze!

Swanny is honestly a delight to look after here at the rescue, whoever welcomes her into their family are going to be very lucky people!

Swanny is a fabulous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She’s an inquisitive girl with the unmistakable nose of a Beagle, always eager to explore and see what’s going on around her. Swanny can be confident when she chooses, but she still has a shy side, and with the gentle encouragement of her kennel friends, she’s starting to show her sweet, sociable nature.

She will need a confident, larger male resident dog in her new home to help her settle, guide her, and teach her about life in a home. Once she’s comfortable, Swanny would absolutely love an active family who can take her on plenty of adventures and keep her mind and body engaged.

Swanny is an absolute gem and, as she has never lived in a home before, will need patient adopters to help her learn house training, walking on a lead, and all the routines of home life. With kindness, consistency, and love, we believe she will settle quickly and become a devoted, loving companion.

Swanny has come to us with cataracts in both eyes, that does not seem to bother her. She has had an umbilical hernia repaired at the time of her spay as well as 2 teeth extracted. She also has one fractured pre-molar which our vets have advised to leave, but this may need to be looked at in the future.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Arctic
description:
Arctic is not ready for adoption at this time. Keep checking back for updates.

I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a multi dog household and I am fine with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am starting to really enjoy going for walks on a lead and harness!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

Please meet Arctic! She is a very special girl looking for a very special home with patient, experienced adopters who will never give up on her and who will love her for exactly who she is.

Arctic first came to us from a breeder in 2025. When she arrived, she was an extremely frightened and shut-down girl who found people and handling very overwhelming. Since then, life has been a bit of a rollercoaster for this special girl. She was adopted twice but has sadly found herself back in our care both times. Her first adoption sadly wasn't the right match due to her level of fear, as she could nip if pushed beyond her comfort zone. Her second return came after she accidentally escaped through the front door. In the panic of the situation, she bit her adopter when they tried to catch her, and it was decided that returning her to us was the best option.

Arctic is now settling into foster care, where she has already started to show us more of her wonderful personality. She found the first couple of days quite stressful and spent a lot of time pacing while she explored her new surroundings, but she has settled well and is becoming much more relaxed. She is a very curious girl who likes to know what is going on and will happily follow her foster family from room to room to see what they are doing.

She has been mostly clean during the day, although she has had the occasional overnight accident as she adjusts to her new routine. Arctic sleeps quietly overnight in her crate and is always pleased to see her foster carer in the morning, eagerly waiting for her breakfast.

Arctic is still a very anxious girl and remains particularly worried about being touched or handled. However, she is already making gentle progress. She is slowly learning to trust her foster carer, who is able to carefully pick her up and gently groom her, during which she will accept handling and strokes and actually seems to secretly enjoy it. She has even started choosing to sit on the sofa alongside her foster carer and the other dogs, although she is not yet comfortable with being touched whilst relaxing. Everything is very much on Arctic's terms, and she is showing that, with patience, she is capable of building trusting relationships.

She will need a very special, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs. If she feels pushed beyond her comfort zone, she can make the wrong decisions purely out of fear, so her new family will need to be patient, understanding and committed to helping her continue building her confidence over the long term. She may never be a lap dog, but she is a lovely girl who will show her affection in her own quiet ways, and watching her grow in confidence will be incredibly rewarding.

Arctic had never experienced life in a home before her adoption. Although she spent around six months in her most recent home and is now continuing to learn in foster care, she will still need adopters who understand that she may need a refresher with house training and time to adjust to a new routine.

She has learned all about walking on a lead and harness and now LOVES to go out for walks! She doesn't enjoy having her harness put on, but does allow it awkwardly. She loves meeting new dogs on walks but is wary of meeting people.

One thing Arctic has always loved is the company of other dogs. They are her greatest source of comfort and reassurance, and we feel she would thrive in a home with multiple confident resident dogs, as she relies on canine company so much. She has impeccable doggy manners and gets on brilliantly with all of the dogs in her foster home. She is also happily living alongside a cat in foster care and takes no notice of them.

Arctic is looking for a home that will love her for exactly who she is, rather than who they hope she might become. She is already showing that she enjoys the comforts of home, from curling up on a soft bed to relaxing on the sofa with her canine friends. With experienced adopters, patient guidance and confident canine companions by her side, we truly believe Arctic will continue to blossom and enjoy the happy, secure future she so deserves.

When Arctic originally came to us, she had some fur loss, but this has grown back wonderfully. She also had an enlarged mammary gland, but our vets are not concerned about this at present, although it may require monitoring by her adopters and their own vet. She is currently receiving treatment for some small patches of chronic dermatitis on her lower lip.

Arctic has been given the Gift of Life by Laura Woods

Arctic is really starting to make good progress in foster. She is now lead walking and LOVES to go out. She doesn’t like having her harness put on but allows it awkwardly! Arctic loves meeting new dogs on walks, but is wary of people.

She is slowly getting used to being handled, and I’m able to brush and comb her - I think she secretly quite enjoys it. She is becoming less touch sensitive but will still shy away and often flinches, but this is becoming less frequent. I no longer need a blanket to pick her up. Sometimes when I’m fussing her, she forgets she is scared and relaxes, her eyes start to close which is so sweet.

This fluffballs cheeky personality is starting to emerge, and she will dance around and woof at meal times, she doesn’t like eating from a bowl but will eat off of a clean cloth.

Arctic gets on great with all of the dogs and is often found cuddled up with my other foster dog. She fully relies on other dogs to feel safe - the more the merrier in Arctic’s eyes!

In three weeks, she has come such a long way, she is still a work in progress but wow! I’m so proud of her.

Arctic has been in foster care just over a week. She was very stressed for the first couple of days and did a lot of pacing. She thoroughly explored her new environment and has settled down.

From the start she has been curious about anything going on in the house, and follows us to whatever room we are in. She has been mostly clean during the day, but has the odd accident overnight.

Arctic sleeps quietly overnight in her crate. She seems happy to see me in the morning and eagerly awaits her breakfast! She gets on great with all of the other dogs and ignores the cat. She relies on the dogs and has impeccable doggy manners.

At the moment Arctic is very touch avoidant. Slowly I am making headway with this and am able to pick her up in a blanket and then gently comb her. She will allow me to stroke and handle her during this time. I am gaining her trust and she will sit on the sofa with me and the other dogs, but if I touch her she gets off. It’s still early days.

When the current heatwave ends I will work on the harness training started at the rescue. I think given time and patience Arctic will learn that human touch is a good thing, she already enjoys the comforts of a soft bed and a sofa!

Today little Arctic had what may have been her first professional spa day! She was in desperate need of a good scrub and a blast out of all her undercoat.

Arctic has come a long way since I first met her and although she's still quite nervous to be picked up once she's in your arms she settles quite quickly. She blew me away with how well she took to her bath, and especially the dryer as she needed to have her coat blown out and it didn't seem to phase her one bit. Although she may not admit it I think she enjoyed some parts.

After having a good brush and comb, and being an angel as I trimmed her nails, she let me carry her back home for her dinner but before eating she took herself for a waltz as I'm sure she felt much fresher.

Arctic is such a lovely soul behind her fear and with the right love and patience I think she would blossom beautifully into the little madam I know she can be.

Arctic has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. At the moment, she’s very frightened and she will retreat to the back of her kennel and shake like a leaf when approached.Arctic is looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her settle in and show her that life can be safe and full of love.She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her and her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life and begins to pick up new skills like house training. She will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and will need to practice first around the home and garden as she gains confidence.With time, love, and gentle reassurance, we believe she can blossom into a loving companion. If you have a peaceful home and a heart big enough to help her on her journey, Arctic could be the one who needs you most.Arctic has an enlarged mammary gland which our vets are not concerned about, and she has some fur loss which we hope will begin to improve and grow back after her spay.

name: Cloud
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I don't mind cats!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, and would like to continue this in my new home!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Cloud is a lovely little lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. Since arriving with us, she has come on in leaps and bounds and has blossomed into a wonderfully affectionate little girl. She has recently moved into a wonderful foster home where she is settling in beautifully and experiencing home life for the first time.

Cloud has the sweetest nature and is incredibly loving with the people she knows and trusts. Once you've built a bond with her, you'll have a friend for life. She adores cuddles and, if she had her way, she'd spend the whole day curled up on your lap. She is forever pawing at her favourite people, asking to be picked up, as being carried is one of her favourite things. She is a proper little lap dog who simply loves being close to the people she feels safe with.

Although Cloud has grown hugely in confidence, she can still find strangers and unfamiliar situations a little worrying. When she sees new people out and about, she can panic, so she will need patient adopters who understand that trust takes time. Once she knows you, however, she is an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion.

Cloud gets on wonderfully with other dogs and will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home. Having another dog by her side gives her reassurance and helps her confidence continue to grow. She walks beautifully on her harness, especially when she has a canine friend to follow, and thoroughly enjoys getting out and about. She has also passed her cat test and could potentially live with a dog-savvy feline. While she can be a little unsure of larger dogs at first, she is always gentle and simply looks to her people and doggy friends for reassurance.

As Cloud has never lived in a home before moving to her foster home, she will need time to learn about house training and all the other routines that come with family life. She would suit a home where someone is around for most, if not all, of the day, as she absolutely loves human company and is happiest snuggled up on a lap or relaxing alongside her doggy friends.

Cloud would like a quiet home and could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 years and over who understand that she may need a little time to settle into her new surroundings.

Cloud is an absolute diamond with so much love to give. She has blossomed into a happy, affectionate little girl, and we know she is going to make the most wonderful companion for one very lucky family.

Cloud has now been in foster for a week and already this little girl just wants to love everyone and happily sits on your lap or beside you staring at you with her big eyes. Yes they do weep slightly but a gentle wipe with an eye pad and she’s fine. She’s been bathed by me and was so good and relaxed when I was drying her that she fell asleep on my lap!

Cloud eats her food nicely without gulping it down and is always keen to try any treats that are on offer. She has been wearing a harness indoors and with it being cooler next week I will be encouraging to try the lead and if I feel she’s ready we’ll attempt to walk outside. I’m sure she’ll love meeting all those new dogs on the block.

Cloud does need a resident, friendly dog to help her settle and I’m sure they will very quickly be best buddies.

So if you feel you could offer her that forever, loving, home that she so deserves then please don’t keep this gorgeous girl waiting any longer.

She adores being close to her people and loves nothing more than curling up beside them for a cuddle. She is an absolute diamond with so much love to give, and we know she is going to make a wonderful companion for one very lucky family.

Cloud is a lovely little lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. Cloud has come on in leaps and bounds since arriving with us. She is now a lovely girl to handle and has built wonderful relationships with the people she knows and trusts. She absolutely loves a cuddle and will happily snuggle up beside her favourite people for plenty of affection. Although she can still be a little unsure in new situations, her confidence continues to grow every day.

Cloud gets on wonderfully with other dogs and enjoys spending time with different canine companions each day, which has really helped her confidence blossom. She is very well socialised and loves being out in the exercise yards with her doggy friends. She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can continue to guide and reassure her as she settles into family life.

As Cloud has never lived in a home before, she will still need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her time to adjust and help her learn at her own pace. She now walks beautifully on her harness and thoroughly enjoys getting out and about, and she would love to continue exploring the world with her forever family.

Cloud would like a quiet home and could share her home with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she may need a little time to settle into her new surroundings.

Cloud has truly blossomed into a happy, affectionate little girl. She adores being close to her people and loves nothing more than curling up beside them for a cuddle. She is an absolute diamond with so much love to give, and we know she is going to make a wonderful companion for one very lucky family.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jonah
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning about wearing a harness, but not going for walks yet.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am underweight and have some fur loss as well as sore skin.

Jonah is a very nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is in need of lots of kindness and TLC. When he first arrived with us, he was very overwhelmed and was extremely worried about being handled. He required gentle handling and a slow and gentle approach as if pushed out of his comfort zone he may have panicked and chosen to make the wrong decision purely out of fear. However, since then he has started to settle in so well and is becoming such a brave little boy. He will now come you greet you and see if you have any tasty treats for him and will even enjoy a gentle tickle once he gets to know you.

He will now happily greet his kennel mummy in the morning with a big waggy tail and offers her lots and lots of kisses and will even allow her to gently fuss him. The progress he's making is truly wonderful and it's allowing us to see glimpses of the real him and we think he will absolutely thrive in the right home. He loves toys and food which has been a big help in building a bond with him and earning his trust.

Jonah will be best suited to a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace without any expectations.

He absolutely loves his kennel friends and can often be found snuggled up in bed with them and clearly gets comfort and reassurance from their company. He also loves to play with his friends, which is just so lovely to see. It is essential that Jonah has at least one kind, confident resident dog in his new home. A canine companion will help him feel secure and give him someone to look to as he gains confidence and begins to embrace home life.

He has never lived in a home before so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he settles in to his new life and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. At the moment, he is so worried that learning to walk on a lead is likely to take time, and initially, spending time exploring a secure garden and building his confidence may be the best place to start. He has started learning all about wearing a harness to get used to the feel of this on his body and the next steps will be to introduce a lead.

Jonah is an incredibly sensitive soul who simply hasn't had the chance to experience the love and security every dog deserves. With patience, understanding, and a family willing to let him progress at his own pace, we believe he has every chance of learning to trust and becoming a wonderfully loyal companion.

Jonah has arrived to us extremely underweight, with some hair loss and what seems to be old cuts on his ears as well as some dermatitis, which is being treated. This boy needs plenty of TLC as he continues to grow.

Jonah has been given the Gift of Life by Sue Gibbs

Jonah has been with me for about 3 weeks now and I couldn’t be prouder of the progress he’s made since his arrival. He was so overwhelmed and shut down at first, and it was quite clear that life hadn’t been very kind to him. Despite this, he’s managed to open his heart little by little, and now greets me with a big waggy tail every morning, gives me lots of kisses, AND has even been brave enough to start having gentle fusses. It’s truly given me a glimpse of the real him .. the dog he’s always wanted to be but has never been able to. I’m hopeful for his future, and I really do believe that he will absolutely thrive in the right home.

He can still be worried about being picked up, especially by people he doesn’t know, but I think that’s completely understandable. It may be a little while until he’s comfortable with it, so his future adopters will need to keep this in mind. I haven’t taken him out on a harness yet, but he has been wearing one through the days to get him used to something being on his body. I’m planning on gently introducing him to the outside world over the next couple of weeks!

Jonah absolutely loves his kennel girlfriends and I’ll often find him snuggled up in bed with them. He does also love to play with them, so it would be a dream come true to find him a sister or brother who will cuddle and play with him. He also LOVES toys, and food too, which has been very helpful in multiple ways. It’s helped me build a bond with him and earn his trust a little, but also helped him put on some much needed weight as he arrived so thin.

Jonah may not become a different dog overnight, or miraculously transform into a normal, confident boy, but he will try. As long as he is shown an abundance of love and kindness, he will try. So please, give him a chance to do that.

Jonah is a very nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is still finding his feet in his new surroundings. When he first arrived with us, he was very overwhelmed and was extremely worried about being handled. He required gentle handling and a slow and gentle approach as if pushed out of his comfort zone he may have panicked and chosen to make the wrong decision purely out of fear. However, over the last week he has started to settle in so well and is becoming such a brave little boy. He will now come you greet you and see if you have any tasty treats for him and will even enjoy a gentle tickle once he gets to know you.

He will be best suited to a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him to settle in at his own pace without any expectations. It is essential that Jonah has at least one kind, confident resident dog in his new home. A canine companion will help him feel secure and give him someone to look to as he gains confidence and begins to embrace home life.

He has never lived in a home before so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he settles in to his new life and learns all about home life and new skills like house training. At the moment, he is so worried that learning to walk on a lead is likely to take time, and initially, spending time exploring a secure garden and building his confidence may be the best place to start.

name: Fox
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I walk well on a lead and harness, but do need to build up confidence still.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Fox is a nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. Since arrival, Fox has really started to blossom and is showing us more of her lovely personality every day. She is a wonderfully smiley girl whose confidence continues to grow, and she will now happily approach people for a gentle chin scratch before settling nearby and relaxing in their company.

Fox has now moved into a wonderful foster home, where she is getting to experience home life for the first time and is settling in well.

Fox still takes a great deal of comfort from other dogs and relies on them for reassurance. During her time at the rescue, she has shared her kennel with several different dogs and has been an absolute angel with every one of them, regardless of their size or gender. She is a gentle and social girl who clearly finds confidence from having another dog by her side.

Fox will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she continues to settle in and find her paws. A canine companion will be an important part of helping Fox feel safe and continue building her confidence.

As Fox has never lived in a home before moving to foster, her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles in and learns all about home life and house training, though she has been clean in the house so far in foster. She walks well on a harness and is making great progress. She will need patient adopters who are happy to take things at her pace and allow her confidence to build gradually.

In the right home, Fox could share her space with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

Fox is a sensitive and gentle girl who is trying her best to be brave. She has already come such a long way, and with continued patience, support, and the companionship of another dog, she will continue to blossom into a happy and confident companion.

Fox has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Fox has now been in foster for a week and has settled in well. She is comfortable in the house and doesn’t mind household noises. She has always toileted in the garden from the outset.

It has been too hot to go for walks until today. She had to be carried into the van and although very much enjoyed the sniffs round the woods, was very frightened of any noise. When we got going she did begin to settle which I’m sure will improve as we go along.

She eats well although again a little nervous and comes and goes to the bowl a few times.

Fox will accept a gentle fuss under her chin but not on top of her head and will come to me when the others are having a fuss.

She will need a home with no chickens or birds as she is far too interested in them.

Fox is really blossoming during her time at the rescue. She’s a wonderfully smiley girl whose confidence grows a little more every day. She will now happily approach people for a gentle chin scratch and is content to lie down and relax nearby.Fox still takes a great deal of comfort from her canine companions and relies heavily on her kennel friends for reassurance. During her time at the rescue, she has shared her kennel with several different dogs and has been an absolute angel with every one of them, regardless of their size or gender.

Fox is a nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is currently too worried to ask for fuss, but her confidence is slowly beginning to grow. At the moment, she will only approach when she has the reassurance of hiding behind one of her kennel friends, showing just how much she relies on their support.

Fox gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies heavily on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Fox has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. She will need patient adopters who are happy to take things at her pace and allow her confidence to build gradually.

Fox is a sensitive and gentle girl who is trying her best to be brave. With time, patience, and the support of another dog, she will begin to feel safe and slowly blossom into a much more confident companion.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Nell
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness and can live with teenagers.

I would like a home with my best friend Jackson! I haven't met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in and need 6ft+ fences.

I am strong on the lead and can pull, but would love an active home.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

NELL WOULD LIKE A HOME WITH HER BEST FRIENDJACKSON

15-08-26 Nell is a very sweet girl who has come to us with her best friendJacksonafter their owner sadly passed away. Nell was originally adopted from us as a young puppy and has spent the last several years being loved and cherished in a home. She is now looking for another forever home where she can continue to be a much loved member of the family.

Nell and Jackson love each other very much and are very bonded, so we are looking for a special home where they can stay together. Nell is a lovely girl who adores people and happily greets everyone with a waggy tail. She enjoys lots of fuss and attention and will make a wonderful companion for someone looking for a friendly, affectionate dog.

Nell is a little overweight at the moment, but she absolutely loves going for walks, so regular exercise will be a great way to help her get back to a healthier weight. She can be quite strong on the lead and does pull, so her adopters will need to be confident and physically able to handle her.

Having previously lived in a home, Nell should be house trained, although she may need some gentle reminders while she settles into her new surroundings. We would consider homing Nell and Jackson with dog-savvy teenagers.

Nell and Jackson have already lost the person they loved, so it is incredibly important to us that they are able to face this next chapter together. They are looking for a loving home with someone who can give them both the time, care and security they deserve. A home with 6ft fencing is essential.

If you think you could offer Nell and Jackson their happy ever after together, please don't leave them waiting.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crush
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have bilateral nuclear sclerosis, and will be neutered before adoption!

13-08-26 Crush is a fairly nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. He can be very shy and tends to rely heavily on his kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so he will need time and patience as he settles into his new surroundings.

Crush will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that he can look to and lean on as he learns about home life and begins to build his confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be understanding as he learns all about house training and adjusts to a new routine.

Crush doesn't walk on a lead yet, and the outside world may feel a little overwhelming at first, so spending time exploring a secure garden and enjoying plenty of sniffing opportunities would be a great place for him to start.

He could live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he will need plenty of time and space to settle in and begin to trust. Crush is a lovely boy who simply needs plenty of TLC, patience, and kindness as he finds his paws in the world.

He has come to us with bilateral nuclear sclerosis that will need to be monitored in his new home, and does not seem to bother him at this time.

Crush has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Eve
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I'm fully vaccinated and will be spayed before adoption.

08-08-26 Eve is a nervous girl who has come into our care from a breeder.

She is a very scared little girl who is understandably finding the world quite overwhelming. Eve relies heavily on the comfort of her doggy friends and is currently very skittish. She is a flight risk, so her new family will need to take great care to ensure she always feels safe and secure while she settles into her new life.

Eve will need another kind, confident dog in the home to take her under their wing and be a much-needed support system to help guide her, build her confidence, and reassure her as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Eve has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding, allowing her to progress at her own pace without any pressure.

Eve is looking for a calm, adult-only home with confident adopters who understand that building trust will take time. A secure garden and a confident resident dog will be essential to help her adjust safely and gently to home life.

Eve is a gentle soul who has a long journey ahead of her, but every small step forward will be a huge achievement. With time, patience, and the support of a confident canine companion, we hope she will gradually discover that the world isn't such a scary place after all.

Eve has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.
