I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

18-05-26 Pandora has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a scared little girl who is worried to find herself here at the moment, but she is trying ever so hard to be brave. If approached slowly and gently, Pandora is happy to enjoy a little fuss and is beginning to show what a sweet girl she is.

Pandora is looking for a calm and quiet home and would benefit from adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and reassurance as she settles into her new life. She gains confidence from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help show her the way. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be new to Pandora and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training. She walks well on a harness but it is advised to  initially further practice around the safety of the garden to help build her confidence. She will need an extra secure fence of at least 6ft to ensure her safety.

Although Pandora is not yet walking on a lead, we feel she will be best suited to an active home where, once she has gained confidence and learned all about the world around her, she will be able to enjoy lots of adventures with her family. With time, patience and the support of her doggy friend, we are sure Pandora will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Our vets have noted that she has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which doesn't require any medication but will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet going forward. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her face, which our vets diagnosed as a salivary mucocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this and it has remained stable so far. However, it is likely to gradually refill over the coming weeks or months and would need to be drained again if this happens. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Pandora's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like to live with a female dog. No cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk on a lead and harness and love to explore quiet areas.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, and am doing so good!

I'm fully vaccinated and have been neutered.

Royal is a very special Chow Chow who has come to us from a breeder in search of his forever home. When he first arrived, he was extremely frightened of the world around him and was very wary of being touched or handled. Thanks to gentle care and patience, Royal has made incredible progress and is continuing to blossom in foster, where he is experiencing home life for the very first time.

Royal has exceeded all expectations with how well he has settled into foster. He has been an absolute superstar, sleeping soundly through the night, travelling well in the car, walking beautifully on lead and has even been completely clean in the house. Every day brings a new milestone, and it has been a joy to watch his confidence grow as he discovers all the comforts and pleasures of family life.

Although Royal is still nervous of people initially, he so desperately wants to trust and tries his hardest to be brave. He has begun asking his foster carers for gentle neck and bum scratches, happily takes treats from their hands, enjoys rummaging through the toy box, has found his little voice and now greets them with his wonderful wagging tail. He is such a sweet, gentle soul who simply needs time to work things out at his own pace.

Royal absolutely relies on the resident female dogs in foster for confidence and reassurance. He watches their every move, learning how to be part of a family, and loves playing alongside them. He will need to share his forever home with at least one kind, confident female dog who enjoys a good play and can continue to show him the way. He cannot live with cats.

As this is Royal's first experience of living in a home, he thrives on routine and will need patient, understanding adopters who will allow him to settle without pressure. He has made remarkable progress already, but he is still very nervous of the unknown and benefits from people who understand that he needs time to process new experiences. A calm, rural or quiet home would suit him best, as he is currently worried by traffic. He is looking for an adult-only home with breed experience and experience with very nervous rescue dogs would be highly beneficial.

Royal has recently had a bath and full groom at the rescue and was an absolute gentleman throughout. As a Chow Chow, his beautiful coat will require regular daily grooming. He is very tolerant of being brushed when it is introduced slowly, little and often, and this has become an important part of his routine.

Royal is an incredibly special boy who has embraced this new chapter in his life with quiet bravery. With patience, kindness and the continued support of confident canine companions, he will become a wonderfully loyal and loving companion. Watching him continue to discover the world and grow in confidence will be an incredibly rewarding journey, and he is sure to make his forever family smile every single day.

Wow! This darling boy has just exceeded all expectations with how well he’s settled into his very first home, in his first week. Not a single accident (unheard of for a boy), sleeps soundly over night out of a crate, happy to be left alone with the company of the resident dogs, walks well on a lead, travels well. A literal angel boy.

Royal is the sweetest soul, he doesn’t trust humans easily but he really wants to and tries so hard to be brave.

He relies heavily on our resident girl gang for confidence & reassurance, watching & copying them intently to learn what being a member of a family is all about.

After an initial overwhelming few days for him, every day now brings a new ‘first’ & burst of joy on our part! Asking for a neck / bum scratch, taking a treat from our hand, rummaging in the toy box, playing with the girls, finding his little voice & wagging his amazing tail when we talk to him. He is just loving this next step in life and is so ready to be someone’s special boy.

Royal currently needs an adult only home as has not yet been tested with children. He needs confident kind resident female dogs who like a good play. A rural / quiet location would be preferable as he’s currently quite scared of traffic.

He is still very nervous of the unknown, thrives on routine and needs to be guided and given time to work things out without any pressure so experience with very scared dogs would be helpful.

As a Chow, his beautiful coat will need grooming daily. He is very tolerant of this if done slowly, little & often.

Please get in touch if you feel you might be the right match for this special big guy, he will make you smile every day.

Royal is not a dog I’ve had the chance to work with until recently. I’ve heard a lot about him, as he’s one of our longer stayers. I had heard many great things from other members of staff, including the incredible progress he’s made since joining us!When I did get the chance to work with him, my first impression was “oh my days, you are beautiful!” On first sight, he is one of the most beautiful dogs I’ve ever seen and certainly the most stunning chow I’ve ever seen! How can you look at this handsome boy and not fall in love?!When I actually began working with him, I realised how shy and timid he actually was. Initially, he wouldn’t come to the front of the kennel to see me, he’d hide away in the back. It was evident to me that this boy did not trust me. As I continued to work with him, I was very aware of my actions, to ensure I wasn’t causing any anxiety. I began with treats (who doesn’t love a cheeky bribe?). It slowly worked. Initially, he wanted nothing to do with me. I didn’t want to invade his safe spaces (safe spaces are so important for a more scared or anxious dog. Could you imagine a big scary stranger coming into your home and not leaving? I wouldn’t feel too easy if that occurred to me). So, I’d place the treat and leave the kennel. He’d come out, have a little nosey and take the treat. With time, he began slowly coming out of the back as I entered his kennel. He then began taking treats from my hands and now, whenever I walk onto the section, he comes straight to the gate and waits for me. Honestly, such an incredible feeling making a bond like this with such an incredible boy! There is honestly no feeling like it. They say a dog is a humans best friend but, what no one tells you it works both ways. To build that bond, teach him that I’m not scary, I’m here to help him feel safe, comfortable, happy and to get such a response… it’s honestly the best feeling in the world. Royal needs a home, he needs people to show him this on a day to day basis. We do what we can but, we can’t teach him the safety and comfort of a home, of a family that’s there for him 24/7.Once I got to know this guy a little more, I was taken away. We go out on walks. I feel like this was another bonding experience for us. He loves a walk but, loud noises and interactions with loud people/dogs do freak him out, thus we try to go for quieter walks. He also loves frolicking in the yard. From my experience, he seems to just love being outside!When I worked with him, he didn’t have a friend in his kennel, however, since working with him I have seen him enjoying in the yard with other dogs and is now kennelled with a boxer. He seems very happy. As previously mentioned on his profile, he is to be homed with females around his size or alone. I have not worked with him enough to comment further on his compatibility and amiability with other dogs so, please read the rest of his profile and updates to get a fuller understanding of this incredible boy!At this point, I’ve worked with him enough for him to trust me. He’s happy to see me, he’s fine for me to touch him and fuss him. The Royal I see is a happy dude. He is a scared dog, I’m very aware of that but, the Royal I know now is far different to the Royal I first met. You just have to gain his trust and he’ll let you see him. When you first meet him, he will be shy. He’ll hide and he will not trust you. DO NOT let this deter you. He is one of the sweetest dogs I’ve ever met. From when I first met him to now, I feel like he’s a completely different dog. I was respectful of his boundaries, slow and calm, I did what I could to make him feel comfortable and safe, he then began to trust me and show me his true self (he hides it beneath all that fur). Honestly, I love him. I will take time out of my day to go see him, give him a little treat and some love, just because he is honestly that special. I cannot believe he’s been here over a year. He is one of our most special dogs. I don’t see how anyone can get to know this dog and not love him.Don’t overlook this fluffy dude. Yes, he’s shy and nervous but, the longer you spend with him, care for him and gain his trust, the more you’ll fall in love with him. I can say with confidence; if you put the effort in with Royal, you will fall in love with him.

I absolutely love this boy with my whole heart.

I've been working hard on helping him get used to being brushed because, as a Chow, it's something his future adopters will need to keep up with regularly to keep his coat healthy and prevent mats from developing, especially behind his ears.

Royal is now an absolute angel when it comes to grooming. I brush him every day, and with it being shedding season, no matter how long I brush for, there always seems to be more fur coming out! These days, he simply finds a comfy spot, settles down, and lets me get on with it. If he's had enough, or if I come across a mat that's uncomfortable for him, he communicates so well to let me know he's done for the day.

I also recently decided it was time to give him a bath. I wasn't sure how he'd cope, as it involved picking him up and putting him in the bath, but he was an absolute angel from start to finish. He allowed me to pick him up without any fuss and stood beautifully while I bathed and shampooed him.

I'm so incredibly proud of him. Afterwards, I introduced him to the grooming blower to help remove some of his loose coat. He wasn't a huge fan of it, but he tolerated it for a short while, and I'll continue using it regularly so he can build his confidence with it.

I honestly think all this grooming time has strengthened our bond even more, because lately he seems to be seeking out so much more affection and attention from me. He's such a special boy, and it has been wonderful watching his confidence grow.

Royal has now been with us for over a year, and we’re still waiting for the right person to see just how special he is. He’s had two meet and greets during this time, but sadly neither worked out as he was too nervous meeting new families.

Royal is a sensitive boy who simply needs time, patience, and understanding. He can be unsure at first, but once he begins to trust you, his cheeky, affectionate personality really shines through and it’s such a joy to see.

With a consistent routine, Royal truly thrives. He now enjoys running freely around our large yard without a harness or lead, and when it’s time to go back, he comes straight over. He’s also been out on two longer walks away from the rescue with one of our regular volunteers and has done amazingly well.

All Royal is looking for is someone willing to give him the time and patience he deserves. In return, he’ll become a loyal and loving companion.

I’ve come on leaps and bounds over the past month. I’m still a little shy and can get nervous when I meet new people, but I’m working on it!

I feel most comfortable when I spend quality time with people. It doesn’t take long for me to start feeling at ease (though I still sometimes like my own space). The more time you spend with me, the more comfortable I become—and treats help too! I’ll return your love in equal measure, as long as I’m given the right time, support, and respect.

I love going out for walks, though I can get nervous around loud noises or sudden movements. They might make me jump or feel uneasy, but a bit of love and reassurance always helps!

I feel more comfortable every day. I benefit not only from interaction with my humans, but also from the company of my kennel friends that I live with.

Another month has gone by, and my cheeky boy Royal is still waiting in kennels. I honestly don’t know why this handsome lad isn’t getting much interest. Not only is he completely unique-looking, but he also has the funniest, quirkiest personality. If you want a dog who’ll make you laugh every single day here he is!

Royal is 99% kennel clean and always keeps his bedding tidy… well, until I make his bed perfectly for him. Then he likes to “show me how it’s supposed to be done” by pulling it all across the floor. He walks beautifully on the lead now; he can still get a little spooked from time to time, but he’s made massive progress since the day he arrived.

He loves his toys he just doesn’t love sharing them! He’s also a bit selective with kennel mates, so his ideal home would include a calm, placid large female dog who won’t make too much fuss over him.

Royal truly is an amazing boy, inside and out, and I hope he doesn’t have to wait much longer for the forever home he deserves.

Royal never fails to make us smile with his crazy, funny, and quirky personality. He’s got such a cheeky side to him just waiting for the right people to help it shine.

On the lead, Royal is already walking beautifully, though he can still get a little nervous at times. His new family will need to be patient and willing to help him build confidence. Loud noises or sudden movements can overwhelm him, so he’ll do best with calm, quiet walks to start.

This week Royal had his very first trip down to the big yard! He loved it, though he found his confidence by sticking close to his doggy friend. With more practice, we’re sure he’ll begin to explore on his own.

Royal absolutely adores other dogs. Once he’s settled in, he loves to play, so he’ll need a kind and confident resident dog to show him the ropes, give him reassurance, and of course, enjoy plenty of playtime together.

He’s such a handsome boy with so much love to give we can’t believe he hasn’t found his forever home yet!

This past month has been a huge step forward for our boy Royal! Once a little unsure of the world, Royal is now walking beautifully on lead, it’s such a massive step for him considering how nervous he once was!

Royal currently shares his kennel with both a male and a female dog and he’s proving to be a respectful and easy companion. He enjoys their company, often watching what they do and following their lead. Royal will definitely need another resident dog around his size in his home, so he can continue to have the doggy companionship to help him continue to grow in confidence.

Despite his progress, Royal is still a sensitive soul, and it takes a little time for him to warm up to you. Royals forever family will need to give him time and patience to come out of his shell, so for this reason I believe Royal would be best suited to a home with no children.

Please don’t leave Royal waiting much longer for his forever home, he really deserves a cosy sofa to curl up on!

I’m so proud of Royal, this boy has come on tremendously since arriving at Many Tears. From arriving a terrified dog and very unsure of us humans, he has now slowly but surely begun to trust us and realise we are not so bad, especially when we arrive with cheesy treats.

Royal loves food, toys and being outside in our yards. He has just began harness training, ready to begin lead walking. At the moment he is not so keen on lead walking but he has taken a few tentative steps and with the help of some squeezy cheese and possibly a confident doggie friend to follow I think it won’t be long before he can begin to enjoy exploring the world.

Royals adopters will need to understand he is still very wary and unsure of his environment and he is going to need plenty of time, love and patience to trust his humans, but in the right home and given time I think this boy is going to be a big, playful and lovable boy. Royal will need a home where there is already a resident dog.

Royal is a very scared boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is especially scared when it comes to being touched by us humans but when you get him in the back of the kennel he will allow you to gently stroke him but he is uncomfortable with this. At the moment Royal could possibly make the wrong decision if handled incorrectly but this is purely through fear and he is already starting to make improvements. He will actually get excited to see his kennel mum in the mornings and will wag his tail but he’s not sure how to interact with her yet.

Royal has never lived in a home so this is going to be completely overwhelming at first and he will definitely need at least one other dog in the home to help his confidence. This will help him with house training and lead walking but these are things that are going to take him time to learn as the garden may be as scary as the home at first.

Royal will need a very calm and quiet, adult only home and adopters who have lots of experience with scared dogs. We think he’ll come out of his shell a lot more over time but Royal needs a lot of TLC, time and patience.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Chewwie
description:
I’d like a quiet home filled with love and kindness!

I would like a home with another dog medium size or larger. I am fine with cats.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 2 teeth removed!

Chewwie originally came to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He was lucky enough to be adopted, but sadly, despite being very loved, it became clear that the home wasn't quite the right match for him and he has now returned to our care to begin his search once again. Chewwie was very worried of the adult sons in the home and also wasn't a great match with the smaller resident dog.

Chewwie is a sensitive boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and can find unfamiliar situations overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but remained worried around the adult sons in the household. For this reason, he is looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Since returning to our care, however, Chewwie has been an absolute pleasure. From the day he came back, he has been nothing but gentle, loving and affectionate with everyone here. Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, we have seen a completely different side to him in kennels. He happily bounces over to greet us, is always looking for a fuss, and simply loves being around people. His affectionate nature shines through every day, and he has reminded us just what a special boy he is.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to family life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts of home, especially curling up in his cosy beds. He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and gradually build up any time spent alone as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium-sized or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog-savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has learnt to walk nicely on a lead and now really enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will benefit from ongoing encouragement as his confidence continues to grow.

Once Chewwie knows you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate companion with a wonderfully cheeky personality. He loves playing with other dogs and is especially fond of his kennel friend. He's also a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the paddling pool, making the most of every opportunity for fun. Like many mischievous youngsters, he has also been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially enjoys hard toys, while softer toys and enrichment items should be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. His return to rescue has shown us just how affectionate, gentle and resilient he is, and we know that in the right home he will continue to flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, fun-loving and wonderfully cheeky companion who will fill their days with smiles.

When Chewwie first arrived, he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. Following his return to the rescue, he began limping on the same leg and holding it up. X-rays at a local veterinary practice showed no abnormalities or injuries, so it is thought to be a soft tissue injury which should continue to improve. His adopters and their own vet should continue to monitor this as a precaution.

Chewwie has been given the Gift of Life by Paula Elliot

Chewwie is an absolute angel. From the day he arrived on my section, he's been nothing but gentle, loving, affectionate, and just a truly special soul.

Despite being returned because he was said to be nervous, I honestly haven't seen that side of him. With me, he's all about cuddles and attention. He'll happily bounce over to say hello and is always looking for affection. He's also got a cheeky side that keeps me smiling. If you leave your folder, phone, or radio lying around for even a second, don't be surprised if Chewwie decides it's his now!

He's a total water baby and absolutely loves splashing around in the pool with his kennel friend. Watching him let loose, have fun, and just be a dog is one of my favourite things. He also loves heading down to the big yard where he can have a good sniff, stretch his legs, and enjoy himself.

Chewwie really is such an amazing dog, and I feel so lucky to know him. Looking after him has been an absolute privilege.

Chewwie is a sensitive and nervous boy who had experienced very little before coming into rescue and still finds new situations quite overwhelming. In his previous home, he formed a very close bond with his female adopter and absolutely adored her, but he remained worried around men and struggled to relax around the adult sons in the household. He will therefore be looking for a calm and quiet home with patient adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow him all the time he needs to settle and build trust.

Although he had never lived in a home before his adoption, Chewwie adapted beautifully to home life. He was house trained and thoroughly enjoyed all the comforts that a home has to offer, especially his cosy beds! He did find being left alone quite worrying, so his new adopters will need to be around for most of the time initially and slowly build up the amount of time he is left as his confidence grows.

Chewwie will need another kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help reassure him and show him the ropes, but this dog will need to be medium size or larger. He previously shared his home with a cat and happily ignored them, so he could potentially live with a dog savvy cat.

Since being adopted, Chewwie has also learnt how to walk on a lead and now enjoys his walks, although he can still be worried in unfamiliar places and will need ongoing support and encouragement as he continues to gain confidence.

Once Chewwie gets to know you, he is an incredibly loving and affectionate boy who adores a fuss and cuddle. He has a wonderfully cheeky personality and loves to play with other dogs. He is also a bit of a mischievous boy and has been known to pinch things he shouldn't! His adopters will need to keep a close eye on shoes and other tempting items, as we are told he developed quite a fondness for chewing shoes in his previous home. He especially loves hard toys, but softer toys and enrichment items will need to be supervised as he can quickly chew through them.

Chewwie is a truly special boy who has so much love to give. In the right home he will start to come out of his shell and truly flourish. In return, his lucky adopters will gain a devoted, affectionate and wonderfully cheeky friend who will make them smile every day.

When Chewwie first arrived he had a lick granuloma on his front leg, which healed well. When he returned to the rescue he was limping on his front leg and holding it up, we took him to a local vets for an x-ray and no abnormalities or injuries were found, so it's possible that it is a soft tissue injury which should start to feel better soon, but this is something his adopters and their vet will need to monitor.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Toucan
description:
I would like an active, adult-only home with plenty of adventures and love!

I need to be the only dog in the home, and cannot live with cats!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden with 6ft+ fences to play in.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home and am house trained.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but unfortunately found himself back in rescue.

Toucan is a bright and friendly boy who enjoys meeting new people and, given time to build a bond, forms lovely relationships with his humans. He is affectionate and engaging, and with the right guidance, will make a wonderful addition to a committed home.

He is an active lad who loves his walks and exploring the world around him. At present, he can be strong on the lead as he is eager to get out and sniff everything he sees, so his adopters will need to continue working on his lead training and help him learn to walk more calmly. He is currently being trained to walk on a halti here. His absolute favourite thing in the world is playing with a ball and he just lives to play fetch! He would choose his ball over a treat any day and has proven himself to be the best ball catcher the rescue has seen!

Toucan is a clever boy who is picking things up quickly. He will benefit from a consistent routine and ongoing training to help him feel secure and understand expectations. Providing him with structure, alongside quiet resting spaces where he won’t be disturbed, will be key in helping him manage any anxieties. Although he has lived in a home, he may need some reminders about home life and skills like house training as he settles back into home life.

Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult-only home where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed.

Toucan spent some time in a foster home, but sadly it became clear that his preference was to be an only dog and he didn't enjoy sharing his home with another dog. He does get along well with other dogs when out and about and is fine passing them on walks etc, he would just prefer not to share his space with them. We think he is going to love being the only dog in the home where he can get all the love and attention for himself.

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn’t causing him any issues.

Toucan is a fun, intelligent, and affectionate boy who, with the right experienced adopters, routine, and understanding, will grow into a fantastic and rewarding companion.

Toucan has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Hale

Another month has gone by here at the rescue and still Toucan remains, poor boy isn’t having any luck.

Recently he’s started going out for long walks with one of our experienced volunteers and to say he loves it is an understatement, come rain or shine this boy loves to be outside, either walking or running around the big yard chasing his ball.

The lady that was fostering him also comes up regularly to spend time with him and he gets so excited when he sees her, which shows that once he loves you, he loves you forever and you have a friend for life.

Toucan is a very smart boy and you can’t really fool him by pretending to throw the ball because he catches on quickly that you haven’t, also he is very good at knowing where I’m pointing to. I don’t mean if I’m next to something and pointing right at it, I mean if he can’t find his ball for example, I can point in the direction it went and he’ll look at me and go that way, very very smart boy.

As much as I love Toucan and really enjoy his company, it’s time now for him to find his forever home, I know there’s someone out there for him, the right person could be reading this right now. If you think it could be you but your hesitant, don’t be, honestly Toucan is an amazing dog and everyone that has met him has nothing but lovely things to say about him.

Toucan spent some time in a foster home, but sadly it became clear that his preference was to be an only dog and he didn't enjoy sharing his home with another dog, so he has come back to kennels to continue the search for his perfect home.

Toucan is an absolute angel, but he does find kennel life quite stressful and can become vocal when unsettled. As a result of kennel stress, he can lose weight, so I’m keeping a close eye on him and making sure he’s getting all the nutrition and care he needs.

Toucan is a very active boy! His favourite thing in the world? A ball! He lives to play fetch. I can offer him a treat, but if there’s a ball around he’s much more interested in that. He is the best ball catcher at the rescue, the focus he has on that tennis ball is honestly something I admire. Besides his love for all things round, he is a genuinely sweet boy, who enjoys a fuss and of course a walk. He can be strong on a lead so for this reason I’m currently halti training him and although he’s not a huge fan yet, he is doing really well with it and is currently tolerating it.

Toucan is very trainable and tries his best to figure out what you’re asking him. He’s very smart and it breaks my heart that this beautiful boy is spending his days in kennels instead of out there in the world, playing fetch to his hearts content.

If you’re looking for a smart, active and adventurous best friend then please consider Toucan, he really is an amazing dog and he’s very handsome too.

Toucan is a lovely boy who has settled in as though he’s always been part of the family. He’s very confident and affectionate, and has happily met family and friends - he loves everyone, including my 17-year-old nephew.

He has a big love of food (including everyone else’s!), so he is fed in his crate using a slow feeder bowl to help him pace himself. He needs to gain some weight, so we’ve been adding extra protein to his biscuits and he’s already starting to look healthier.

Toucan is house clean and travels brilliantly in the car, happily jumping in and out. He gets on amazingly well with the four dogs in the home as well as friends’ dogs.

He is comfortable with the crate and, although the door is now left open at night, he still chooses to sleep in there. Toucan can pull on the lead, which we’re currently working on. He isn’t bothered by loud noises and absolutely loves playing ball - he’s fantastic at fetch.

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but has unfortunately found himself back in rescue. Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult only home, where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed. Please don't let this put you off, as he is truly a wonderful boy and his previous adopters have said how wonderful he is and will be in the right home.

Toucan is is always on the go, eager to explore, and looking for his next task. He has a vibrant, happy-go-lucky personality and would thrive in an active home that can provide plenty of attention, as well as physical and mental stimulation. He is super smart and loves to use his brain and already knows "sit", "paw" and "down." He is a lovely boy who is very affectionate and really enjoys having cuddles and fuss once he gets to know you.

Toucan is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog as long as his adopters had plenty of time to spend with him. He could also be homed with another kind resident dog and has shared his kennel well with dogs at the rescue. He can sometimes be reactive to other dogs when passing their kennels but is fine when out and about on lead. He still needs some training on the lead as he likes to be in charge, pulling us along on his travels.

Toucan has learned to walk on a harness, but he can pull and so will need adopters who can manage this and who are willing to work on this with him. He is obsessed with tennis balls and will play all day if you had the time, so he really hopes his new family will enjoy throwing balls for him!

Toucan can be a little greedy, so at the moment he is fed separately from any other dogs. He is a little and so he is now on a raw food diet to help him gain weight.

He had never lived in a home before his adoption and so home life is very new to him and he will need kindness and patience as he settles in. He was clean in his previous home but may have some accidents as he settles into a new home. With kindness, consistency, and plenty of opportunities to burn off his energy, he will make a wonderful, loyal companion for the right family.

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn't causing him any issues.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Lassie
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I cannot live with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Lassie has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was a very nervous girl as she had not had much experience with people, so everything felt very new and overwhelming to her. She could be quite skittish when approached and was worried about meeting new people and being handled. Since then her confidence has started to really grow. Once she gets to know you, she is the most loyal, loving and affectionate girl and it's so wonderful to see.

Lassie will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would benefit from adopters who have breed experience and experience with worried dogs.

She will be looking for a home where there was at least one other kind and playful resident dog to be her friend and guide. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here out and about and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. However, we have found that she is most comfortable sharing her home with other Collies and will therefore need a home with at least one resident Collie. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries. She doesn't like to share her food with other dogs, so her adopters would need to ensure she was fed separately and would need to separate when feeding any long last treats or chews too.

Lassie now walks well on a lead and would love to find an active home where she can go on lots of walks and adventures with her new family and where her clever collie brain can be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. She is only used to walking in quiet areas, so would need gentle introduction to any busier places. Lassie has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles into the home and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.

With time, patience, and lots of love, Lassie will blossom. Once she has settled and gained confidence, she will become a cracking addition to her new family and will enjoy all the adventures life has to offer.

Lassie will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Lassie spent some time in the office today and coped really well. She happily tucked into a chicken foot for a tasty treat, although she couldn't resist pinching her kennel friend's one too! She was very curious about everything going on around her and enjoyed exploring her surroundings.

A member of staff she hadn't met before came into the office, and although Lassie was a little wary at first, she quickly settled and went back to happily enjoying her chicken foot. It was lovely to see her take the new experience in her stride and continue growing in confidence.

Beautiful beautiful Lassie! What a collie she is, she is so bright and has really come on so much with her basic training. Now knowing "sit" and "lie down". When we're out walking and a car is approaching, all I have to do is ask her to the verge and she sits and waits beautifully until we're able to start walking again. She really doesn't seem to be fazed by much traffic, but is very fixated with sheep if she comes across any. She passes horses lovely and will happily walk past other dogs no issue, but isn't keen on them approaching her. She's a big fan of food which helps with her training.She just needs people that understand that the girl she is when they first meet her is very worried but once she trusts you, her true personality really shines through.

Lassie is such a pretty girl who would do anything for you when she trusts you but is still wary of people initially. She did take treats off of a new person yesterday which was amazing to see. She needs to be in a collie experienced home with someone who will allow her the time to trust them at her own pace. She does love having a playfriend and she seems to be happiest when amongst other collies and collie crosses. She doesn't like sharing her food but is happy to share toys, beds and treats.

Lassie absolutely loves going out for her walks and gets very excited when she knows it’s time to head out. She really enjoys having a good sniff along the way and is always very interested in watching what’s going on in the fields as she passes by. Once she gets to know you, she is incredibly loving and affectionate, although she can take a little bit of time to warm up to new people. Lassie would still need a home with a resident dog, and she would truly thrive in a collie-experienced home where her needs and personality can be well understood.

Lassie is such a beautiful girl and once she knows you, she is the most affectionate, loyal and loving companion. She now walks well on a lead and absolutely loves her walks.

She will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who is a similar size to her and who loves to have a good play sometimes.

She doesn't like to share her food bowl, so he will need to be fed separately and this is something that her adopters will need to manage. In the right home she'll be someone's absolute best friend.

Lassie is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has not had much experience with people, so everything feels very new and overwhelming to her. She can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need a calm, experienced home where she can be given the time and patience she needs to learn to trust.

At the moment, Lassie is scared of being touched, but she has already started to build a bond with her kennel mum and now allows gentle strokes from her. This shows that with consistency and kindness, shecanlearn to trust, and once she feels safe, she will begin to show her sweet side.

Lassie does walk on a lead, though she finds new experiences worrying, so she will need gentle introductions to the big wide world. She will also need to learn about house training and all the basics of living in a home, as these are things she has never known before.

Because Lassie is such a sensitive soul, she will need an adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who are happy to take things slowly at her pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel secure and show her the ropes. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

name: Shiloh
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

03-08-26 Meet Shiloh.Shiloh is a very special boy looking for a very special home.He originally came to us in 2022 as part of an unsold litter and was lucky enough to find a loving home. Sadly, his adopters are no longer able to manage his behavioural needs, so Shiloh has returned to us in the hope that we can find him a home that is better suited to him and where he can continue to thrive.

Shiloh is a wonderfully funny, affectionate boy who absolutely adores his people. He has the biggest, goofiest grin and loves nothing more than a good chest tickle, playing and spending time with the people he trusts. He is also a complete water baby and absolutely loves playing in the river and streams! He is used to having a very active lifestyle, including 3 mile walks in the morning and several opportunities to play in the stream throughout the day, so his new family will need to be able to offer him the active lifestyle he requires.

Shiloh does, however, have some significant behavioural needs, and it is very important that his new family fully understands these before applying. He is a sensitive boy who can take time to trust people and initially expects the worst from new situations. He can be particularly worried by men. With patience, kindness and reward-based training, he has been making wonderful progress and is learning that people can be trusted.

Shiloh does have a history of biting when frightened, including when startled awake. It’s very important that he must have a quiet, undisturbed place where he can sleep and relax. In his previous home he was not allowed on the sofas or beds. Shiloh can panic if suddenly woken and may react defensively, so his new family will need to be very respectful of his space and understand his communication. He also has a history of guarding high-value items. He is generally very good with his own food and will happily wait for his release command before eating, but he will try to steal human food if given the opportunity and may guard it. His new owners will therefore need to have previous experience of managing dogs with resource guarding and similar behavioural challenges.

Shiloh can also be reactive when out on walks. He is muzzle trained and walks well while wearing his muzzle, which is the safest way for him to enjoy his walks. His reactions towards other dogs appear to be largely frustration-related, so this must be taken seriously and managed appropriately. Despite this, Shiloh has been doing so well at the rescue and has recently started having play dates with suitable dogs. He has been an incredibly respectful boy during these interactions, which has been lovely to see!

Shiloh does have a high prey drive and will chase livestock, sohe must remain on lead and muzzled when out of the home.He can pull on walks, but for an experienced and active family looking for a walking companion, Shiloh could be a wonderful adventure buddy.

He can also find formal handling very worrying and is currently working hard on becoming braver when visiting the vets. He is muzzled for veterinary examinations and will need a family who understands that formal handling and veterinary care will need to be approached slowly and carefully.

Despite all of his worries, Shiloh is a boy who tries incredibly hard. We are told that in the home he knows the command to go to his bed and is happy to settle there and chill out by himself. More than anything, he loves his people and wants to be close to those he trusts.

Shiloh is looking for anadult-only home with no visiting children.His ideal home would berural and away from busy, urban environments, with a large, very secure garden with 6ft+ fences.His new family will need to be experienced dog owners who have previously lived with dogs with behavioural challenges, ideally with experience of similar breeds too. They must be willing to give Shiloh plenty of time to settle, never rush him and continue the kind, reward-based training that is helping him make such wonderful progress.

Shiloh isn't going to be the right dog for everyone, and we appreciate that his requirements are extensive. However, for the right person,we believe there is a really special dog underneath all of those worries.Shiloh has so much love to give, and we would love to find him a home where his people can see the wonderful, goofy, affectionate boy that we see every day.

If you think you could offer this very special boy the calm, experienced and active home he deserves, we would love for you to consider Shiloh.

name: Crumble
description:
I need an adult-only, experienced home where I can feel safe and loved.

I want to be the only dog in the house. No cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I love my walks so one or two a day would be great!

I’ve never lived in a home, so I need to learn housetraining and lead walking.

Crumble is a lovely lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings. She seems to be gaining confidence each day, which is wonderful to see.

While she can still be sensitive and appreciates having her space respected, it’s clear that Crumble simply needed time to feel safe. With gentle reassurance and plenty of TLC, her true personality is beginning to shine through. She is a gentle soul who responds best to calm, kind interactions and slow introductions.

She would be happiest and thrive best as the only dog in the home, where she can enjoy all the attention, settle more easily into a routine, and build a strong bond with her new family.

As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training and learning everyday routines. She will need a home without cats as she is overly interested.

We are looking for an experienced, adult-only home where Crumble can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. A quiet household with understanding adopters who are happy to let her take things slowly will allow her to truly flourish. With the right people, time, and lots of love, Crumble will make a wonderfully rewarding companion.

On arrival, our vets noted that Crumble had a Grade 2 luxating patella. During her time with us she has shown very intermittent lameness, mostly only seen when she’s getting up from laying down for a long time. She was sent for x-rays which showed potential damage to her left cruciate ligament, as well as hip dysplasia in her right hip. She is currently managing very well with rest and pain relief, and we will work on building correct muscle tone to support her as well as slow introductions to controlled exercise and physio.

There’s not a bad word you could say about this girly pop. She is goofy, affectionate, playful, friendly and gaining confidence by the day! She has been trying her best to be kennel clean, no encouragement needed.

She is a staff favourite and that girls little teefys are part of her personality! Nibbling at you to show you just how much she loves to play with you, entertains her pal Criss cross and her kennel mums in the yard.

She belongs in a home where her people can show her the best doggy life imaginable while also understanding that Crumble has also not known much of the world and requires a bit of patience and care when handling her.

Taking every opportunity to play and zoom around with her best friend, Criss Cross.Her confidence is growing and enjoying her walks and greeting new people at her own free will as long as she is guaranteed some fuss or treats.

She enjoys sprawling out on the floor with her chew toy just enjoying the vibes.When she finds her home she will be very eager in sharing her affectionate nature with her family

Crumble is becoming a very happy chow now and has recently discovered that there's no limit on zoomies. She does get along with her chow friend, Criss Cross, but isn't keen on other dogs, so is looking for a home as an only. She is wary of people initially, but once you've gained her trust she becomes your absolute best mate. She loves her walks and gets very excited when she sees you bringing her harness towards her. She's a big foodie too and loves treats.

Crumble is coming on so beautifully and it truly makes my heart melt. Today we had some cuddle and play time in her kennel, and it was such a special moment. For a girl who once wasn’t very happy with touch, she’s now rolling over for belly rubs, snuggling in her bed, and even playing “paw paw” with me.

She’s also learning about wearing a harness and is improving every day. If you have a Crumble shaped hole in your life, she really is something special.

Crumble is a worried lady who came into our care from a breeder, searching for a fresh start. When she first arrived, she was very worried and unsure of the world around her, but with time and patience she has begun to settle beautifully. Crumble is now much less fearful of us humans and has really started to come out of her shell, choosing to engage more with staff members and showing curiosity about her surroundings.

Crumble will need a confident and friendly resident dog who can help guide her and show her the ropes. As she has never lived in a home environment before, she will need patient support with house training, lead walking, and learning everyday routines. But will need to take things slow to start with some garden sniffs adventures on the lead may be too scary to start.

Crumble has a previous bite wound inside her ear, which is currently being treated.

name: Querty
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I have eyelid trauma that does not seem to bother me & I will be spayed.

06-08-26 Querty is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is trying her very best to be brave but is still quite apprehensive of people. Although she is unsure, Querty will quietly seek out a little fuss and attention, showing us that she has some confidence waiting to emerge.

Querty gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Querty has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding, allowing her to adjust at her own pace and celebrate every little milestone along the way. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 13+ who will allow her time to settle in at her own pace. Her adopters will need to have experience with ex-breeders to understand her needs.

Querty is a sweet, gentle girl who is already showing glimpses of the lovely companion she could become. With the support of a friendly canine friend and a calm, patient family, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything that a loving home has to offer.

Querty has arrived with trauma to her left eyelid which has left her eye constantly weepy.

Querty has been given the Gift of Life by Fiona Walsh

name: Faith
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a large, extra-secure garden to keep me safe as I learn about the home.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

07-08-26 Faith is a beautiful girl who has come to us from a breeder in search of a new start. She is understandably apprehensive of people and is not yet comfortable with being handled. Although she isn't keen on being picked up, she accepts it when we need to check her over, showing just how gentle she is despite her worries. Faith is still learning that people can be trusted and will need patient adopters who are happy to let her settle at her own pace.

Faith gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws. She will need an adult-only home with experience with the Collie breed and that Faith will need plenty of enrichment and exercise to keep her busy!

As Faith has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training, and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her plenty of time, patience, and reassurance as she adjusts to everything that is new to her. She will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft, to keep her safe in her new home.

Faith is a gentle soul who deserves the chance to feel safe and loved. With a calm home, a confident canine companion, and lots of kindness, we hope she will gradually grow in confidence and begin to enjoy all the comforts of family life.

Faith has been given the Gift of Life by Raychel Mount

name: Unity
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

19-07-26 Unity has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a very frightened little girl who is finding all the recent changes in her life overwhelming. Everything around her is new and unfamiliar, so she will need patient, understanding adopters who can help her discover that the world isn't such a scary place.

Unity is looking for a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time, patience and commitment they need. She will thrive with a family who are happy to let her settle at her own pace, allowing her confidence to grow naturally without putting her under pressure.

She finds great comfort in the company of other dogs and will need to live with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who can show her the ropes and help her feel safe. A canine companion will play a vital role in helping Unity gain confidence as she adjusts to her new life.

Unity has never experienced life in a home before, so she will need gentle guidance as she learns about home life and new skills like house training. She has not yet learnt to walk on a lead or harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden until she is feeling brave enough to venture further.

Unity is a gentle, sensitive girl who has so much potential. With a loving, experienced family, a confident canine friend by her side and all the time she needs to settle, we are sure she will gradually blossom into the wonderful companion she was always meant to be.

Unity has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

name: Nelly
description:
I will need an adult only home with breed-experience.

I’d like to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on the lead but I am strong, so I will need continued training!

I have lived in a home, but may need a few reminders as I settle in.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

Nelly, also known as 'Nellyphant' amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

Nelly is a typical fun-loving Bulldog girl who is full of character. She loves attention, affection and being involved in everything her people are doing. She enjoys a good play session, especially when there is a ball involved! Tennis balls, footballs, honestly, anything she can throw around will make her happy. She is even learning that dropping the ball means the fun can start all over again. Once playtime is finished, she is just as happy settling down for a well-earned rest.

Sadly, the instability Nelly has experienced has left her feeling worried when she is left alone. She can become distressed when separated and will need a home where she is not left for long periods. Her adopters will need to build up time apart gradually, using patience and consistency to help her understand that her people will always return.

Nelly is currently learning about other dogs and is not yet comfortable around them. She is doing brilliantly with her muzzle training, which allows her to enjoy her walks safely while she learns that other dogs are not something to worry about. She can enjoy walking alongside calm, quiet dogs, but she may react if she feels overwhelmed, especially with larger dogs or if another dog barks at her first. Her new family will need to continue her muzzle training on walks and support her with positive, patient guidance.

Nelly can already walk on a lead, although she is a strong and enthusiastic girl who can pull when excited. She will need adopters who are confident handling her and who are happy to continue her lead training. She loves getting out for walks, having zoomies and exploring, but she is equally happy being a cuddle-loving couch potato afterwards.

Nelly has come from a home before, so she may already understand some household routines, but she may need gentle reminders as she settles into a new environment. She will need an adult-only home with breed-experienced adopters who understand her bouncy nature and can provide the boundaries, consistency and love she needs. She will need to be the only dog in the home, with no visiting dogs and no cats. She will also need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft+.

Nelly is wonderful at the vets and loves the attention she receives there. She enjoys spending time with the staff, soaking up the fuss and showing everyone what a friendly and affectionate girl she is.

Nelly is a resilient, loving dog who has been through more than she should have, yet she continues to greet the world with excitement and affection. She is ready for a family who will spoil her, make her feel safe and show her just how wonderful life can be. For lovers of Bulldog breeds, Nelly’s silly personality and loving nature are sure to bring endless joy.

*Nelly has been measured by our local Dog Licensing Officer and confirmed that she is not considered a banned breed.

Nelly, AKA 'Nellyphant', plays football and she’s amazing at it! She also absolutely loves a herding ball. In fact, Nelly would play with any ball or toy for hours if she had her way, and we have to remind her to take breaks and relax for a bit.

Nelly has an exuberant nature, and no day is bad when Nelly's about. Nelly is now muzzle trained and proudly trots along the lanes near the rescue, donning her bright pink muzzle.

Nelly really is a delightful, confident, and human-loving dog, and as much as she likes to play, she will settle down and chill, often contentedly hanging out with the office staff at the rescue whilst they're busy working away.

Nelly's ideal home would have no other dogs and adult humans who have plenty of time to play and hang out with her, as well as knowledge and experience of bull breeds.

This super lady really does deserve to find a lovely home of her own soon.

Nelly, also known as Hippo amongst the kennel staff, is a beautiful girl with a huge personality and an even bigger heart. Nelly came into our care after experiencing a difficult past, having spent much of her life confined to a very small room and sadly being passed between several homes. Despite everything she has been through, her love for people has never faded. She absolutely adores human company and greets everyone she meets like they are her new best friend.

name: Lady
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need another kind resident dog in my new home. I haven't met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have had 1 tooth extracted and am ready to find my forever home!

Lady has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a sweet and gentle girl who was a little worried to find herself here when she first arrived, but did start to soon become very inquisitive and was trying so hard to be brave. She has since moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in well and learning all about home life for the first time ever.

Lady is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle at her own pace and build her confidence, she would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs. Her confidence is starting to grow and she will now allow her fosterer to gently stroke her and seems to enjoy this.

She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help her feel secure as she settles in. She can guard her food bowl from other dogs, so she will need to be feed separately in her new home and will need adopters who are confident managing this, but she hasn't shown any signs of guarding treats.

Lady had never lived in a home before moving to foster, she is starting to learn all about home life and house training and is toileting on newspaper at the moment, so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she continues to learn. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and will need to practice first around the home and garden before venturing further.

With time, kindness and encouragement, we believe Lady will blossom into a wonderful companion. Lady is a truly sweet girl, and we can’t wait to see her thrive in a loving home.

She has had one tooth extracted at the time of her spay.

Lady has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Lady has now been in her foster home for just over a week and is settling in well. She is a gentle, sweet girl who will now stand for gentle strokes and, after just a few days, was comfortable enough to allow her foster carer to clean and trim around her eyes. She is also doing well with her house training and will use newspapers when indoors.

Lady won't take long to settle into a forever home, as long as she's given the time and space to get to know her new family and surroundings. Once she feels safe, her lovely personality really begins to shine.

Lady has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a sweet and gentle girl who is a little worried to find herself here, but she has been easy to handle and is already becoming a very inquisitive little girl! It's clear that she is trying so hard to be brave and really wants to come and say hello, so we don't think it will take her too long to come out of her shell in her new home.

Lady is looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle at her own pace and build her confidence, she would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs. We would consider homing her with gentle dog savvy older teenagers.

Lady has never lived in a home before, so she will need patient and understanding adopters who can help her learn all about home life. She will need support with the basics such as house training, learning to walk on a lead, and discovering that the world isn’t such a scary place. With time, kindness and encouragement, we believe Lady will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Lady is a truly sweet girl, and we can’t wait to see her thrive in a loving home.

name: Emrys
description:
I am looking for an adult only home with experienced adopters.

I could live with other dogs or be the only dog. I cannot be homed with cats.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Emrys is such a wonderful boy. He’s currently living in a foster home where has been for a year now and has absolutely flourished with them. He originally came to us from a farm so had very little in the way of training and socialising. This meant he could find new people worrying and during a short adoption of just a few months, he struggled to get used to a male visitor and would react towards him and redirected onto another person while stressed. He was returned to his foster home following this and hasn’t put a paw out of place since.

In foster, Emrys does very well, he absolutely adores his three collie best friends and we think he would thrive in a home with a resident dog to keep him company. We would consider an experienced home adopting him as an only dog however he loves having doggy friends so would need regular playdates. Unfortunately Emrys cannot live with cats. He is looking for a collie and rescue experienced home to help him thrive. He absolutely loves his walks and as he is such a clever lad, he will need brain games to wear out his mind too! If an active home is looking for a dog to join in on a sport like agility, we are sure he would do well!

Once Emrys trusts you, he is a wonderful companion and after an exciting walk where he gets to play with his friends, he does really enjoy a cuddle and a snooze on the couch. He is looking for a quiet, adult only home who understands collie behaviour, especially collies bred to work. When introduced to people with plenty of space to move away if he gets worried, he makes friends quickly. His amazing foster home have done so well in bringing out his silly, confident side and absolutely love his quirks. He is such a brilliant boy and has been waiting very patiently for his forever family.

Emrys has a fatty lump on the right flank that does not pose as an issue and is being monitored.

Emrys has been in foster with us for the past 10 months and has proven to be a confident, affectionate collie. He loves his walks just as much as he enjoys relaxing on the sofa afterwards.

He gets along well with both dogs and people, is clean in the house, and travels happily in the car. During his time with us, Emrys has shown no signs of reactivity and has greeted all visitors kindly.

He is a truly lovely dog and would make a fantastic, loyal companion.

Emrys has been in foster with us for seven months now, and he’s a real character. He gets on well with all dogs and, since being back with us, has shown no reactive or guarding behaviours. In the right home, he will truly thrive and make a wonderful companion.

Emrys can occasionally feel nervous around new people, and when this happens he takes himself off to his safe space, which is in the garden. From there, he’ll assess the situation at his own pace before coming back inside when he’s ready to meet someone new. It’s important that he’s given the time and space to do this calmly.

Once he knows you, Emrys is an absolute joy to be around. He loves his walks and secure field runs, is calm and settled in the evenings, and is incredibly affectionate.

With his wicked personality and loving nature, Emrys will make a fantastic companion for the right person.

Emrys has been back in foster for 11 weeks now and has settled in beautifully with no problems at all. He gets on very well with the three resident dogs as well as visiting dogs, and he is friendly with visitors and strangers outside the home. Emrys is totally house clean, travels well in the car, and is very treat-orientated, which makes him easy to train. After his walks, he loves nothing more than relaxing with his foster family.

Emrys has settled back in beautifully with his foster family and hasn’t shown any issues at all. He loves racing around the garden with the resident dogs and is starting to enjoy playing with toys and bringing a ball back.

He’s now completely house trained, walks very nicely on the lead, and is happy to travel in the car.

Emrys is such a lovable boy and is coming along wonderfully. He’ll make a fantastic companion for the right home.

Emrys is a striking, high-energy Collie who came to us from a farm where his owner could no longer give him the time he needed. After arriving he quickly found himself in foster, where he received plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and affection, everything a clever Collie thrives on.He was adopted for a short time, but sadly returned to us after displaying behaviours in the home that hadn’t been seen while in foster. His adopters told us that Emrys exhibited some guarding tendencies and could react negatively when he felt backed into a corner or overwhelmed. Because of this, he’s looking for a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand the needs of a sensitive, intelligent dog and can support him with firm but kind guidance.Emrys will need a secure garden with space to run, and a home that can provide him with plenty of structured physical and mental activity to keep him happy and settled. He’s a bright boy who’s eager to please and loves learning. With patience, consistency, and the right support, Emrys has every potential to thrive.Emrys is now back with his original foster where he has shown many lovely qualities, he is clean in the house, travels well in the car, walks nicely on the lead, and is affectionate with those he trusts. He’s also food-motivated and already learning basic commands. We believe that Emrys thrives on activity and as he has not displayed these behaviours in foster it may be because he is provided with so much stimulation and exercises. His adopters will need to keep this in mind, and ideally be very active and willing to provide him with different games and activities to keep his mind busy.Emrys could live with another confident resident dog or be the only dog in the right home. He cannot live with cats, and due to his sensitivity, he will need a home without children or visiting children.This boy has so much potential and is just waiting for the right people to help him blossom.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Criss Cross
description:
I need an adult-only experienced home that understands me.

I'd prefer to be the only dog in the home and no cats please!

I’m still shy, so I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can now walk on a lead and harness and enjoy my walks.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Criss Cross, a big-hearted, sensitive lad who has come to us from a breeder and is slowly learning to find his confidence in the world. When Criss Cross arrived as a worried soul, needing extra patience, understanding, and gentle care. He had very little formal handling in his past, and early on could be grumbly or anxious when unsure. He required slow, careful introductions to people, places, and experiences while he started to understand his new surroundings.

While Criss Cross can still be a little shy when meeting new people, once he feels comfortable his affectionate side really shines through. He actively seeks out fuss and cuddles and has become quite the cuddle bug, often trying to return kisses to the people he trusts. He is learning his manners well and responds nicely to calm, consistent guidance.

Criss Cross is growing in confidence with his harness training and now enjoys daily walks beyond the rescue. He has even started greeting some people on his walks for a hello and perhaps a treat or a fuss. He can still feel a little unsure if people are behind him, but gentle encouragement and reassurance help him relax and continue exploring the world around him.

He has also started learning about kennel cleanliness, with staff helping him practice good toilet habits to make the transition into a home life easier for him in the future. When enjoying some quiet time on his own, Criss Cross loves exploring his toy collection, especially anything involving treats or food puzzles.

Criss Cross would prefer to be the only dog in the home so he can fully relax and enjoy all the attention for himself.
