Lacey is a 1-year-old female Labrador Retriever. She is looking for an active family home where she can continue to enjoy the happy and energetic lifestyle that suits her best. Lacey has a wonderful character and loves everyone she meets.

She enjoys being out on walks and is always happy to explore with her family. One of her favourite things is spending time around water, and she especially loves lakes. She is also house trained, making her ready to settle into a home.

Lacey was rescued from the meat trade in China alongside her mum and siblings. Her mum and siblings have already found their homes in the UK, and now it is Lacey’s turn to find a loving family of her own.

She has come a long way and is ready to begin the next chapter of her life.

Lacey can live with all dogs, making her a great companion for a home with canine friends. She has not been cat tested, so it is not known whether she could live with cats. She can also live with children aged 10 years and over.

Lacey is currently living in foster care in Buckinghamshire while she waits for her forever home. She is fully vetted and ready to join the right family.

With her affectionate nature, love of people and enjoyment of outdoor adventures, Lacey is hoping to find a home where she can continue to thrive.

name: Cece
description:
Cece is an 18 month old Shepherd mix who arrived at the shelter as an unclaimed stray, a story we’ve heard many a time. No one came looking for her, and she had no microchip or collar, so who knows where she came from.

She was however in good health, and happy to meet new people, so we’re hopeful that she’s not had a difficult start in life.

Cece is around a year and a half old and she is a beautiful girl with a very happy, friendly and sociable personality. She loves being around people and is very eager to please, quietly confident, and reads other dogs well.

It took a little while for her to initially calm down when she first arrived in the shelter as she had some nervous energy to burn off, but once we’d found her the ideal kennel mates and she’d had some time to decompress, her true nature started to shine through.

As mentioned, Cece now shares her kennel with multiple other dogs of various sizes, ages and energy levels. She’s loving having the opportunity to make new friends and enjoys playing with them and just being in their company.

While we don’t feel she’s dependant on other dogs, she definitely likes hanging out with them, and she’s more than happy to share her bed, which is so cute.

18 months old is still young, so Cece would benefit from some basic training to help refine her manners a little. She learnt to sit in no time, despite all the distractions around her in the shelter.

As she is food motivated, this works really well as a reward. When she’s excited to see you Cece is prone to jumping up a bit, but it doesn’t take long for this to pass and with some routine and a proper home setting, we’re confident that is very trainable.

The ideal home for Cece would be with a family who enjoy time outdoors, have direct access to a secure garden, and who are keen to invest some time into a young dog learning about a whole new world.

We think the outskirts of the city would be preferable for Cece, or of course a more rural setting would suit her just fine too.

She’d enjoy a fairly active lifestyle, and with some time and patience we think she will make a brilliant addition to a family home.

name: Cassie
description:
Cassie is a one year old Shepherd mix and was found running through farmland when a local rescuer was able to coax her into her car and take her to safety.

Surprisingly, during her check up at the vets they discovered that she actually had a registered microchip, so they were able to track down her owners and asked them to come and collect her.

But of course, had the story ended positively, then Cassie wouldn’t be on our website. Sadly, her family said they didn’t want her anymore as she was too energetic, and that the rescuer could rehome her.

There was no sense of remorse or accountability, they just gave her away and moved on with their lives.

Cassie is a shepherd mix and she is indeed an energetic, active and highly intelligent young dog. She’s estimated to be just under a year old, and she is always raring to get outside and go on an adventure.

Right now, she’s in private kennels where she’s safe and sound until she finds her forever home, but she needs more exercise and enrichment than they can offer her, and as a result whenever she goes out for a run in the yard she is like a coiled spring.

Cassie is looking for a family who have had high energy dogs before and can give her the physical and mental outlets that she needs to thrive. She is so, so loyal and bonds with people very quickly.

She’s extremely keen to please and eager to learn, and as she’s so food motivated this makes the perfect reward!

Cassie would be best suited to a home outside of the city with an active family who enjoy running, exploring and just generally being outdoors.

When her needs are met, like any dog, Cassie is a bundle of love and loves hanging out with people. She’s also great with other dogs, especially those of a similar energy level to her, and she loves racing around in the grass with them.

She would also be best suited to a home with a reasonable size garden, as she really likes being outdoors.

Cassie may be young and bouncy, but she also has lots of love to give. She is the perfect dog for someone seeking a best friend, adventure partner and a companion that they can train.

name: Eraty
description:
Hi, I’m Eraty, a small size 3 year old kokoni cross girl.

I don’t remember much kindness from my early life.

I was one of 27 dogs rescued from a hoarding situation last October. We had never really been socialised, and human contact wasn’t something we looked forward to.

Like the others, I was especially worried about anyone touching around my neck. It brought back memories I’d rather forget.

When I arrived in rescue, I was scared of almost everything. People were confusing, the world felt big, and trusting anyone seemed impossible.

The dogs there became my best friends straight away. They showed me how to play, how to relax, and most importantly, how to feel safe. My foster mum and dad had to work a little harder.

For weeks, I watched them from a distance, trying to understand why they kept being so gentle with me.

They never expected more than I could give.

One day I realised I wanted to be a little closer. Then a little closer again. Before I knew it, I was sitting beside them on the sofa, enjoying head scratches and asking for cuddles all by myself.

These days, I’m a happy girl who loves countryside walks, playing with my doggy friends, and relaxing at home. I also live with cats and get along with them very well.

I’m still a sensitive soul and I’ll need a family who understands that trust is something I’ve had to learn. But every step of my journey has shown that underneath the fear was a loving dog just waiting for someone to believe in her.

A friendly, playful resident dog is a must to build my confidence.

If you’re patient, kind, and willing to let me go at my own pace, I think we could be something very special together.

name: Ripp
description:
A breeder surrender who is very shy but shows no sign of aggression unless pushed unnecessarily outside of his comfort zone. Why would you want to?

He needs a safe, quiet and warm home where he can mooch about inside and outside with a private enclosed garden.

When he feels safe, Ripp will reward you with so much love.

He will then feel safe enough to venture out on rural walks. This is a special boy that needs a very special person.

Ripp is ready to travel, wherever that wonderful home may be.

name: Valentina
description:
Valentina had her freedom ride from the pound in February where she had spent two years.

She had a chip but her owner never responded to the calls.

That’s all behind her now and as you can see she is glowing!

Valentina is three years old and an English Bulldog cross. She is slight and weighs 20 kgs.

Short walks are best and she enjoys the company of male dogs her own size.

Spayed, fully vaccinated, blood tested and holding an EU passport.

Valentina is ready to travel and will be delivered to your front door.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 3 year old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier Cross.

Lucy came to us a few weeks ago after being rescued from a heavy chain and showing obvious signs of a recent litter and probably several others in her past.

Having given Lucy time to settle into her new routine and environment here at Sunny Shores, we felt the time was right to take her to our vet and get her blood tests, vaccinations, chip and passport sorted.

Our vet aged her at around two years of age.

Her underside is looking much better and her general condition is massively improved thanks to good quality regular food.

Once very hand shy, she handled the journey and the vet’s needles like a pro and returned to Sunny Shores for a walk and a fuss showing off her huge Staffy smile.

Lucy is now very confident around people she knows and loves a fuss and with a proper introduction she will soon adapt to new people and her new life.

name: Noah
description:
Noah is a two year old cross breed and is every bit the silly goofball that he looks to be in his photos. We love this daft boy, and he came to us a few weeks ago after being found as yet another wandering stray.

Unfortunately for Noah, in terms of appearance he is the kind of dog that we often see overlooked for a long time – we don’t know why, they just always seem to take longer!

We’re hoping that just maybe he’ll get lucky before he has to spend months on end behind bars.

Noah is around two years old and full of fun. He is such a positive dog and despite his life in the shelter being relatively boring, any moment of excitement that he does get to experience, he does so with 100% enthusiasm.

He loves any kind of human interaction and is beside himself with happiness when someone goes into his kennel to spend time with him. He’s a very sociable, human focused dog and just wants to be loved.

Noah shares his kennel with a quiet, older female dog, and despite his energy he understands that he needs to give her some space and calm down when she’s not feeling it.

He seems to be able to read canine body language well, and we think he could live with or without other dogs.

He appreciates their company and seems to enjoy an opportunity to play when it’s offered, but he is also very people oriented so doesn’t depend on other dogs to feel secure and confident.

Noah is young and still very bouncy at times, although a lot of this is due to lack of exercise and no outlets for his excitement.

With a proper routine and lots of lovely long walks, we’re sure he will calm down, but it would still be in his best interest to have some entry level training, to learn the basics and improve his manners.

He is so keen to please and very food motivated, so he loves to learn! He has already perfected a very nice ‘sit’ in the shelter, and looks extremely proud of himself whilst doing so.

Noah has a huge heart and so much love to give. He’s looking for an active home with a garden, someone up for the fun that a younger, more energetic dog can bring into their household, and someone that can also shower him in the love that he craves.

He will make the absolute best friend once he’s had a chance to settle in and find his feet.

name: Brock
description:
Drop dead gorgeous Brock is a two year old Pointer/Bully mix and arrived at the shelter a couple of months ago after the dog warden brought him in as a stray.

We were assuming someone would come and collect him, as he was in great health and was so happy around people, but sadly days turned into weeks and no one came to get him.

Brock is now searching for a new home where he can be treated like the prince he truly is!

Brock is estimated to be around two years old and definitely has some kind of hound in him among various other breeds – he’s a real mixed bag but so handsome.

He has stunning markings which look very Bracque, and he is also very people oriented and clever. He is keen to please and loves to impress people. He learned a gorgeous sit in just a few tries and now sits beautifully waiting for a treat in his kennel.

Brock would be best suited to a home where he’s the centre of attention. Since being in the shelter he has been fine with female dogs, but he is more picky with male dogs and doesn’t really like to share his space with them.

With this in mind he would also be better suited to a family that have experience of owning dogs before, just so they feel comfortable managing interactions. With people though, Brock is an absolute superstar and just adores everyone.

Brock would be happy in a home with a fairly active lifestyle and someone who wants to work a bit more on his training. As he’s clever, he really enjoys learning and benefits from some focus and direction.

He also has potential to enjoy scent training, as he loves to use his nose like – typical hound! He would also prefer a home with access to a nice garden.

Brock would be great with children and he loves any kind of attention. He can be bouncy and excitable, so with that in mind children aged 8+ are probably more appropriate.

Brock would make an amazing adventure companion and would love to opportunity to spend lots of time outdoors. He has plenty of stamina, and would relish the opportunity to become the apple of someone’s eye.

He is very loyal and loving, and as long as someone is comfortable with him not being the best of friends with every single dog he meets, he could absolutely shine in the right forever home.

name: Taffy
description:
Taffy is a one year old German Shepherd cross and was brought into the shelter by the dog wandering after she was found wandering through the fields as a stray.

She wasn’t difficult to catch as she was more than happy to see new humans and trot over to them! She’s now very patiently waiting for her second chance, hoping that her new family are out there.

Taffy is estimated to be around a year old and as appears to be a theme with our shepherd girls, she’s so clever. The boys aren’t quite at their level just yet!

Taffy is very smart and similarly to Birdie, who came in a few weeks before her, she also new some basic commands which suggests she’s had a home, or at least positive human interaction (maybe from a farm owner or outside an army base) from someone.

Taffy now shares her kennels with another dog and although she was initially a bit disgruntled about having to share her space with a male dog, they’ve since really started to get along.

She will grumble at him a bit if he’s invading her space or jumping on her too much, but between them they seem to have sussed out their new friendship and are getting on just fine.

Taffy could definitely live alongside a resident dog in her new home, but she’s a confident girl and doesn’t seek out their company.

Being a shepherd, Taffy is not only smart but she’s also fiercely loyal and very active. She would thrive in a home where she has access to a secure garden to run around in and sunbathe, and she would also be best suited to a family who enjoy an energetic lifestyle.

Getting the opportunity to explore would be perfect for Taffy, and she’ll be a great partner in crime on an adventure or a long hike.

She is still getting used to lead training, but thanks to the volunteer visits at the weekend she’s getting more familiar and confident. She loves being outside, watching the birds, rolling about in the grass and sniffing about in the dirt.

But, when she’s had her fun outdoors she is more than happy to chill out in her kennel, and she loves inching herself closer and closer to you until she’s finally resting in your lap. She has the mindset of a small dog and is definitely not aware of her size!

Taffy is a really good girl and we would love to see her shine in a new home where she has the focus, commitment and love she’s due. She is a wonderful character and will only continue to blossom.

name: Aslan
description:
Aslan is a two year old cross breed and he was brought into the shelter after he and other dog were found living as strays.

We don’t know how long they’d been there, but they were both in quite good condition and seemed quite streetwise, so we think they’d been close to somewhere where they were being fed regularly.

Although they were initially quite scared when they came in with the dog warden, within a few days they’d shaken off their nerves and settled in.

Aslan is a beautiful dog and really loves people. We’re hopeful this means that somewhere along the line, he’s been treated with kindness.

He is trusting, hugely affectionate, and very friendly towards new people, so the volunteers love spending time with him as he’s just the happiest boy all of the time.

We think that Aslan has spent a reasonable amount of time roaming free as quite a lot is new to him. He’s not familiar with the lead, so this is taking a bit of work to introduce him to, and he jumps up a lot, so we’re working on that too.

It comes from a place of love and he’s just wanting to be close, but he’s not a small dog so it would definitely be overwhelming for young children despite his good intentions!

When he’s outside in the yard, Aslan is on a mission to investigate everything and he loves to follow interesting smells, roll about in the grass and be a nosey neighbour.

He is very interested in everything going on around him, and it can sometimes he hard to get his attention so he needs plenty of time to potter about before you can work on training and focus.

Aslan currently shares his kennel with a female dog and although she wasn’t best pleased to be sharing her space when he arrived, he hasn’t once uttered a paw out of place, so she has accepted that he’s there to stay!

The pair of them now quite enjoy hanging out together sunbathing, and Aslan is very good at just co-existing. He is definitely quite a silly, clumsy dog, but his heart is definitely in the right place and he just wants to belong.

Aslan would be a lovely companion for a family based more semi-rurally with a garden, and with a calm home atmosphere but a fairly active lifestyle.

He would appreciate plenty of human or company, and we feel that he can live as the only resident dog. He’s a special boy and we know there’s someone out there missing their soul dog – here he is!

name: Poppy
description:
Sweet little Poppy is five years old and was brought into the vets shortly after having puppies.

She was never collected again by her family, and ended up being handed into the shelter by the vet who wanted to make sure she found a home that would treat her with the love and care she deserves.

She is expected to be around five years old and is just the most charming, silly little sausage.

Poppy can be a little bit shy with new people, especially men, but the way to her heart is via her favourite toys! Pick up her toysand it’s as though she’s known you forever.

She loves to play and is so funny and excitable, racing about all over the place and collecting them all up and placing them neatly in a pile. She will be in her element in a home where she has her very own basket of toys to rummage through every day!

Poppy is a very gentle girl and she loves affection. Once she trusts you, she likes to sit as close as physically possible and breathein your face while you stroke her ears.

She has a couple of missing, wonky teeth which only add to her adorable charm. She also likes to clutch onto your arm with both paws for the ultimate cuddle, but she does so very gently, so as not to be too bouncy. She’s just a real sweetheart.

Unfortunately, Poppy is positive for Leishmania, which is a chronic health condition caused by the bite of an infected sandfly.

Poppy’s condition is stable and she’s on the right medication to ensure she’s fit and healthy, but it is of course something for prospective adopters to consider, as she will need regular medication and monitoring.

Outwardly, she is very healthy, happy, in no pain and has a good appetite and a zest for life.

Poppy is fairly submissive and would be ideal for a calm home with someone who can shower her with fuss and attention. She gets along with other dogs, but doesn’t depend on them, and she would be great in a home with children too.

She loves to be close and you can just tell she is going to make such an amazing companion given the second chance she deserves. Her temperament is wonderful, and she has a heart of absolute gold.

name: Birdie
description:
Birdie is a one year old Shepherd mix and was brought in as yet another stray without a microchip, and no one ever came to the shelter to claim her.

She has settled in really well despite the busy, noisy environment, and she’s proving to be quite the superstar.

The first thing we noticed about Birdie shorty after she arrived was just how intelligent she is. She is very quick to learn, and given she knows some basic commands already we’re fairly convinced that she likes had a home at some point.

She knows to sit, give her paw (very enthusiastically), and she’s not far off with lie down. She is so keen to please and loves being rewarded with treats of any kind. She’s very serious when the treats come out, and she’s ready to impress!

At around a year old, Birdie is still only an adolescent dog, so is looking for an active home with a family keen to continue her training and socialisation.

She can be bouncy and bubbly around new people, so needs family that are confident handling a bigger dog. She means no harm at all, but she has lanky legs and clumsy paws at times!

Birdie is really good with other dogs. She shares her kennel with a male shepherd and has absolutely no problems sharing her space with him. She is happy eating near him, shows no resource guarding, and takes treats politely.

There’s no competition between the two of them, and we think she would get along well with another dog of a similar energy ad size in her new forever home. She is a confident dog though, and doesn’t depend on canine company.

Birdie is great with people and very sociable. She is always eager to greet new faces and loves to spend time out in the fields with the volunteers at the weekend.

She is getting better on the lead the most accustomed she gets to it, and we definitely think that she would be best suited to an active, outdoorsy home with a family who love exploring, long walks and adventures.

She would also prefer a home with direct access to a secure garden.

Birdie has heaps of love to give and will make such a loyal, loving companion in the right home. She would love a family to smother her in the love she craves, and she will definitely repay you with undying devotion.

Once she’s bonded with you, she’s bonded forever.

name: Amber
description:
Amber is a 6-month-old female Cross-Breed. She is one of four siblings who were found in the buffer zone, and she is now looking for a loving forever home. Despite her uncertain start, she remains a sweet and playful puppy who thrives on human companionship and attention.

Currently weighing 14 kg, Amber is expected to grow into a medium to large-sized dog once fully mature. She is learning to walk on a lead and is starting to understand some basic commands, making her a great candidate for continued training in her future home.

Amber can be rehomed as the only dog or alongside a resident dog. She has not been tested with cats, but given her young age, she could potentially adapt to living with them with slow and careful introductions.

She is also suitable for a home with children, making her an excellent family companion.

Amber is currently in Cyprus and is ready to fly to the UK. She will arrive with her dog passport, fully wormed, vaccinated, microchipped, and with blood tests completed. She also comes with full rescue support from Saving Souls.

If you are looking for an affectionate and trainable young dog, Amber could be the perfect addition to your home.

name: Sasha
description:
Sasha – 5 year old female Cross-Breed has been locked in the pound for three years, desperately waiting for her own family. She is the most loving dog with humans, making it even sadder that she spends all her time alone in a cage.

Sasha adores human companionship and is very friendly with people and children over five. She loves being petted, playing with toys, and going for walks.

She is medium-sized at 23kg with a short coat. However, Sasha does not get along with other dogs and must be the only pet in the home. It’s possible that the stress of being caged for so long has contributed to this.

Sasha is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in the UK. She will be neutered, vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, have her own pet passport, and have rescue back-up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Mosi
description:
Mosi is a 7-month-old female Labrador cross currently in Cyprus and looking for a loving home in the UK.

She was found in a pound at just three months old and has now spent four months waiting for her chance to experience a real home.

Mosi is a medium-sized dog, expected to reach around 20-25kg when fully grown. She is full of life, enjoys the company of both male and female dogs, and absolutely loves human attention.

While she hasn’t been tested with cats or children yet, this can be arranged for a serious adopter. Given her young age, she is likely to integrate well into a home with proper introductions and guidance.

Mosi will travel to the UK vaccinated, microchipped, treated for parasites, and with her own pet passport. She will also come with a neutering contract as she is still too young to be spayed.

If you are interested in offering Mosi the loving home she deserves, please get in touch with Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Layla
description:
Layla is a 7-month-old female Labrador cross currently in Cyprus and searching for a loving home in the UK.

She was found in a pound at just three months old and has now spent four months waiting for her chance at a better life.

Weighing around 12kg now, Layla is expected to grow into a medium-sized dog (20-25kg when fully grown).

She is full of life, adores human attention, and gets along well with both male and female dogs. While she hasn’t been tested with cats or children yet, this can be arranged for a serious adopter.

Given her young age, she is likely to adapt well to a variety of home environments with proper introductions.

Layla will travel to the UK vaccinated, microchipped, treated for parasites, and with her own pet passport. She will also come with a neutering contract as she is still too young to be spayed.

If you are interested in offering Layla the loving home she deserves, please get in touch with Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Tommy
description:
Tommy is a 2-year-old male Cross-Breed, currently in Cyprus and searching for a loving home in the UK. Weighing 19 kg, he is a medium-sized dog with a friendly and calm nature.

Despite his unfortunate circumstances, Tommy remains one of the happiest and most affectionate dogs, always greeting people with his signature smile.

At the moment, Tommy is living in a Pound where conditions are far from ideal. The enclosure is covered in tarpaulin, limiting his ability to see outside, and with only one volunteer caring for many dogs, he doesn’t get much time to roam freely.

However, even in these challenging conditions, Tommy’s spirit remains unbroken—he continues to be an incredibly friendly and social dog, always eager for attention.

Tommy gets along well with both people and other dogs, making him a great companion for a home with or without a resident dog. He is also good on the lead and enjoys car rides, which will make adventures with his future family all the more enjoyable.

While his behaviour around cats is unknown, he has shown he can live with children.

Tommy is neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, and treated for parasites. He will come with his own pet passport and full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

He is a wonderful boy who deserves a loving home where he can finally experience the warmth and care he has been missing.

name: Tobby
description:
Tobby is a 2-year-old Male Pointer Cross.

Tobby is a stunning young Pointer mix who has had a tough start in life. Initially shy when meeting new people, he is gaining confidence every day and is desperate for love and affection.

He is fantastic with children and other dogs, making him a wonderful companion for a family or an individual looking for a loyal friend.

He was previously in a noisy, stressful pound, but has now moved to a home boarding facility where he enjoys running and playing with other dogs in a more relaxed environment.

Tobby is still young and deserves a fresh start in a loving home. He can live with or without another dog, but his behaviour around cats is unknown.

He will travel to the UK with full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue. He will be neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, treated for parasites, and have his own pet passport.

name: Manos
description:
Manos is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed with hound traits. He is a small to medium-sized dog currently in Cyprus. When he first arrived, he was very weak, but he has since recovered well and is now a playful and energetic companion.

He has a friendly and affectionate nature, making him a joy to be around.

Manos is great with other dogs, getting along perfectly with them in social settings. He is also very respectful of children, making him a suitable family pet. One of his endearing traits is his slobbery affection, which adds to his charm.

He is well-behaved on the lead and enjoys travelling, making car journeys stress-free and enjoyable.

He will be neutered soon and is expected to be ready to fly on the May flight. Before travel, he will also undergo blood testing, microchipping, and worming, ensuring he is fully prepared for his new home.

Manos will arrive with his dog passport and full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue, guaranteeing support throughout his transition.

name: Lola
description:
*** LOLA WILL COME TO FOSTER IN BANSTEAD, SURREY, ON 13TH SEPTEMBER 2026.

Our extra special girl Lola is approximately five years old and a German Shepherd dog or thereabouts. Lola weighs twenty-five kilos and measures eighteen inches from shoulder to paw.

She was a much-loved dog by her family who had to leave the country under the most tragic circumstances. Hence Lola has been in our Cyprus shelter for over six months.

Our shelter manager describes Lola as highly intelligent, loving and loyal. She has the most delightful disposition and an adorable nature.

Lola responds to basic demands and will sit on demand. She will gaze at her food bowl until instructed to eat. Lola has settled really well into shelter life and has forged many endearing relationships.

Her amazing tricolour is beautifully enhanced by her white tips. Lola is an absolute star and the perfect adoption candidate for a very fortunate adopting family.

Lola walks nicely on her lead after a short period of excitement. She seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children. Lola is such a prize.

name: Reyna
description:
Reyna is an eight year old female Border Collie. Reyna was given to the shelter along with her three puppies (Ares, Sena and Zeus) by a family who kept her outside her whole life.

We think she’s been chained up for most of that time and hasn’t had the chance to interact with humans much or other dogs.

Reyna arrived at the shelter very scared with many fears and insecurities.

She is improving in time and allows people to give her attention and be stroked but she will need a patient and caring home that will let her confidence grow in her own time as she is very scared of things that are new to her.

Once she is familiar with people, she’s very sweet and affectionate

Reyna is currently at the shelter we work closely with in Northern Spain.

Reyna’s Spanish passport says she’s almost 8 years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Reyna a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Reyna is currently in Spain but she is ready to travel to her forever home in the UK.

name: Kyra
description:
Kyra is a 6 month old female Labrador Retriever Cross, currently in Cyprus, looking for a loving home in the UK.

Kyra is an absolutely gorgeous black Labrador cross. As a young pup, Kyra and her siblings were ripped away from their mum and dumped in a field by some monster.

There were 3 girls and 2 boys in the litter and they are all adorable. Kyra is one of the 3 little girls. She is 5/6 months old now.

Her brother Harley, who she was sharing a cage with, flew home last month and is doing so well. Piper has a home to go to. It would be amazing if Kyra could leave on the next flight with Piper.

She is dog friendly and people friendly and is a cuddly, playful puppy who desperately needs to swap a kennel cage for a loving home.Kyra is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in the UK.

She will be neutered, vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, have her own pet passport, and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Phoenix
description:
Phoenix, large female cross breed in Cyprus, 23 months old.

Phoenix and her 2 babies were found in an old abandoned chicken farm and she had made a big hole in the ground and was hiding her babies in there to keep them safe.

They went into a noisy pound and the babies were petrified so they came to Saving Souls .We think Phoenix is pointer cross litse hound.

She is a strong affectionate girl who loves cuddles .She is great with other dogs and very friendly and mixes daily with 30-40 other dogs with no issue.She is approx 25 kgs and because of her enthusiasm for everything would be better with older children only. She is 23 months now so she is still a young girl herself. Her babies are gone and she is left behind. I wouldn’t trust her with cats but with dogs she is 100%. She would love an active life with lots of walks.

Phoenix comes with full rescue back up from Saving Souls. She will also have her dog passport, blood work, microchip and wormed/flea’d.

name: Beau
description:
We were made aware of the 3 pointers at the over-flowing Pound, Ash, Dante and Cody. When we saw their videos we could see a dog that was skin and bones in the background, so we immediately asked about that dog too.

Even though we had no space, we agreed to take the 3 pointers and also 2 others in desperate need, we would somehow find a way.

That skinny dog in the background was Beau. He clearly wasn’t getting any food at the Pound. They only get fed a small amount and if you are a dominant dog then you don’t get any at all, all the other dogs eat it all.

We were worried he wouldn’t last the weekend and would die there at the Pound, so we took him straight away to our rescue kennels.

After some good food and proper care it didn’t take long for him to put on some weight and look the picture of heath.

He is a little shy initially but will soon learn to trust.

He is dog friendly and he deserves the best home now.

Beau is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in UK. He will be neutered, vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, have his own pet passport and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Brady
description:
We were made aware of the 3 pointers at the over-flowing Pound, Ash, Dante and Cody. When we saw their videos we could see 2 dogs that were skin and bones in the background, so we immediately asked about them too.

Even though we had no space, we agreed to take the 3 pointers and also 2 others in desperate need, we would somehow find a way.

One of the dogs in the background was Brady. They got fed very little and had no vet care. He is just 1 year old and is such a friendly baby it was unthinkable to leave him there with such an uncertain future.

With so many dogs at the Pound, we had to get him out before he was put to sleep.

After some good food and proper care it didn’t take long for him to put on some weight and look the picture of heath.

He is dog friendly and people friendly and knows nothing of how life should be.

Brady is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in UK. He will be neutered, vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, have his own pet passport and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Nicol
description:
Nicol was rescued from a horrendous pound in poor condition however following treatment she is now in perfect health.

She is nearly 6 and a half years old and about 25kg.

She is described as a greyhound cross lady.

She is very sweet dog who is friendly with everyone.

She does still pull a bit on the lead but is obedient and gentle. She loves to be with people and loves company and may suit an older retired couple.

Nicol is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in UK.

She will be vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, come with her own pet passport and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Paolo
description:
Paolo is a 1-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a happy-go-lucky young dog with a big personality and lots of energy. Found in Cyprus, Paolo is small in size, weighing just under 9.5kg, and is now looking for his forever home.

He is described as smart, full of life, and always ready for an adventure. Paolo enjoys playtime in the yard and absolutely loves long walks, making him a great fit for an active family who can keep up with his lively nature.

Paolo walks well on the lead and is currently learning some basic commands. His enthusiasm and eagerness to please make him a fun dog to train. He would thrive in a home that offers both physical and mental stimulation.

He is good with other dogs and can be rehomed either as the only dog or alongside a friendly resident dog. While his behaviour around cats is unknown, he is still young and could potentially adapt with careful introductions.

Paolo is also suitable to live with respectful children. He comes with full rescue back-up from Saving Souls and is ready to travel to the UK once his forever home is found.

name: Oshi
description:
Oshi is an 18-month-old male Belgian Shepherd Malinois. He was found wandering near a highway in Cyprus, and despite his uncertain past, he has shown signs of being accustomed to home life.

His clean kennel habits suggest he was previously house-trained, as he waits to be let out before relieving himself.

Oshi is a new arrival, so his full temperament is still being assessed. However, he has shown no signs of reactivity to other dogs. He could be rehomed as an only dog or with a resident dog, depending on the adopter’s circumstances. His calm nature and adaptability indicate that he has the potential to thrive in a loving home.

Due to his size and strength, Oshi is best suited for a household with children aged 12 years and above. He has not been tested with cats, so his compatibility with feline companions is unknown. Any potential introductions to cats would need to be done carefully and gradually.

Oshi walks well on the lead, making him an excellent companion for an active adopter who can provide him with regular exercise and mental stimulation.

As a Belgian Shepherd Malinois, he will need an owner familiar with the breed’s intelligence and energy levels to ensure he remains engaged and well-balanced.

Oshi is fully vaccinated, microchipped, wormed, and comes with a pet passport. He is ready to fly to the UK and will arrive with full rescue backup from Saving Souls Animal Rescue, ensuring support for his adopter.

name: (Deceased) Holly
description:
Holly – 8 year old female American Bulldog is a gorgeous girl with striking eyes!

Holly came to us as a welfare case, so we have very little history available on her. She has shown herself to be a laid-back and friendly girl with people, good with her basic commands, and walks nicely on lead.

She enjoys a treat and especially playing ball. Sadly, she is very stressed in kennels and is currently reacting to other dogs in that environment. We may find this improves in a home environment.

Holly would be best suited to being an only dog in a household with experience of large breed dogs. Given her size and the limited background we have on her, we’d prefer older children only. She is not cat tested.

Holly is neutered and microchipped and is currently completing her vaccinations.

If you would like to meet Holly, she is currently situated just outside Sheffield. We’d love to hear from you.

name: Morits
description:
What’s worse than seeing puppies growing up in the shelter cage?….older dogs living out their days in the shelter cage, when time on this planet is running out for them.

Meet Morits – A Gentle Soul Ready for His Second Chance

Morits has spent eight long years longing for something many of us take for granted: love, warmth, and a place to call home.

Morits was found living in a field with his brother about 3 years ago and they were taken in by Roberts Dog Sanctuary. His brother has since been rehomed but Morits now waits alone in a shelter in Cyprus, his big heart full of hope.

At his age he should be living in comfort, not sleeping on cold concrete floors.

This handsome boy may be 8, but he still has so much life and love to give. He walks beautifully on the lead and would make the perfect companion for peaceful strolls or quiet afternoons by your side.

Morits is gentle with female dogs and, with the right introduction, could share his space with a calm male friend.

Because of his size, he’s best suited to a home with older children who will respect his need for kindness and calm.

Morits is healthy, ready to travel, and most importantly ready to love. After years of surviving in the shadows, he deserves a retirement filled with soft beds, gentle hands, and a family to call his own.

Give Morits the ending he deserves. Let him show you just how deeply a rescued heart can love.

Morits is currently in Cyprus looking for a home in UK. He will be neutered, vaccinated, chipped, treated for parasites, have his own pet passport and rescue back up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue.

name: Blake
description:
Blake is a 3 year old male Labrador Retriever Cross, currently being fostered in Bulgaria and ready to travel to his forever home.

Medium-to-large in size at around 27 kilograms, Blake has the soulful eyes and gentle nature that make him instantly lovable.

He had a rough start in life, but you’d never guess it from his joyful personality. Blake greets every day with enthusiasm — always up for a walk, a game, or a cuddle.

He’s playful, social, and full of positive energy. His goofy side shines when he’s running around with his doggy friends or flopping over for belly rubs.

This clever boy is quick to learn and loves both mental stimulation and human attention. He’s great on the lead, good in the car, and loves outdoor adventures — the perfect fit for an active person or family who enjoys spending time outside.

Blake gets along wonderfully with other dogs and is friendly with children. Cats can be tested on request. His ideal home would be one where he’s included in daily activities, given plenty of exercise, and surrounded by love and structure.

With the right family, Blake will grow into an extraordinary, loyal companion.

He is neutered, fully vaccinated, microchipped, vet-checked, and travels with an EU pet passport and full DEFRA-approved paperwork.

Blake is patiently waiting for a family to see the wonderful dog he truly is — and to give him the loving forever home he deserves.

name: Dixie
description:
Dixie is a 2 year old female medium mixed breed currently in Warwickshire. She is not yet spayed on previous veterinary advice.

Dixie is looking for a new home due to a change in her owner’s circumstances which means she is being left for long periods.

Dixie is an intelligent and active dog who enjoys outdoor environments, particularly countryside walks and time near water. She is playful and energetic, and benefits from regular physical and mental stimulation.

She forms strong bonds with her primary person but can be wary of unfamiliar people. She requires slow, structured introductions and time to build trust. Once comfortable, she is affectionate and loyal.

Dixie walks well on lead but may pull initially or when distracted by wildlife or other dogs. She enjoys the company of medium and large dogs and can play in an energetic manner. She is not suitable to live with small dogs.

She can become overwhelmed in busy environments and may show reactive behaviour towards people approaching her, particularly on lead or near the car. She has been muzzle trained and has undergone training to support her behaviour. An experienced adopter is required.

Dixie is fully housetrained and settles well in the home. She can be left for periods once settled and benefits from a calm, structured routine.

She can show guarding behaviours around food and space, so management and understanding of these behaviours will be important.

Dixie would suit an experienced, adult-only home in a quieter or rural environment. A home with other medium to large, well-balanced dogs may help her confidence.

She will require an adopter committed to ongoing training, clear boundaries and gradual confidence-building.

name: Ally
description:
Ally is a four year old German Shepherd mix. Poor Ally came into the shelter over a year ago after being rescued running scared in the roads.

She was so sad in the shelter when she first arrived and would sit by the kennel bars and cry for hours.

We think she has previously had a family and was desperate for them to come and get her, but of course that never happened, and months later she’s still without a home to call her own.

Ally is a lovely dog who through no fault of her own has just been overlooked time and time again. By nature she’s an active, intelligent and very loyal girl.

She’s eager to please and is so bored in the shelter, so she would thrive in an active home with someone who wants to explore with the company of a canine best friend.

Shepherds have great stamina, so long hikes and camping holidays will be no problem for a dog like Ally – she’d love it! She’d also love any kind of training, as she loves to please and learning new things is great fun for intelligent breeds like herself.

Ally shares her kennel with another dog and although she seems to enjoy his company, it’s clear that humans are her first love.

She is content around other dogs, happily to walking alongside them when outside the shelter and sharing her space with them, but we feel she would be fine either with or without a resident dog to live with.

Ally’s ideal home would have a garden where she can let off some steam and stretch her legs, but even if her garden is small as long as she’s based outside of the city surrounded by plenty of places to explore, she’ll be happy.

We have no doubt that she will be so loyal to her new family, but she may have some separation anxiety to overcome due to her abandonment based on her behaviour in the shelter.

With patience, reassurance, routine and consistency this is something that can be overcome, and who can blame her for feeling worried after experiencing being dumped before?

Ally would love a family home where she can experience the security of feeling loved, wanted, and a sense of belonging.

She has a soft heart and although her abandonment should have broken her trust in people, she’s been nothing but forgiving and resilient. We would love for her to find the family she’s been waiting so long for.

name: Rico
description:
Rico is a 4-year-old male Spanish Bodeguero. This handsome and lively boy comes from a breed originally known for guarding Spanish bodegas, where families stored wine, sherry, and cheeses.

The Bodeguero’s role was to keep the area safe and free from rats — a task that shaped them into intelligent, alert, and loyal companions.

True to his breed, Rico is hardy, active, and full of personality, making him an excellent pet for anyone who loves an energetic and affectionate dog.

Once someone’s cherished pet, Rico was sadly abandoned and found himself in a pound. Thankfully, he’s now safe and cared for, showing just how adaptable and resilient he is.

He’s lead trained, house trained, and wonderfully social with both people and other dogs. Rico’s friendly and confident nature shines through in every interaction, and he’s eager to please those around him.

Rico is fully vaccinated, health checked, microchipped, and neutered, and he also holds a full EU passport, meaning he’s ready to travel to his new home.

He’s an affectionate, outgoing dog who thrives on human connection and activity — whether that’s a long walk, playtime in the garden, or simply spending time with his people.

Rico deserves a loving family who’ll give him the security and companionship he’s been missing and who’ll let his bright, loyal personality truly shine.

name: Harry
description:
Harry is a 9 year old male Cross-Breed who came into care after being rescued from a wild plot of land, where he was living under some bushes.

He was extremely scared and presented with various infected wounds. After some months in care, he has lost his initial fear (he was also helped greatly by the amazing ladies who found him).

Though he is still shy with people until he realises they are not going to hurt him, once he knows you, he will not leave your side.

Harry is medium active. He loves to run but in moderation. He is good with the other dogs at the shelter and enjoys playing and digging.

Harry loves his food and will need to be on a controlled diet to maintain his weight. He is 48 cm tall and weighs approximately 18 kg.

All of the dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme, and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons not to do so, will be sterilised. Harry is neutered. Medical results and treatments will be advised upon successful application.

An adoption contract and fee, home check, and lifetime rescue back-up apply as standard.

name: Gomez
description:
Gomez moved into private boarding kennels in July 2025 where he has resided ever since.

After months in a busy kennel block Gomez was becoming stressed. He was reactive to other dogs when walking the kennel line with staff. He was moved to a quieter area where he has now relaxed more and has become a much calmer dog.

Gomez accepts collar/harness and lead but he can try and bite the lead sometimes. He walks really well on the lead with no pulling. He can be a little scared of some people and does bark at dogs he sees. He has not met any children on his walks.

Gomez has been known to tear up his bed with boredom so he will need lots of toys and brain games to keep him busy in his new home. He will also need to get daily physical exercise on walks.

Gomez has probably been left without food in the past so he snatched food and treats from your hand. The kennels have tried to teach him to be gentle. This is something that his new home will need to be aware of and work with him to continue this training.

As Gomez has been living in kennels his toilet training will need a refresher in his new home which will be easily done with a clear, scheduled toileting routine.

As he has spent a long period of time in kennels Gomez will need someone around most of the day. This is so that he can build a bond with his new family.

Any alone time will need to be built up very gradually over time and monitored to ensure Gomez is comfortable being left alone. He may be susceptible to separation anxiety once he has settled in.

Gomez will need an experienced home who can offer him what he needs but take things at his own pace as he will need some adjustment time when he comes out of the kennels.

Gomez will need to be walked on a harness and be given some additional positive training with sights and sounds he hasn’t seen for a while.

Gomez has a lot of love to give and is a good boy. He is now ready to find his forever home where he will be given patience, time, reassurance and be allowed to decompress after a long period in a kennel environment.

He needs someone with experience to guide him, show him what is expected of him using positive reinforcement and give him all the love he has missed out on.

He needs to go at his own pace to ensure he is comfortable with the positive life changes he is experiencing.

name: Laika
description:
Liaka is a ten year old female Brittany. Laika is quite a small Brittany, very active and energetic for her age. She is very sociable with other dogs and lives in a kennel with a Setter, with whom she shares space and food without any problems.

Laika is very obedient when called within the confines of the shelter (it could be different on an exciting walk), she likes to lie quietly in her bed, and also enjoys running in the enclosure.

Laika has a cheerful temperament and is very affectionate and attached to people. She is a great all round dog.

Laika is a beautiful girl. She was given up by a hunter when no longer any use to him. Laika is now at the shelter we closely with in North Spain ready for a new life in the UK

If you are interested in giving wonderful Laika a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Laika is in Spain and ready to travel to her forever home. Will that be with you?

name: Jensen
description:
Jensen is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He has been in foster care since arriving in the UK last December and is now ready to find his forever home.

Described as a handsome boy, Jensen has a sweet-natured and friendly personality that makes him very endearing to the people around him.

He is a medium-sized dog with a strong, stocky build, giving him a sturdy and solid appearance. Jensen clearly enjoys human company and thrives on interaction, showing a loving and sociable temperament.

His fondness for people makes him a great companion in a home where he can receive plenty of attention.

Jensen is good with children, although a home with older children aged 12 and above would be more suitable for him.

This recommendation likely reflects his strength and energy levels, ensuring safe and comfortable interactions for everyone involved. He is an active dog who enjoys his walks and benefits from regular exercise to keep him happy and healthy.

His lead training is still ongoing, but he is an intelligent dog who is already beginning to pick up new commands. With continued consistency and patience, he is expected to improve further and become even more well-mannered on the lead.

He is also doing well with recall, which is a promising sign of his responsiveness and willingness to learn.

Jensen would do best as the only dog in the home, as he prefers not to share his space with other dogs. Additionally, he is not suitable to live with cats.

These preferences should be considered carefully to ensure he is placed in an environment where he can feel secure and relaxed.

He is currently in foster in Fleet, giving potential adopters in that area or nearby regions the opportunity to meet him. Jensen is looking for a home that can match his energy, continue his training, and provide him with the companionship he clearly enjoys.

name: Bairon
description:
Bairon is a 1 year old male English Setter. He is currently in Spain after being given up by a hunter who no longer wanted him for hunting. Despite this start, Bairon has maintained a cheerful and playful personality that really reflects his young age.

He is an active dog with plenty of energy, so he will need a home that can keep up with his lively nature. Like most young setters, he enjoys movement, play, and stimulation, making him a great match for an active household.

His medium size makes him manageable, but his energy means he will thrive with regular exercise and engagement.

Bairon shares his kennel with another young dog, and the two get along very well, playing and eating together without any issues.

This shows he is sociable and comfortable around other dogs. He is also very confident with people and enjoys affection, making him an easy companion to bond with.

He would fit into most homes that are prepared for a young and energetic dog. With the right environment, Bairon is likely to flourish and become a loyal and fun-loving family member. Transport to the UK is available for the right home.

name: Rodney
description:
Rodney is a small to medium sized crossbreed aged around four years old.Rodney – fostered in Norwich Norfolk.

Rodney was abandoned outside the shelter at Crivatu with his siblings four years ago. Three of the litter came to the UK as pups but sadly two remained.

As nice as the shelter at Crivatu is it’s not a substitute for a real home and family and we are so hoping that at last Rodney will get his chance.

Rodney is a friendly little chap who loves a cuddle and is very much a lap dog. He enjoys his walks and is well behaved when out. He could live with another female dog but would be very happy to be the only dog in the home. He needs an adult home.

name: Reuben
description:
Reuben is a 2.5 year old male Cross-Breed with a huge personality! Full of energy, charm, and cheeky prince-like confidence, he quickly wins hearts.

Playful, athletic, and loving, Reuben enjoys long walks, games, cuddles, and showing off his tricks! He knows sit, paw on both sides, high five, and his brilliant “meerkat” trick.

He loves people and children, plays well with other dogs, and appears comfortable around cats. He would suit an active family or couple who can provide walks, play, training, mental stimulation, and companionship.

Reuben is toilet trained and can be left for appropriate periods after plenty of exercise. He can be cheeky and needs calm, consistent boundaries when overstimulated, plus positive reassurance.

A secure garden or easy access to safe outdoor space would be ideal. Further training would benefit this clever boy.

Reuben is handsome, funny, loving, and incredibly loyal. He’s ready to find his forever family!

name: Lucio
description:
Lucio is a 2-year-old small male German Shepherd type Cross. This handsome boy has already been through a great deal, having spent more than a year of his life locked up in a cage while waiting for his chance at a better life.

That chance eventually came, and Lucio flew to the UK on 19 April, where he is now waiting for his forever home.

Lucio is currently staying in kennels in Preesal, Lancashire. Before coming to the UK, he lived at a shelter in Cyprus, where he became a particular favourite of one of the volunteer’s daughters.

She could not understand why such a lovely dog was still waiting for a home.

Described as affectionate and cheerful, Lucio also has a very clever personality. He responds well to the right guidance and is able to adjust nicely when given the support and direction he needs.

His combination of intelligence and affectionate nature makes him a dog who will benefit from an experienced and committed home.

Lucio is looking for either an experienced foster home or a forever home, with foster-to-adopt also being considered. His new family should be active and able to meet both his physical and mental needs.

He will need people who are prepared to give him the guidance and activity he needs as he continues adjusting to life in the UK.

Lucio cannot live with cats. He can live with female dogs or could be the only dog in the household, giving potential adopters a couple of suitable options when considering his future home.

He can live with children aged 10 and over, provided they are dog-savvy. His new family should therefore be comfortable managing his needs while ensuring that any children in the household understand how to interact appropriately with him.

Lucio has already had several important aspects of his care completed. He is neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, and has been treated for parasites, and he also has his own pet passport.

Lucio also has rescue back-up from Saving Souls Animal Rescue. After spending so much of his early life waiting for an opportunity, he is now looking for the permanent home where he can finally enjoy life as a much-loved family companion.

An experienced and active family willing to continue supporting him could give Lucio the chance to settle into the happy future he has been waiting for.

name: Ivan
description:
Ivan is a one year old Greek Harehound, and unfortunately he is looking for a new home as soon as possible. He arrived in the UK in June 2025 at the age of five months old, and has been in a loving, supportive home since then.

But very sadly, the arrival of a baby has led to Ivan being relinquished back into our care. Our deadline to find Ivan a foster home is the middle of May, and if we’re unable to do so he will have to go into kennels.

Due to the significant life changes his family are going through, Ivan has not been given adequate attention or training over recent months.

With his family now functioning on reduced sleep, they have admitted that they no longer have the time for him and that he’s spending more and more time in his crate.

All of this change has resulted in his behaviour deteriorating as he’s found situations more overwhelming to deal with. We recognise that his environment is also not the most conducive to his needs, and this too plays a role in him needing a new home.

Ivan is looking for a semi-rural home where he has more space, a nice garden to run about in, and a family who understands hounds. He is currently living in London and is struggling with the suburban surroundings.

There are a lot of factors that he finds overwhelming and this is causing pent up frustration and anxiety. He would be much happier outside of the city where he can enjoy long walks in green spaces.

Ivan needs some time to reset, adjust to a new environment, and decompress. He is extremely food motivated, which really helps with training, and he has learnt a few tricks too.

He is also housetrained and crate trained, but does unfortunately struggle with the car which needs some continued desensitisation training.

In true hound fashion, Ivan is incredibly affectionate with his family, loves a snuggle on the sofa, and is happiest when chasing after a ball.

He’s an energetic boy and needs an active home, but he also responds well to mental stimulation and enrichment with his food, such as stuffed kongs and scatter feeding.

Ivan’s main struggles relate to reactivity and anxiety. Before leaving the shelter and in his initial UK foster home, Ivan was brilliant with other dogs and socialised with males and females of a variety of ages.

Unfortunately this hasn’t been the case since being adopted, and he is now very selective with other dogs. It is possible that in a calmer environment this may improve, and he has had good relationships with mature female dogs.

Although Ivan currently lives with a newborn and has been very adaptable to the new arrival, we’re looking for a home with older children simply to keep his environment a bit more predictable and relaxed.

Ivan is looking for a family that can give him the time, patience and training to settle in at his own pace.

We feel a change of environment will really be integral in supporting his onward progress, and we won’t be considering urban homes given his struggles in London.

We know how loving, sweet natured and friendly Ivan can be and we’re looking for a home where he can enjoy lots of adventures, a calm home atmosphere, and has the attention and understanding of a more experienced adopter.

name: Shire
description:
Shire is a ten month old female mixed breed dog, born in May 2025, and weighing around twenty kilograms. She is currently located in Glasgow and is fully vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, and in good health.

Shire is a beautiful young dog with a gentle and sensitive nature. She is playful, curious, and affectionate, and she enjoys being close to her people and sharing calm, cuddly moments.

She can be slightly shy in unfamiliar environments or when meeting new people, but with patience and reassurance, she begins to relax and show her sweet and loving character.

She will benefit from a calm and understanding home that allows her to build confidence at her own pace.

Shire is still learning about the world and would be best suited to a home with prior experience with rescue dogs.

She will need adopters who can provide structure, consistency, and gentle guidance, helping her feel safe and secure as she settles into her new life.

Shire is a kind, affectionate, and truly beautiful young dog who is ready to find a patient and loving home where she can feel safe, grow in confidence, and truly belong.

name: Leo
description:
Leo is a 9 month old male Cross-Breed, expected to grow into a medium to large-sized adult. He is currently fostered in Bulgaria and is ready to travel to the United Kingdom once the right home is found.

Leo is fully vaccinated, microchipped, clinically healthy, and has tested negative for Brucellosis and routine veterinary diseases. He is still too young to be neutered.

Leo’s story is one of incredible resilience. As a very young puppy, he was hit by a car and left alone on the roadside for two weeks. When he was finally rescued, he was in critical condition with a severely broken leg.

Because too much time had passed, surgery was not possible. Despite this, Leo showed remarkable strength and determination. With veterinary care, rest, and rehabilitation, his leg healed into a functional position, and he is now able to walk, play, and enjoy life.

Today, Leo is an exceptionally social, affectionate, and happy young dog. He absolutely loves people and thrives on human companionship. He is playful, funny, and enjoys being part of everyday activities with his carers.

Leo is very good with other dogs and enjoys their company. He is also cat friendly and has been exposed to other animals, showing a calm and balanced temperament.

He walks perfectly on the lead, travels well, and has perfect hygiene habits.

Leo would suit a loving home that can offer him companionship, continued guidance, and a secure environment.

He has a wonderful temperament and will make a loyal and devoted companion to the family who gives him the second chance he truly deserves. Leo is exceptionally smart and eager to learn.

He will sut perfectly active people who are interested in dog training.

Leo is now ready to leave his difficult past behind and begin a new life with a family who will love and protect him forever.

name: Kevin
description:
Kevin is a one year old Pointer/Labrador mix who was brought into the shelter as a stray by the dog warden at the very beginning of the year.

He was quite shellshocked to start with and very overwhelmed by all the noise and comings and goings at the shelter, but within a week he had really found his feet, made some friends, and settled in well.

Kevin is a young dog at only around a year old, and is an active, hilarious and affectionate boy. He is also really beautiful (his pictures don’t do I’m justice!) but has so far been overlooked, most likely because he really does just blend in at the shelter.

It’s so much harder to get the black dogs noticed, and Kevin hasn’t been so lucky just yet.

During the past few months though, he’s taken the opportunity to make friends with lots of other dogs and due to his sociable, adaptable nature, he’s been integrated into lots of different groups.

He currently shares a kennel with a group of siblings (males and females) who have just about accepted him as one of their own! He loves to play and really gets along with other pups of a similar nature to him.

Kevin is still really only a puppy and has a bouncy, energetic nature, and is still learning every day.

He would really benefit from some basic training to work on some entry level commands and manners, and because he’s so keen to please we think he will respond really well.

He is food motivated, but also very play motivated too, and he absolutely loves to chase after a ball or run around with a toy in the yard!

The ideal home for Kevin would be an active, semi-rural home with a family who enjoy spending time outdoors, understand that a young dog needs training and direction, and are looking for a dog to really be a part of their everyday lives.

Kevin loves being with people, and can sometimes be whiney, so we think that he could potentially struggle with some separation anxiety in the early days.

Although Kevin is great with other dogs, as long as he has plenty of human company during the day we think that he would be happy enough living on his own.

He would still benefit from opportunities to socialise and interact with other dogs though, such as at day-care or on group walks. This will continue to help him grow into a balanced boy with good social skills.

Kevin is super loving and adores human affection, so we would love to see him find the outdoorsy family he deserves.

He will make an excellent companion on long walks and adventures, and he’s so ready to get out of the shelter and enjoy a new and exciting lease of life.

name: Charlie
description:
Charlie is a young, friendly, cross-breed, medium-sized dog, around 12 months old. He has beautiful, speckled markings and a gentle, eager-to-please nature.

He is breed, likely spaniel crossed with pointer, and weighs around 10 kg. He was found wandering alone but has made excellent progress in foster care and is ready for a committed home.

Charlie is friendly with other dogs and may bark when he first sees them, but his tail is wagging and he is keen to make friends.

He can be a little nervous when meeting new people for the first time, but he warms up quickly, especially if offered a small treat. He lives with two confident cats who tend to bully him.

He will chase if a cat runs, so a home with dog-savvy or confident cats is best. He is affectionate, enjoys human company and responds well to praise and reassurance.

He loves children and enjoys their company. He is still young and may occasionally mouth hands, but he is improving with consistent guidance.

He enjoys outings and behaves well in public places. He loves visiting Pets at Home and will sit politely for a sausage after breakfast at the garden centre.

He may occasionally bark in the garden, but he is learning to be quiet and will come when called. He settles quickly when asked to sit and given calm reassurance. Charlie has made good training progress.

He has good recall in an enclosed park and will come when called, and he is practising this in other environments which are more distracting. He is used to wearing a lead but still needs guidance to walk nicely and not pull on the shorter lead.

He is mostly clean in the home but may still have the occasional accident. He has learned sit, wait, down, get down and paw. He takes food gently and waits politely for his meals.

He enjoys playing with a ball, even if returning it is optional. Charlie would be best suited to a home with children aged five and over and a secure private garden.

He is better as an only dog, as he prefers one-to-one attention and forms strong bonds with his people. Dog-savvy cats are suitable. He needs an active home that enjoys walking, training and outdoor time.

He loves running in open secure fields and would suit a family who can offer regular exercise and enrichment.

name: Brandon
description:
Brandon has to be on the next flight. He’s 3 years old and when he arrived at the shelter last year he was emaciated. He was nothing but skin and bone.

Completely starved and mistreated. We suspect he was a hunters dog – made to go hungry to ‘make him a better hunter’. Brandon is a pointer and ready to find his forever home.

Unfortunately Brandon entered the shelter nearly a year ago. He has been well cared for and did initially put on some weight. But the stress of being caged up all day has got to him and he has lost weight again.

That’s why we need him in a home asap. He’s struggling. Perhaps he once knew a home and had a family. He can be fostered or adopted.

Brandon is friendly and curious of everyone he meets. He’s happy to be getting regular meals, but what he really needs now is a human to give him the life he deserves.

He enjoys any time he gets to spend with people. He’s super cuddly – true to the pointer breed.

He shares a space with both male and female dogs of similar size and can be homed as an only dog or with females and/or submissive male dogs.

After initial excitement to be out of his kennel, Brandon walks well on the lead. He is super (!) food oriented and will be a joy to train.

Overall, Brandon simply adores people and would also be ok with children aged 10+.

Brandon is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Barney
description:
Another day, another black dog. This boy is Barney & he is approx 2 years old. He is only medium sized cross-breed. He is currently in some private kennels in Cyprus after being found as a stray.

When he arrived, he lost quite a bit of weight through stress. He is also super clean in his kennel. Perhaps both signs that he was in a home and loved before?

Barney is only young, so he has energy to burn. He needs to get out of the kennel environment so he can live out what’s left of his youth. He cannot live with male dogs but is good with females. Equally he would be ok as an only dog.

Barney would suit most home situations – a single person, a couple, a family…

He relishes at any opportunity to engage with humans. Even at the vets he is just excited to be around people. Let’s find him his forever family so his life can start.

Due to the time he has spent in kennels, his vet fees are sponsored, so we are only asking for his travel costs to be covered.

Barney is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Loco
description:
It was sad to see that, after I last saw Loco 6 months ago, he still hasn’t been adopted and is still stressed. Loco is such a joy to be around. But he has that heartbreaking look in his eyes pleading you to help him.

Wondering what he’s done wrong. He’s very affectionate and a bit goofy at times.

Loco is medium sized and approx 2.5-3 years old and the shelter have been working on his leash training, sit, and down. This boy thrives on love and reassurance.

Any fosterer or adopter needs to be willing to put the work in to train him (he’s very food oriented) – as is standard for any rescue dog.

We don’t know about Loco’s background but we do know that the situation he has found himself in is very upsetting for him. This leads us to believe that he once knew not only a home but perhaps a proper family.

Any children should be 10+ due to Loco’s strength. Even though he is only medium sized, he is a strong boy.

If he is to be homed with another dog then they need to be female or a non-dominant male. He currently shares his kennel with a female.

Loco is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Floki (Flopy)
description:
Flopy (Floki del Valle de Duero) is a male two year old German Wirehaired Pointer. He is a wonderful boy; tall, strong and athletic with a slender, elegant body and beautiful honey coloured eyes.

Floki is a truly special dog looking for an active, loving home where he can thrive. He’s a joy to have around—affectionate and full of personality.

Loving and affectionate – he absolutely thrives on human attentionAbsolutely loves the great outdoors, he is very active and intelligent, he enjoys his exercise and training sessionsRecall training is going well, of course this will need continual work and reinforcementWalks quite well on the lead, especially after a good runExcellent in the house – usually calm, clean, and no food guarding

Floki is incredibly likeable and easy to live with. He enjoys being part of family life and settles well indoors. He may occasionally carry off socks or gloves, but never destroys anything—just his quirky charm!

He mixes well with dogs both at home and out on walks, although he may vocalise if barked at when on lead or react in stressful situations.

Floki, like most GWP, is an active dog who needs a home that can offer plenty of exercise and stimulation. He’s used to lots of exercise and training and enjoys being involved in activities, including group walks and training sessions.

He currently eats well but struggles to gain weight.

Floki is a gorgeous, affectionate, and fun companion who is an absolute pleasure to spend time with. If you’re looking for a loyal, active, intelligent and loving dog to join your life, Floki could be the perfect match.

Floki would love a rural home with lots of space and opportunity to stretch the legs

Floki was given up by his Spanish hunter because he was very keen on eating the catch, rather than returning it to his hunter!

If you are interested in giving wonderful Floki, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Flopy is currently in Hereford Essex.

name: Astra
description:
Hi everyone! Let me introduce myself: my name is Astra.I’m an 8 month old female hound cross, 22 kgs when adult.

I am very sweet and ready to grow up strong and loyal alongside my future family.

Like all puppies, I have lots of energy, curiosity and a great desire to discover the world, learn new things and live a thousand adventures with someone who has time, patience and lots of love to give me.

Unfortunately, my life didn’t start in the best way: I was found on the street and taken to a kennel together with my little sisters.

I am now locked in a cage, when instead I should be running on the grass, playing, exploring and discovering real life.

Despite everything, I haven’t lost trust: as soon as someone comes close, I immediately look for cuddles and attention, hoping that one day they will be meant just for me.

I am urgently looking for adoption or even a temporary foster home that will allow me to leave the kennel and finally start a new life.

Please help me, I’m the last one left of the litter in the kennel, I’m really suffering a lot.

name: Son
description:
Son, is a three year old male German Shorthaired Pointer. Son is a very handsome GSP, he is a spectacular dog, large and elegant in stature.

He is clearly a sensitive soul and was very fearful when he arrived at the shelter we work closely with in North Spain. He trembled and tried to move away in an extremely submissive manner.

However in the short time he has been at the shelter he is already improvement in his confidence.

Son loves the companionship of female dogs and they have helped his confidence no end. Son is still wary of other male dogs so he would fit most easily in a home with a female dog companion.
