Son has a good appetite, is easy to handle as fear makes him so submissive. Son is looking for an understanding home with people and dogs that can bring out the wonderful dog hidden behind the anxious face.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Son a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Son is in Spain and is ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Enzo
description:
Enzo is a two year old male Jagd Terrier. Enzo is a really gorgeous boy. The Jagd Terrier is not often seen in the UK but might be most similar to the Fox Terrier.

Enzo is a looking for his forever home after being given up by a hunter as he was deemed unsuitable for hunting life. Now, he’s ready to leave that past behind and become a much-loved companion.

Weighing just 11 kg, Enzo may be small, but he has a big positive personality. He’s cheerful, playful, and constantly on the move, always sniffing, exploring, and enjoying everything around him.

His lively nature makes him a great match for someone with an active lifestyle who can keep up with his energy.

He is very sociable with other dogs, though confident and strong-willed. He has a brilliant, fun-loving nature, extremely affectionate and attached.

With people, Enzo is truly adorable. He is incredibly affectionate, deeply attached, and loves nothing more than being close to his humans.

He’ll happily follow you everywhere, always ready for cuddles and gentle attention, forming a strong and loyal bond.

Enzo is already very obedient when called within the safety of the shelter we closely with in North Spain, which shows great promise. However, he will need continued recall training before being allowed off lead in open areas to ensure his safety.

Enzo is looking for a home that can offer him plenty of activity, patience, and love. In return, he will give endless companionship, affection, and joy.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Enzo a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Enzo is in Spain and ready to travel to his forever home in the UK. Will that be with you?

name: Kane
description:
Kane is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed. He is currently in Cheshire.

He is a goofy boy with a cheeky personality which everyone loves.

Kane enjoys cuddles with the people he trusts and would love nothing more than to be a lapdog (despite his size).

Kane is very food orientated and will do anything for some treats, even if it means stealing them!

He loves to play and will often entertain himself with his toys and he loves to be kept mental stimulated with Kongs and lick mats.

Kane needs an adult only and cat free home.

He could live with dogs given slow and sensible introductions and the ability to separate.

Kane accepts a collar, harness and lead and loves his walks. However, he is reactive if there are other people or dogs around.

Kane prefers to walk in quieter areas like the woods. He is very strong on the lead although his current family are working on this with him and he is making great progress.

Kane is very obedient and will stop at roads when asked and listens to the touch command.

He can be noise sensitive to the outside world such as postmen and car doors shutting which can make him anxious.

Kane is reactive towards strangers in the home therefore will need a quieter home with minimal visitors.

Kane still displays puppy behaviours and can mouth and nip during play, this will need to be worked on by his future home and he will need to be kept active and mentally stimulated to keep his mind busy.

Kane is toilet trained. Kane is not crate trained.

He has only been left for short periods at a time.

Kane is okay in the car but has only been for short journeys.

name: Mona
description:
Mona is a 6 month old female Shepherd cross. She is currently living in a foster home in Leeds and is available for meets and greets with potential adopters.

Mona weighs 12kg now and is not expected to grow larger than 20-25kg. This sweet girl has been through a lot of hardship since she came into the world and would love to find a home and family to call her own.

She was born in a work yard in Sarajevo, Bosnia in the middle of winter, and has survived almost freezing to death, serious illness, and being chased by dog catchers.

Sadly, she lost half her tail before she was rescued, and she was in a lot of pain at the time. Fortunately, it doesn’t cause her any discomfort now and she loves to wag it!

Despite everything she’s been through, she is so very, sweet, loving and gentle. She is still a puppy and loves to play and run around! Mona lives in a foster home with other dogs, and she could live with another dog (or dogs) or as an only dog.

Mona is doing really well in her foster home and is learning what it’s like to feel safe, get regular meals and treats, as well as going on short walks discovering the outside world.

She loves her cuddles and will snuggle up next to you for reassurance and love. Mona has also discovered the joy of toys, and loves chasing her ball!

This clever girl is eager to learn and is very trainable. If she is given the time and patience she needs to settle into her new life, she will make the most loyal and devoted family member.

Mona has met cats, but unfortunately, she seems scared of them. This makes her go on the offensive, so she will need a cat free home.

She is good with children, but preferably over the age of 5, since being a puppy she can still be a bit mouthy at times, and perhaps a little clumsy.

Please get in touch if you think you can give Mona the loving home she needs and deserves.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 6 month old female Shepherd cross. She is currently living in a foster home in Leeds and is available for meets and greets with potential adopters.

Lucy weighs 15kg now and is not expected to grow larger than 25-30kg. This sweet girl has been through a lot of hardship since she came into the world and would love to find a home and family to call her own.

She was born in a work yard in the middle of winter, and has survived almost freezing to death, serious illness, and being chased by dog catchers.

Despite everything she’s been through, she is so very sweet, loving and gentle. She is still a puppy and loves to play and run around! Lucy lives in a foster home with other dogs, and she could live with another dog (or dogs) or as an only dog.

Lucy would love a home with someone who enjoys being active. She’s doing really well in her foster home and is learning what it’s like to feel safe, get regular meals and treats, as well as going on short walks, discovering the outside world.

She is learning that cuddles are nice and will start to seek you out for snuggles when she’s feeling safe. Lucy has also discovered the joy of toys, and loves chasing her ball!

This clever girl is eager to learn and is highly trainable. If she is given the time and patience she needs to settle into her new life, she will make the most loyal and devoted family member.

Lucy has met cats, but unfortunately, she seems very scared of them. This makes her go on the offensive, so she will need a cat free home.

She is good with children, but preferably over the age of 5, since being a puppy she can still be a bit mouthy at times, and perhaps a little clumsy.

Please get in touch if you think you can give Lucy the loving home she needs and deserves.

name: Jordan
description:
He is yet another pointer found as a stray, likely discarded like rubbish by a hunter in Cyprus. He was found at the end of hunting season along with 2 other pointer boys.

He is so human oriented and loving that he doesn’t deserve to find himself in a shelter. We can only hope that his current scenario is better than his previous life.

Jordan happily shares his space with other dogs but what he truly loves is human affection and exciting walks. Once settled, it’s likely that he will be an active boy — he’s a pointer after all.

Jordan is a well rounded boy: good with dogs, friendly and loving with strangers and children, walks well on the leash, takes treats gently…there is nothing bad to say about him.

Due to his breed, it’s likely he will have medium-high energy levels once settled in a home. He will enjoy an active lifestyle but will also know how to chill and cuddle up under a blanket for the evening.

Jordan is not good with cats due to his prey drive so a home with no small furries is a must.

Jordan is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and castrated.

name: Chase
description:
Chase is a 9 month old male Labrador Retriever Cross.

Poor Chase entered the shelter when he was just a young pup. He is shy and is losing his puppyhood to a cage, seeing the same 4 walls day in day out.

He needs a nice home to help him settle so he can finish his puppyhood and make up for lost time. He will be medium sized when fully grown.

Chase has been cat tested and we think he would be OK living with cats with careful introductions (as you would with any dog).

Chase has been doing some leash training and is coming on well. But being out of his kennel is difficult for him as he is a shy boy in the shelter.

We just know that once he is in a home he will be able to be his true self and we really can’t wait to hear about his personality, we just need his family to notice him!

The good thing is, Chase loves his food so training should be enjoyable for both him and his new family.

Please give Chase a chance. It’s heartbreaking to see him still in the shelter.

If homed with children, they need to be older and patient and understand that Chase needs time to settle.

This boy is going to be the best companion for anyone lucky enough to adopt him.

Chase is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated.

name: Reuben
description:
Reuben is a 2-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is currently living in a small cage at a pound, which is clearly not enough to meet his needs. Spending only a short amount of time outside each day has left him desperate for a better life.

He is described as an energetic and playful boy, full of life and enthusiasm. His lively personality means he would benefit from a home that can give him both physical exercise and mental stimulation. Regular activity will be important to help him stay happy and balanced.

Reuben also loves human attention and enjoys being around people. This shows that he is affectionate and eager to bond with his future owner. A home where he can receive plenty of interaction will suit him best.

He is suitable to live with other dogs, which could help him feel more comfortable and engaged. However, he cannot live with cats, so a cat-free home is essential. Careful introductions to other dogs would still be beneficial.

Reuben would do best in a home with older children who can understand his energy levels and needs. A calmer but active household would help him settle in while still allowing him to express his playful nature. He needs a balance of structure and freedom.

Currently based in Cyprus, Reuben is willing to travel to the UK or Germany for the right home. This gives him a wider chance of finding someone who can offer him the life he deserves.

His situation makes it even more urgent for him to be given that opportunity.

He will be rehomed with a full adoption package, including vaccinations, microchipping, neutering, and blood tests. This ensures he is fully prepared for his transition into a new home.

The support provided helps make the process smoother for both him and his adopter.

A home check will be required as part of the adoption process. This is to ensure that Reuben is placed in a safe and suitable environment. The goal is to find him a stable and loving home where he can finally thrive.

Reuben is simply looking for a chance to leave his cage behind and experience real happiness. With the right care, attention, and space, he has the potential to become a loyal and joyful companion. He just needs someone willing to give him that chance.

name: Seth
description:
Seth is a young male English Pointer, approximately 10 months old, was found as a stray when he was just 6 months, and has been in a shelter in Cyprus ever since.

He is a typical pointer: super friendly, loving, cuddly, extremely human oriented, good with other dogs, and loves children and anyone he meets.

We suspect Seth may have been from an unwanted litter produced by a hunters dog. He was probably then dumped on the roadside to fend for himself away from everything he had ever known.

He was found with 2 other male pointers a few years older than him and has been happily living with them in a pack with some other female pointers aswell.

Seth will be a real treat to train and welcome into your home. Just as any pointer does, for those that are familiar with the breed, they make the most wonderful companions.

They don’t ask for much: a full belly, a warm sofa, a human to cuddle up with, and regular physical and mental stimulation. They go hard with their exercise but also enjoy their sofa time.

We really hope that Seth will get out of the shelter while he is still a pup.

Seth is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and will be castrated.

name: Rena
description:
Rena, 1 year old female mixed breed, friendly with everyone

Rena is such a sweet girl. If you are looking for a well rounded dog who is gentle and gets on with everyone, please consider Rena.

Rena is good with other dogs, strangers, people, and children. She has such a calming presence and you can tell she just wants to be loved. Not to mention she is also very pretty!

She walks well on the leash and is more interested in the people who are with her. She takes treats gently.

Although she is calm once out of her kennel, she does enjoy a good play with other dogs and has energy to burn.

Rena is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases.

name: Cody
description:
Cody – 3 year old male Jack Russell Terrier Cross. Whilst he might be small in size, he has the personality of dreams, never stops making everybody smile, and loves to make new friends.

Cody is a wonderful little dog with a heart full of love and a lot of character. Rescued from Romania as a puppy, he came to us with a traumatic injury to his tail, which required surgery.

He was quite a shy little pup but was adopted into a home fairly quickly.

Unfortunately, this was not the right environment for Cody and he never really settled, so a year later he was back at DC. He was adopted out again and, through no fault of his own, was returned within a few weeks as the resident dog did not like him.

Cody had been a perfect gentleman, so he came back yet again to live his best life with his Wonky friends.

Cody is a sweet and friendly dog once he’s settled but can be a little shy at first. Once he gets to know you, he’s an absolute bundle of fun!

He’s great with other dogs, loves to run around and play, and is always up for an adventure.

He’s also very curious and loves meeting new people while out on walks. Since being back in rescue, Cody’s behaviour has changed a lot and he is now a happy wee chappy with everyone he meets, including strangers.

We feel that much of his behaviour in his first home was due to his environment and that a quieter, relaxed home will bring out all of his positive attributes.

Cody has learned several commands, including Sit, Stay, Down, Watch, Come (his recall is good but could use reinforcement), and Leave It.

He is generally good on the lead and enjoys his walks, though he can be a bit stubborn at times.

Cody had shown some resource guarding in his first home but has been easily trained out of this with positive reinforcement techniques.

He should not be given bones or chew toys like yak chews, as he tends to guard them.

Cody is happy around humans on walks, even strangers, and loves to sniff them, but he’ll always do things in his own way and at his own pace.

He’s comfortable with being picked up and loves a cuddle. As Mother Wolf always says, “Never say never” for a new home, and although he is as happy as can be at the rescue, he deserves so much more and would love his own people and a home of his own.

We don’t think that Cody would like to live with small children, but older ones in a quiet home would be fine.

Cody is looking for a family who can give him the space and understanding he needs to feel safe and loved. Could that be you? If you think you’re the perfect match for Cody, we’d love to hear from you!

name: Lily
description:
Our extra special girl Lily is approximately six years old and a near perfect cross breed at the bottom end of medium sized. Lily weighs just fourteen kilos and measures fourteen inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found on the streets Lily has been in our Cyprus shelter for one month.

Our shelter manager reports that Lily is very timid and needs lots of reassurance. She is quiet, very sweet and walks beautifully on her lead. Which begs the question: what more does a girl have to do?

Lily is so attractive with her shining black coat and delicate features. Her gorgeous eyes are perfectly enhanced with her prize-winning ears and sublime expressions.

A very discerning adopting family will recognise the prize that Lily represents. She will be so grateful to join a quiet family in an orderly house with a steady routine. Paradise for all concerned.

Lily seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Bobby
description:
I’m now in a loving foster home near Newport, waiting for my forever family to find me.

I’m a small-sized boy originally from Cyprus, about 8 years old, and my biggest wish is to have a home that will love me, cherish me, and never abandon me again.

I used to have a family. For years, they were my world. But one day, they left me. They just walked away, leaving me behind. I don’t know where they went—maybe they moved or left the island—but I wasn’t part of their future plans.

At first, the shelter was a big adjustment, but I settled in and learned to trust again. The people there were kind, and I adored them—they gave me the cuddles and attention I missed so much.

Now, in foster, I’m showing just how sweet and loving I am. I dream of a home where I can feel safe, loved, and part of a family that will never leave me behind.I’m good with other calm dogs when introduced slowly, but I’d also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home. What matters most is having someone who can spend time with me during the day—I just want to be by your side.

A little note about my health:Because of the difficult life I had before, I now have early?stage kidney disease. But please don’t worry — I’m not on any medication. I just need to stay on a special kidney?friendly diet, which keeps me feeling well and happy. I really hope this won’t stop me from finding my forever home. I still have so much love to give.

If you’ve fallen in love with my story and want to give me a second chance at happiness, please reach out. I’m ready to fill your life with love, loyalty, and plenty of cuddles.

name: Kevin
description:
Meet Kevin, 1 year old, male crossbreed, medium to large size, friendly with everyone, ideal for first time adopters.

Kevin may not be a tiny puppy anymore, but his heart absolutely is. He’s pure good nature — loving, playful and full of gentle joy. Found as a stray, he’s taken every kindness and given it back tenfold.

He shares his space beautifully with male and female dogs and loves meeting everyone. Confident when approached, excited for walks, and always keen to play with passing dogs, he’s a soft, social boy with a bright spirit.

Kevin travels well, enjoys adventures and cuddles, and has medium energy. He’ll need the usual training, but he’s eager to learn and thrives with guidance.

He shows too much interest in cats to live with them and because he can be a bit bouncy, he’s best in a home without small dogs. He is ready for hikes, sofa snuggles, love and a family of his own,

Whether you’re a single person, a couple, or a family with children 12 plus, Kevin will fit right in. He has no issues at all — even first?time adopters would find him a dream.

Kevin is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, he will travel with a passport, fully vaccinated, tested for infectious diseases, neutered and microchipped.

name: Jackie
description:
This lovely boy is Jackie; a beautiful Malinois, with good looks and a lovely social demeanour.

He was very relaxed with a pack of 8 dogs when he stayed a few days in temporary foster, he likes people and is friendly with them, enjoys his walks and activities.

As experienced dog owners know, the Malinois breed needs active involvement and some mental stimulation, without which the Malinois can become anxious over time as they are not couch potatoes.

He has had some lead training, but he would revel with more obedience training. Jackie would make a wonderful companion for an active family and he would do very well with any outdoor activities.

We are looking for a home with or without another dog and children over 10 years old. Jackie hasn’t been tested for cats yet.

He is a good looking boy, with a lovely sable coat. Great with people and other dogs, a real character. Good on lead, healthy and has such wonderful, inquisitive nature.

name: Parisa
description:
Parisa is an 11 month old female small mixed breed currently in foster care in Doncaster. She is not yet spayed.

Parisa is an active and confident young dog with a curious and playful nature. She enjoys interaction with people and is affectionate and people-focused.

She is social with other dogs and lives well alongside them in her foster home, showing appropriate behaviour and taking guidance from older dogs. She has been child tested and interacted well.

Parisa is still developing her training as a young dog. She understands some basic commands and is responsive, although consistency will be required as she matures.

She walks on a harness but can be excitable on lead and will benefit from continued lead training. She is mostly housetrained but may have occasional accidents, particularly overnight.

She is crate trained but prefers to sleep in a shared space with other dogs.

Parisa enjoys play and will engage with toys and household items, so supervision and appropriate outlets for play will be important.

Parisa would suit an active home able to provide structure, routine and ongoing training as she progresses through adolescence.

name: Bob and Charlie
description:
We have the sad story of Bob and Charlie, who are 5 and a half year old Podenco cross brothers. They have the traditional, tan, short coats and they are gentle lads, with big hearts and very kind natures.

They are a little chunky atm, but we think that’s a reflection of how much they have been loved and how contented they are.

They love all people, no matter the age, and small kids will have their face licked off if the dogs can reach. They do not jump up, but will certainly welcome you and be happy to meet you.

As big as they are, they think they are lap dogs. At night, they love their owners so much, that they both like to sleep in their bedroom to be close.

The very sad part is that the boys owner just died, and their mum will have to downsize and maybe to a flat. She doesn’t want to let them go but she can’t see how she will cope and is looking for a home, if possible for both to remain together.

They have only known themselves for the last 5 and half years and we are looking for one owner for both, but I’m sure they wouldn’t mind being split if it meant not having to go into a shelter.

So to start, let’s just look for one new mum and dad and see how that goes!

There is a lot of information we need to get for them – ie how tall? Weight, But for now lets get them out there to show you all.

This is what their Mum says:Charlie is more dominant, he looks after his brother. he does like his love, especially his shoulders being massaged, but not as much as Bob. Bob could be tickled all day long, even to pulling your hand to keep stroking him when you stop.

They will sit watching while you eat, but they do not beg. If you open a biscuit tin or packet of cheese, does not matter where they are, they will smell or hear it. Their senses are amazing!

They can be left for a few hours, they will just sleep and I have had no complaints of any barking when i leave the house, the neighbours know when i arrive home though, they bark to greet.

They are good guard dogs, they only bark if there is a knock on the door or if someone is passing, but they are only saying hello we are here there is not a dangerous bone in their body.

They are good with other dogs, they used to have a little play mate, she ran them ragged. Although cats they would chase out of the garden.

They do need training on the lead, due to circumstances they have not been walked enough and not for a long time either. Bob will settle on the lead but Charlie tends to pull a lot and he is very strong, but I expect a halti will sort that.

They get excited in the car. Bob is very scared at the vets. Charlie has no problem. They have their passports Overall they are very laid back and relaxed dogs and I will be so sad to see them leave.

name: Presley
description:
Presley is a beautiful young American Bulldog Cross aged just 1 year and 7 months, with a gentle nature and a huge heart.

Since arriving into foster care, Presley has settled wonderfully into life in a busy multi-dog home and has shown herself to be an affectionate, loving, and eager-to-please girl who thrives on companionship and routine.

Although she can initially be a little shy when meeting new people, Presley warms up quickly once she feels safe and comfortable. Once she trusts you, her affectionate and sweet personality shines through.

Presley absolutely enjoys the company of other dogs and has formed lovely bonds with the larger mastiff dogs in her foster home.

She enjoys social interaction and companionship, but she is best suited to calmer, balanced dogs who help keep play and interactions relaxed.

She can occasionally become over-excited during play with higher-energy dogs but responds very well to calm guidance and supervision.

She is affectionate without being overly demanding and is becoming increasingly confident and relaxing independently. She now happily spends time sunbathing in the garden with her foster friends, while still loving cuddles and affection from her people.

Presley is currently living with a dog-savvy 6-year-old child and has been gentle and respectful. Due to her size and occasional excitable moments, older or dog-savvy children would be most suitable.

She walks on a harness and enjoys being active and social. She can initially be a little strong on the lead when excited, especially if something catches her attention, but she is intelligent, eager to learn, and responds well to calm, consistent handling.

Presley is crate trained, happily sleeps in her crate overnight, and can currently be left for around 4–6 hours. She has made excellent progress learning to settle independently and continues to grow in confidence every day.

Like many young dogs, Presley still requires sensible management around food and toys when living with other dogs. She is currently fed separately and toys are managed appropriately within the foster home.

Importantly, she remains gentle and respectful with people around food, treats, and affection.

Presley would thrive in a calm, structured home that can continue reinforcing boundaries, routine, and positive behaviours.

She would particularly suit owners with experience of bully breeds or active dogs who can provide consistency, guidance, and continued training.

Presley is an incredibly loving and rewarding young dog who has so much potential. With the right home, she will make an affectionate, loyal, and wonderfully devoted companion.

name: Rona
description:
Rona needs a patient home that will give her that time to trust and learn that not all people are bad. She warms up quite quickly if she feels safe and secure, she will be an excellent companion in the right home.

At just one year old, beautiful Rona is struggling with life in a busy Cyprus shelter. The noise, the constant movement, and the long days of waiting are overwhelming for a dog as gentle and sensitive as she is.

She tends to stay quiet in her kennel, watching everything around her, unsure how to cope with the chaos.

Rona doesn’t thrive behind kennel doors — she’s the kind of dog who needs the calm and reassurance of a real home, where she can finally feel safe, loved, and understood.

She can be reserved until she has had time to trust. When she has learnt to trust then she is a loving girl that will just curl up on your lap for a cuddle.

Rona is ready to form a strong connection with someone who will give her the security she’s been missing. She belongs in a home, where she can finally feel safe, loved, and understood.

Please don’t overlook her. Many quiet, sensitive dogs like Rona are passed by, and extended time in a shelter can be hard on them. She deserves a home, a family, and the warmth that comes with being cared for.

She can be adopted anywhere in the UK or Cyprus — her forever home could be with a family (children 12+) a couple, or a single adopter.

She walks well on the lead (once she has learnt to trust) and travels calmly, making her a lovely companion for days out and new adventures.

She is good with other dogs and shares her space with both males and females, large and small. She has not been cat tested but this can be arranged.

Rona will be neutered, fully vaccinated (including Rabies), microchipped, blood tested and have her own passport. Full rescue back-up with Saving Souls Animal Rescue – a UK based charity.

name: Nelson
description:
Nelson is a handsome 10-month-old Staffie Cross with a huge heart and an even bigger capacity for love. Still very much a youngster, he combines the fun and enthusiasm of a puppy with the calm, affectionate nature of a dog far beyond his years.

Since arriving into foster care, Nelson has quickly become a firm favourite thanks to his loving personality, excellent manners, and easy-going nature. He is the type of dog who simply enjoys being around people and being included in everyday life.

Nelson is a friendly and affectionate boy who loves spending time with his humans, whether that’s joining you on an adventure, relaxing at home, or enjoying a cuddle on the sofa.

He is equally happy playing with other dogs, exploring on walks, or settling down for one of his favourite activities — an afternoon nap.

He is very dog-friendly and has shown lovely social skills with the dogs he has met in foster care. Nelson enjoys canine company and could happily live with another friendly dog.

However, he would also be perfectly content as the only dog in the home, where he can soak up all the attention for himself.

Nelson has met children aged between 6 and 10 years old and has been gentle, calm, and happy to interact with them. He would be well suited to a family home with sensible, dog-savvy children who understand how to respectfully interact with dogs.

Although generally a confident young dog, Nelson can sometimes feel a little unsure in unfamiliar places.

When faced with something new, he may seek reassurance from his handler, but with encouragement and support his confidence continues to grow every day.

He is not particularly fond of heavy rain or loud noises, but copes well when guided by someone he trusts.

Nelson already has some lovely training foundations in place. He knows basic commands including sit and down, walks beautifully on the lead, and has excellent manners around the home.

He is non-destructive, settles well indoors, and can currently be left alone for around three hours without issue.

He is currently thriving on a Paleo Ridge raw diet and enjoys his meals immensely.

While Nelson is dog-friendly and small animal friendly, he is looking for a cat-free home. Careful introductions have been attempted with a cat during foster care, but his body language suggests he would be likely to chase, making a home with cats unsuitable.

Nelson is searching for a loving forever family who can continue helping him build confidence while giving him all the love and companionship he deserves.

Whether joining a home with another friendly dog or becoming someone’s one-and-only best friend, Nelson has all the makings of a truly wonderful companion.

Young, affectionate, well-mannered, and eager to please, Nelson is a special boy who will reward his future family with endless loyalty, love, and companionship.

name: Bonnie
description:
Our extra special girl Bonnie is approximately four years old and a fabulous cross breed at the top end of small maybe tipping into the bottom end of medium.

Bonnie weighs a perfect ten kilos and measures ten inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned by the side of a dual carriageway road, Bonnie has been in our Cyprus shelter for two months.

Our shelter manager describes Bonnie as absolutely delightful and with perfect manners. Bonnie oozes quality and style. She has film star looks with penetrating eyes and an array of glorious facial expressions.

Her appearance is just stunning. Bonnie has a shining black short hair coat with a super flash of white to her chest and tips.

Her stature is dapper with an enormous wow factor. Love at first sight with Bonnie is common amongst the shelter staff and volunteers.

A readymade family dog with so many attributes and so deserving. Bonnie loves a lap, a cuddle and one to one attention. Her adopters will be blessed.

Bonnie walks nicely on her lead and seems to mix perfectly with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Minnie
description:
Please meet Merry Minnie! Minnie is a gorgeous little crossbreed, we believe she is a pug x pekingnese, she is approx. 2 years old and weighs just 6.8kg.

Despite her very small size, she is a little pocket rocket and just loves life, she will happily take to anything and takes everything in her stride, in a word, she is amazing and whoever adopts her will be very lucky indeed!

Minnie was yet another stray left unclaimed in the pound. When she first arrived it was clear she had never lived with dogs before, she was horrified with them and was quite a bully, but now has settled and is well and truly part of the gang!

She loves chasing around with the other dogs and just generally loves life! Her smile brightens up any day, just look at it!

Minnie is full of energy and enthusiasm and will make you laugh all the time with her antics! She loves chasing the dogs around the farm, is great on lead and brilliant off lead in a secure field, she has no idea she is small and she keeps up with all the big guys!

Minnie is a beautiful little lady and will make a very rewarding addition to her new family. She has settled well into our routine and loves pack life, once she likes you, she follows you everywhere and just loves to be cuddled.

Minnie loves to greet you with a little Roo and tap dance, and honestly she is an adorable little girl, but she can be naughty and bullies any dog unlucky enough to be her size or smaller, although she does appear to have grown out of this behaviour now, she was a little madam when she first came hence why she has been with us so long and not put up for adoption sooner.

She is extremely loving and loyal and bonds very quickly to her people. She is also in to everything given the chance! Minnie is neutered, microchipped, de flead, wormed and vaccinated.

Minnie is house trained, being a small dog, if its cold and wet she will use pads! She walks well on the lead, is not destructive and can be left for short periods, She loves to be left snoozing on my bed and is often snuggled up with the cat!

Minnie is an inquisitive and responsive little lady, quick to learn and easy to train (but can be stubborn!).

She loves her home comforts and a cuddle, and likes to sleep on the bed with you if she is allowed; she will sleep downstairs on the sofa or in her own bed if she isn’t allowed in the bedroom. She is very food motivated which makes her easy to train!

Minnie travels very well in the car, she is just an all round pleasure to have. Whoever adopts this little lady will be very lucky indeed as she really has the most amazing character and cheeky face!

Minnie could live with children age 8 plus that are used to dogs. Can you offer this beautiful little lady the home he so desperately deserves?

name: Monty
description:
Monty is a handsome Cocker Spaniel, estimated to be 5–6 years old, who is looking for a loving forever home in the UK.

He is currently cared for in our small, cage-free home rescue in Bulgaria, where he lives as part of the family while waiting for his own.

Monty was sadly found abandoned and left to fend for himself on the streets of Bulgaria. Whatever happened in his past, he has left it behind and has quickly shown us what a truly lovely dog he is.

In fact, we’ve been trying to find something not to like about him…

Monty is calm, affectionate, gentle and incredibly easy to live with. He has settled beautifully into family life and simply enjoys being around people.

Whether it’s relaxing in the garden, joining you on a walk or curling up beside you in the evening, Monty is happiest just being included.

He mixes well with the other dogs in our care and would happily live with another friendly dog, although we also think he would enjoy being the only dog in a home where he could soak up all the attention.

At around 5–6 years old, Monty has left the puppy antics behind but still has many wonderful years ahead of him. He would suit someone looking for a loyal companion who enjoys both gentle adventures and quiet evenings at home.

Monty is the sort of dog who forms a close bond with his family, and we know whoever adopts him is going to wonder how they ever managed without him.

MicrochipPet passportFull vaccinations including rabiesBlood testsFlea and worm treatmentNeuteringDEFRA-approved transport to the UKLifetime rescue supportAt Rescue Dogs For Adoption, all of our dogs live in a home environment rather than kennels, allowing us to understand their personalities and carefully match them with the right families.

We consider all applicants, because finding the perfect home is what matters most.

If you think Monty could be the companion you’ve been waiting for, we’d love to hear from you.

name: Sid
description:
Sid is a five month old male Jack Russell Cross weighing around 5kg. He is a wonderfully social, happy, affectionate and funny little boy. He currently lives happily with 2 other dogs and is also good with cats.

Sid loves people and enjoys being involved in everything around him. He adores cuddles, loves to play, and has a cheerful personality that makes him a joy to have around.

He is already doing very well for his age. Sid walks nicely on the lead and travels well in the car. He is an affectionate and engaging puppy who is eager to learn and explore the world.

Sid is looking for a loving forever home where his playful nature, intelligence and wonderful personality will be appreciated, and where his family will have the time and patience to continue guiding him as he grows.

All our dogs are fully vaccinated, regularly dewormed, microchipped and vet checked.

name: Dolly
description:
Dolly is a beautiful large breed cross of just over four years old who is searching for a home where she can truly thrive.

Sadly, Dolly is returning to rescue due to a mismatch in energy levels within her previous home. This isn’t because she is a difficult dog or has done anything wrong.

Instead, she needs a calmer environment with clear boundaries, consistency, and owners who understand how to help her feel secure and relaxed.

Once Dolly feels safe, her wonderful personality shines through. She is affectionate, loyal, and forms incredibly strong bonds with her people.

While she can initially be a little nervous around strangers, a handful of treats and a little patience are usually all it takes before her soft, loving side appears.

Dolly adores human company and is a real cuddle lover. One of her favourite places to be is curled up next to her person, soaking up affection and enjoying life’s simple comforts.

She enjoys her walks and loves exploring new scents and environments. She is very food motivated, which makes her highly trainable and eager to learn. Around the home, Dolly is generally calm and relaxed, happy to settle down and enjoy family life.

Dolly has lived around children aged 5 and 9 years old and has shown herself to be a loving companion. Any children in the home should be dog-savvy and able to respect her space and boundaries.

While Dolly enjoys social interactions with dogs out and about, she would likely be happiest as the only dog in the home where she can fully relax and receive the attention she deserves.

For experienced owners, she could potentially live alongside a calm, balanced dog following careful introductions and ongoing management.

She walks well overall, although she can pull on the lead at times. A head collar has helped improve this significantly. She travels well in the car and enjoys getting out and about with her people.

Dolly is not currently crate trained, although crate training may help build her confidence and provide her with a safe space of her own.

She can show some anxiety when left alone, likely because she has become accustomed to having canine company around her. She has occasionally been lightly destructive, such as chewing slippers, but nothing excessive.

She has also shown some reactivity in situations involving high excitement levels and around food with other dogs.

These behaviours are manageable with structure, boundaries, and appropriate handling, and are another reason why a calmer home environment would suit her best.

Dolly is a bright, affectionate, and intelligent girl with so much love to give. Beneath everything is a dog who simply wants stability, understanding, and a family who will help her be the best version of herself.

For the right home, Dolly will be a fiercely loyal companion, an affectionate cuddle partner, and a devoted best friend.

name: Addy
description:
Addy is a 20 month old male German Shepherd Cross, a really great boy who is large in size and came to the UK from Romania around a year ago.

He is in foster in Evesham, Worcestershire. His foster describes him as just a big baby. He loves to follow her around, loves toys, is house trained, likes other dogs, and lives with several others.

He is playful and good on walks, though if he sees a cat he will jump up on his back legs like a kangaroo.

Addy is looking for a home with someone who has plenty of time for him and can give him a fun and active life, along with a nice garden.

No children, so that he can be the centre of someone’s world. A quiet home is ideal. He can live with another dog.

Addy will make a great companion to the right person, ideally someone with experience. He is neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, and has a passport.

Please consider this wonderful boy. Adoption fee is £425, a home check is required, and there is rescue backup.

name: Aurin
description:
Aurin is an eleven month old female mixed breed dog, born in May 2025, and weighing around twenty kilograms. She is currently located in Glasgow and is fully vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, and in good health.

Aurin is a playful, curious, and active young dog with a loving and affectionate nature. She enjoys being around people and thrives on attention, happily seeking out cuddles and companionship.

She forms strong bonds and loves to be included in everyday life.

She has a bright and intelligent personality and is eager to learn, showing great potential with the right guidance and consistency.

Aurin brings a lovely energy into the home and would suit an active lifestyle where she can engage both mentally and physically.

Aurin is still developing and learning about the world, so she is looking for a home with prior experience with rescue dogs.

She will need adopters who understand that rescue dogs often require time, patience, and compassion to fully settle and feel secure.

She will benefit from a structured environment with clear boundaries, consistency, and gentle guidance. With the right support, Aurin will grow into a well-balanced, loyal, and devoted companion.

Aurin is a loving, engaging, and intelligent young dog who is ready to find a home where she will be understood, supported, and truly belong.

name: Lucho
description:
Lucho is a male cross-breed dog who will be 3 in May 2026. He is at the Nicosia Sanctuary in Cyprus.

The boy with the biggest smile and the curliest tail!

Lucho was brought to us by the local municipality. He was picked up as a stray and as usual, no microchip and no one came forward to claim him.

What has impressed us about this sweet dog is how quickly he adjusted to life at the sanctuary and how well he gets on with other dogs. Especially if they are playful and like a good bitey-face session!

Even though Lucho was un-neutered when he came to us, he is happy to hang out with both male and female dogs of all descriptions.

But his favourite friends are Snow and Indie who will play with him for hours, chewing on each others legs and ears. He’s very happy for the girls to be in charge, just as long as they keep on playing!

For the first day or two Lucho was a little unsure of us humans but that changed very quickly. He’s now friendly and affectionate, even with new people. Although, given the choice he will choose to play with a doggy friend.

He would love a home with another resident, playful dog. This isn’t a must though, he’d also be happy as an only dog, meeting his friends in the park.

Lucho seems to us like a lovely, well-balanced dog. He’s quite active, but is also happy to relax in his kennel once he’s been out and had a good play. He’ll happily keep himself busy with a nice chew or a toy.

We really like this handsome dog and we’re sure that his forever family will love him too!

SPDC adoption package and homechecks apply.

name: Daniel
description:
Daniel is a medium to large sized crossbreed aged around three years old. Daniel fostered Ipswich Suffolk.

Daniel was rescued from a sheepfold in Romania when he was a puppy. The shepherd called a known rescuer and said that he was going to “get rid”of all the dogs because there were too many.

When rescuers went for them they were all tied very tightly in a sealed cardboard box. One of the pups was even tied at the muzzle. They were seconds away from suffocation.

Daniel and two of his sisters were not lucky enough to get adopted as pups and so grew up in the private shelter. Safe and loved but in a pen not experiencing the joys of their own home. Daniel is now in a UK foster home awaiting an adoption offer.

Daniel is a happy and affectionate boy with a lot of love to give. He mixes well with other dogs but would also be happy as the only dog in his forever home, he’s also fine with cats. He could live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Zora
description:
Zora is a female, medium sized crossbreed pup aged around eight to nine months old. Zora fostered Norwich Norfolk

Zora and her mum and siblings were rescued from a kill shelter in Romania. Sadly no adoption offers were forthcoming for any of the family and when we met them at a private shelter in June we agreed to bring them to the UK to find new homes.

Zora is initially a little timid but is learning the ways of her new world in her UK foster home. She would benefit from the company of another dog in her foster home but could also be the only pet.

She would be ok to live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Juny
description:
Juny is a female, medium sized crossbreed pup aged around eight to nine months old.Juny fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Juny and her mum and siblings were rescued from a kill shelter in Romania. Sadly no adoption offers were forthcoming for any of the family and when we met them at a private shelter in June we agreed to bring them to the UK to find new homes.

Juny is the most confident of the siblings and the quickest to learn the ways of her new world in her UK foster home. She would benefit from the company of another dog in her foster home but could also be the only pet.

She would be ok to live with respectful children aged eight plus.

name: Boba
description:
Boba is a small crossbreed male aged around ten months old. Boba fostered Dereham Norfolk.

Boba was rescued from a landfill site in Romania along with his brother. He is now in a UK foster home and waiting for the offer of a forever home.

Boba is a sweet and friendly little chap who loves humans and other dogs alike. He enjoys his walks and loves playing with his toys. He is a cuddly and affectionate little chap.

Boba could live with or without other dogs in his forever home and will need all of the usual training input that an adolescent dog requires.

He isn’t cat tested. But can live with respectful children 5plus

name: Lola
description:
Lola is a medium sized crossbreed. Her passport says she is aged around four years old but we think she could be around six or seven. Lola fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Lola and her four pups were rescued from a kill shelter in Romania. Sadly no adoption offers were forthcoming for any of the family and when we met them at a private shelter in June we agreed to bring them to the UK to find new homes.

Lola is a calm, sweet and friendly girl who enjoys the company of people. Unusually she seems particularly drawn to men but she is happy to get attention from everyone.

She walks nicely on a lead and enjoys her walks. She could live with respectful children aged eight plus.

Lola could live with another calm dog if it wasn’t too in her personal space but would probably prefer to be the only dog in the home. She’s not great with cats.

name: Bruna
description:
Bruna is a female, medium sized crossbreed pup aged around eight to nine months old. Bruna fostered Hempnall Norfolk

Bruna and her mum and siblings were rescued from a kill shelter in Romania. Sadly no adoption offers were forthcoming for any of the family and when we met them at a private shelter in June we agreed to bring them to the UK to find new homes.

Bruna is initially a little timid but is learning the ways of her new world in her UK foster home. She would benefit from the company of another dog in her foster home but could also be the only pet.

She would be ok to live with respectful children aged ten plus.

name: Johnny
description:
Meet Little Johnny — a truly adorable little chap currently thriving in his UK foster home in Cleethorpes. He’s neutered, 1 year old this month, male, small cross breed, neutered, lots of energy and has settled in beautifully.

Johnny is a bright, cheerful soul with a wonderfully cheeky personality.

He’s making great progress with his toilet training and has just begun exploring the world on his walks. He’s good on both lead and harness, curious about everything he sees, and is gradually becoming more confident around traffic.

Johnny is living with an older female dog at the moment, but he would absolutely love a younger, playful companion to match his energy. He cannot live with cats.

He hasn’t met children yet, so we would suggest children aged 12+.

He is such a sweet, happy youngster who’s ready for his forever home.

name: Leo
description:
Leo is a medium English Setter, 3 years old.

Leo is a very handsome English setter, abandoned by his hunter as he was no longer wanted.

He’s a very cheerful, sociable, playful and noble lad. He’s very affectionate and loves having a big fuss made of him, even by strangers.

He doesn’t show any fears in the shelter environment and is great with playful, loving to play with them. He’s been great with the other dogs too and could live with a resident dog or as an only dog in the home.

Leo has a scar on his left eye which you can see in his photos. This was caused by an injury involving a stick whilst hunting. He can see with this eye other than a small area where the scar is.

It doesn’t affect him or slow him down, he lives a completely normal life.

Leo has not yet been cat tested but can be for the right home.

name: Eric
description:
Eric is a small to medium appx 2 yr old bodeguero ratonero.

Introducing Eric, a very handsome little Spanish Ratonero Bodeguero whose cheerful personality shines through every day. He turned up at a local animal shelter and was advertised but no one came forward to claim him.

Eric is approximately 2 years old and weighs around 9.7kg, making him a small companion with a big heart. Several months ago, Eric appeared to us and as stated, no one came forward.

He was exhausted by the heat, and thanks to the dedication of caring volunteers, Eric has truly blossomed and is now a happy, confident little dog who brings joy wherever they go.

Eric loves his daily walks with volunteers and enthusiastically plays with other kennel mates. Eric walks nicely on the lead, suggesting he has come from a home environment and not a stray.

Surrounded by ten other dogs of various ages, sizes, and both males and females, Eric gets along well and enjoys being part of the group. He is a true sweetheart and is spending some time with a foster family -they are all loving his company.

He loves to sit up on the sofa for snuggles. He is playful and enjoys the company of other dogs.

Recently neutered and fully vaccinated, Eric’s blood tests are all clear, and he is ready to find his very own family.

Eric’s affectionate nature means he loves curling up on a human lap for cuddles, and is going to make someone or a family a very loving and fun little companion.

name: Chase
description:
Chase is a medium-sized cross-breed of approximately 9 months old.

Chase is currently living in a cage-free foster home in Bulgaria and is ready to travel to the UK via DEFRA-approved transport.

Chase was rescued as a young puppy and has grown into a gentle, sweet-natured boy. He has a naturally shy personality and can be cautious when meeting new people or experiencing new situations, but there is absolutely no malice in him.

He simply needs a little patience and understanding while he learns to trust.

He is a calm, non-reactive dog who prefers a quieter lifestyle and would thrive in a home where he can settle at his own pace. Chase is not demanding and is happy to relax nearby once he feels comfortable and secure.

One of Chase’s favourite things is the company of other dogs. He mixes beautifully with dogs of all sizes and gains confidence from having canine companions around him.

He is particularly gentle with smaller dogs and puppies and would happily live with another friendly resident dog.

Chase could also live as an only dog, provided his new family understands that he may need a little extra time and reassurance while adjusting to his new surroundings.

Due to his sensitive nature, we feel Chase would be happiest in a home with older teenage children or adults only. A busy household with young children would likely overwhelm him.

He is fully vaccinated, microchipped, castrated, has completed blood tests and holds a pet passport ready for travel.

Chase is looking for a kind, patient family who can see beyond his initial shyness and allow his lovely personality to shine through. For someone willing to give him that opportunity, he will make a loyal and devoted companion.

WhatsApp us for an informal chat and to meet Chase on live video.

name: Robbie
description:
Robbie is a small cross-breed puppy of approximately 8 months old as of June 26.

Robbie is currently living in a cage-free foster home in Bulgaria and is expected to remain a small dog when fully grown.

Like many of our rescue puppies, Robbie had an uncertain start in life, but he has blossomed into a happy, affectionate and well-socialised young boy who is now ready to find a family of his own.

Robbie has a wonderful temperament. He is friendly, loving and enjoys human company.

He likes to be involved in family life and is always happy to join in whatever is going on, whether that’s playtime in the garden, a walk, or simply relaxing with his people.

He mixes beautifully with other dogs and enjoys making new canine friends. He is also comfortable around cats and has been raised alongside a variety of animals in his foster environment.

As a young puppy, Robbie is curious, intelligent and eager to learn. He is being raised in a home environment where he is exposed to everyday household sounds, routines and experiences, giving him an excellent foundation for life in his future home.

Robbie would suit a wide variety of households, including families, couples, older adopters and homes with existing pets.

Most importantly, he is looking for a family who will continue his training, provide plenty of love and include him as part of the family.

He will travel on DEFRA registered transport to you with vaccinations, microchip, blood tests and a pet passport, together with ongoing rescue back-up for life.

Robbie is a sweet little boy with a bright future ahead of him and is sure to make a wonderful companion for a lucky family.

WhatsApp us for an informal chat and to meet Robbie on live video.

name: Nora
description:
Nora is a beautiful lilac and white Staffie Cross puppy who is looking for her forever home.

At just three months old, she is already showing all the qualities that make Staffies such wonderful family companions – affectionate, sociable, playful, and full of love.

Nora has settled exceptionally well into foster care and has adapted beautifully to family life. She is a happy, confident little puppy who enjoys spending time with people and making friends wherever she goes.

She is currently living alongside other dogs and has shown herself to be very dog friendly. Nora enjoys playing, learning from canine companions, and would happily live with another friendly resident dog.

Equally, she would thrive as the centre of attention in a loving home.

Nora is also living successfully with cats and has shown a calm and respectful attitude towards them, making her suitable for a home with cat-friendly felines.

She has spent time around children aged seven years and has been wonderful with them, showing a gentle and affectionate nature. As with all puppies, interactions should always be supervised while she continues to learn appropriate manners.

Nora is crate trained and settles well in her crate. She can currently be left for up to four hours, although as a young puppy, toilet training remains a work in progress and her new family should be prepared to continue this.

Lead walking is still very new to Nora. She currently finds the outside world a little overwhelming at times, but her confidence is growing every day.

She takes reassurance from other dogs and is gradually learning that new experiences can be fun and rewarding.

Nora has shown no signs of reactive or aggressive behaviour and has adapted wonderfully to living with dogs, cats, and children. Her friendly, easy-going temperament means she could fit into a variety of different homes.

She is currently fed a raw diet and is thriving on it.

Nora is looking for a family who can continue her training, socialisation, and development while providing the love, patience, and guidance every puppy needs. In return, she promises a lifetime of companionship, affection, and plenty of puppy cuddles.

Nora is a truly lovely little girl with a bright future ahead of her and will make a fantastic addition to a lucky family.

name: Nico
description:
Nico is a handsome red Staffie Cross of around 10 months old who is looking for a loving forever home. Despite a difficult start in life, he has blossomed into a gentle, affectionate, and adaptable young dog who has so much love to give.

Nico has settled beautifully into foster care and has proven himself to be a well-mannered and easy-going companion. He enjoys spending time with both people and animals and forms strong bonds with those around him.

One of Nico’s greatest strengths is his wonderful social nature. He is dog friendly and has integrated extremely well with other dogs in foster care.

He is also cat friendly and has shown a calm and respectful attitude towards feline companions. Having lived alongside a seven-year-old child, Nico has demonstrated a gentle and affectionate nature that makes him suitable for a family home.

In the home, Nico is crate trained and approximately 95% toilet trained. He settles well indoors and is not destructive, displaying only the occasional mischievous puppy behaviour expected from a youngster his age.

When left alone, he may initially cry for a few minutes but quickly settles and has comfortably been left for up to four hours.

Nico is still building confidence when out and about. He can be nervous on walks and sometimes finds the outside world a little overwhelming, but he is making excellent progress with patient guidance and encouragement.

As his confidence grows, he is becoming increasingly comfortable exploring new environments.

He is also discovering the joys of toys and playtime and now becomes wonderfully excited when it is time for games and interaction with his people.

Nico is believed to have a hearing impairment and appears to be hard of hearing rather than completely deaf. This does not impact his loving personality or ability to enjoy life.

He takes confidence from the dogs around him and copes incredibly well with daily life. If adopted as an only dog, his new family should be prepared to continue building his confidence and communication skills using positive reinforcement and consistent routines.

Nico is currently fed a raw diet and is thriving on it.

Nico is a truly special young dog with a gentle soul and a bright future ahead of him. He would suit a variety of homes and will reward his new family with endless loyalty, affection, and companionship.

For someone willing to continue his journey and help him grow in confidence, Nico will make an exceptional family companion and best friend.

name: Juno
description:
Juno is an adorable three-month-old Staffie Cross puppy with a beautiful lilac coat and a personality that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Since arriving into foster care, Juno has charmed everyone she meets with her affectionate, friendly, and social nature. She is a happy little puppy who enjoys human company and loves being involved in everything that’s going on around her.

Juno has shown excellent manners with other dogs and enjoys their company. She would happily live with another friendly resident dog who can help continue teaching her about the world, but she would also thrive as the centre of attention in a loving family home.

She has also been assessed around a dog-savvy cat and has shown a gentle and respectful attitude, meaning she could potentially live successfully in a cat-friendly home.

As you would expect from a puppy of her age, Juno is still learning all the important life skills she will need as she grows. She is intelligent, eager to engage with her people, and responds well to positive interaction and encouragement.

Her new family should be prepared to continue her training, socialisation, and development as she matures.

Juno has settled exceptionally well into foster life and is already crate trained. She sleeps happily in her crate and can currently be left for up to four hours without issue.

Like all puppies, she can occasionally be mischievous, but this is simply part of normal puppy development and is easily managed with supervision, routine, and appropriate enrichment.

As she is still awaiting completion of her vaccinations, Juno has not yet started lead walking. Once she is ready to explore the outside world, she will benefit from reward-based training to help build her confidence and develop good lead manners.

One thing potential adopters should be aware of is that Juno may have a hearing impairment. She appears able to hear certain tones, pitches, and volumes but does not respond consistently to all sounds.

This does not impact her loving personality, ability to learn, or quality of life. Many dogs with partial hearing loss live happy and fulfilling lives using hand signals, visual cues, and consistent routines.

Juno is currently fed Beta kibble and is thriving on her diet.

Juno is looking for a committed family who can provide the love, patience, guidance, and training every young puppy needs. In return, she promises a lifetime of affection, companionship, and plenty of puppy cuddles.

For anyone looking to welcome a sweet, affectionate, and incredibly special puppy into their lives, Juno could be the perfect addition to the family.

name: Peggy
description:
Peggy is a 9-year-old female Deerhound Cross Wolfhound. She is a large breed dog who is looking for a calm and settled home where she can enjoy a quieter pace of life.

Peggy previously lived in a rural home and was accustomed to country walks and regular outings to the local coffee shop and pub.

She has experience living in a multi-dog household and has shown that she can live alongside other dogs.

Despite this, her ideal home would be one where she can be the only dog, allowing her to enjoy a peaceful environment and receive all the attention she deserves.

A home with a retired person or someone who works from home would suit her particularly well.

Peggy is not a demanding dog and is happy with a balanced lifestyle that includes a pleasant walk followed by a comfortable snooze.

She appears to enjoy a relaxed routine and would thrive with owners who appreciate a gentle companion. Her laid-back nature makes her well suited to a quieter household.

She has good manners in the home and is clean indoors. Peggy is also lead trained, making walks straightforward and enjoyable. In addition, she can be left alone when needed, which provides flexibility for her future owners.

Peggy has been waiting for a home for five months and is ready to find a family that can offer her the calm and comfortable lifestyle she enjoys.

She would benefit from a home without children and cannot live with cats. With the right home environment, Peggy has all the qualities needed to be a loyal and easy-going companion.

name: Indie
description:
Indie is an 18 month old female small Cross-Breed.

This gorgeous girl is an absolute joy – calm, gentle and full of love. She is affectionate and has a very sweet nature. She can be a little shy in new situations and meeting new people but a good natured resident dog will make all the difference.

She travels well in the car especially when she realises there is a good walk in the offing. She loves to smell all the different things around her from wildflowers to rabbit poo!

She really loves going to the beach where she can roll in the sand and have a really good run around.

Indie walks beautifully on the lead and her recall has come on well. Indie loves playing with other dogs and having a friendly dog to snuggle up with.

She is an absolutely super little girl and all she wants now is a loving home of her own with a resident dog to be her best friend.

Originally from Romania, indie was rescued with her siblings from a hoarding situation there.

Please get in touch if you can give Indie the forever home she needs and deserves.

name: Margot
description:
Margot is an 18-month-old female Collie Cross. She is a medium-sized dog based in York and is looking for a patient and understanding home.

Margot came into rescue in Romania with her mother and siblings when she was just a tiny puppy after spending time in a shelter.

She has been in her foster home for one month and is gradually settling into her new surroundings. Margot is a shy and gentle girl who is still building her confidence.

She would benefit greatly from living with other dogs, as their presence helps her feel more secure and encourages her confidence to grow.

Margot enjoys the company of other dogs and is suitable to live in a home with canine companions. She can also live with dog-savvy cats that understand how to interact respectfully with dogs.

Her calm and gentle nature means she has the potential to fit well into the right household environment.

She can live with older children who will be patient and considerate of her shy personality. A quieter home that allows her to settle at her own pace would help her continue making progress. Her future family should be prepared to give her time to adjust and develop trust.

Margot is mostly clean in the home, although she may occasionally have the odd accident as she continues to settle and learn. She is currently undergoing lead training and is making progress with this important skill.

She can also be left alone when accompanied by another dog, which provides her with reassurance and companionship.

With continued support, understanding, and the company of other dogs, Margot has every opportunity to flourish.

She is a sweet-natured young dog who is looking for a loving home where she can continue to gain confidence and enjoy life as part of a family.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 7-year-old Beagle cross, likely mixed with a smaller terrier breed. She’s on the smaller side of medium, full of personality, and ready to find the forever home she so deserves.

Rescued from the streets of Cyprus while pregnant, Lucy’s puppies were quickly adopted, but she has been waiting in kennels for over two years. Despite this, her zest for life and love for people remains unshaken.

Lucy is a people-oriented dog who adores human interaction. She’s confident, friendly with new people, and her playful, cheeky personality makes her a joy to be around.

When let out of her kennel, she sprints like a rocket but quickly circles back to you for belly rubs. Her favourite pastime is splitting her energy between zoomies and lounging in the dirt for cuddles, always with her tail wagging furiously.

Lucy is energetic but not overwhelming, and with a more active lifestyle, she’s ready to thrive. She loves being outdoors, exploring green spaces, or playing in a secure garden. Her ideal home would be outside the city, with access to safe spaces where she can run and play.

While she does need some basic training (like curbing her tendency to jump up in excitement), Lucy is eager to please and already well-behaved in many ways—she returns to her kennel without protest after playtime.

Lucy is good with other dogs but doesn’t need a resident canine companion to be happy. She’d also be a lovely fit for families with children aged 6+ due to her friendly temperament, though her playful energy might require supervision at first. An adult-only home with plenty of love, cuddles, and treats would also suit her well.

Though currently living in a kennel, Lucy’s adaptable nature means she’ll likely settle quickly into a home environment. She has a clean bill of health and is ready to travel from Cyprus to meet her new family.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a beautiful Segugio Italiano cross, estimated to be around 4-5 years old. She’s on the smaller side of medium and has been patiently waiting for almost three years to find her forever home.

Found abandoned and severely underweight, Freya has been cared for by a local boarding kennel in Cyprus, where she’s blossomed into a gentle, affectionate, and sweet-natured dog.

Freya is slightly reserved and shy when meeting new people, but she has made significant progress in building her confidence, thanks to her kennel mate, Ira. She thrives in calm and predictable environments and would do best with a patient family who can help her continue to grow.

Freya gets along well with other dogs and has a submissive nature in group settings. She enjoys canine company but is also content living as the only dog, provided her adopters give her plenty of attention and reassurance. If there is a resident dog, it might help Freya settle in faster, but it’s not a requirement for her to thrive.

Freya would be best suited to a semi-rural home with a garden where she can engage in scentwork and sniffing games, which help her relax and exercise her natural instincts. Busy households or homes with younger children might overwhelm her, so a calm home with children aged 10+ would be ideal.

True to her scent hound heritage, Freya loves to explore her surroundings, sniffing and searching for treats. She is very food motivated, which is a fantastic way to build trust with her. Freya takes treats gently and patiently waits her turn, endearing herself to everyone she meets.

Although she might be shy initially, Freya’s sweet and affectionate nature will shine once she forms a bond with you. Watching her transition from kennel life to a loving home will be incredibly rewarding.

Freya is healthy and ready to travel from Cyprus to her forever home. Could you be the one to give this lovely girl the peace and happiness she deserves?

name: Gaston
description:
Gaston is a two year old Labrador mix who arrived recently after being found running among traffic.

Once again, without a microchip, there was no way to know if anyone was missing him, and he was admitted to the shelter in the hope a family might come and claim him as their own.

Unfortunately, that never happened, and now we’re looking for Gaston’s forever home.

At the moment Gaston shares his kennel with a number of other dogs, both males and females. He has slotted in really well and gets on with everyone he meets.

He has an energetic, silly style of play and loves a bit of rough and tumble with other dogs, but he can also read the room and knows when it’s time to stop.

Gaston is still a young dog, and he’s therefore looking for a more active lifestyle with a family who can take him on long walks and engage in some basic training with him, to help him let off some steam and to give him some mental focus too.

Although he comes across as quite the goofball, there are some brain cells in that big head of his, and he does actually like to learn. He loves being made a fuss of and gets very excited when he’s praised for being a good boy.

Gaston is still working on lead training, and he can be quite strong when he pulls so this is an area that may need some continued work by his new family.

He is responsive to positive reinforcement, and unsurprisingly for a Labrador type, he loves food as a reward! He can also get over-excited quickly and will jump up without realising his size can be a bit overwhelming!

With this in mind, he would be better suited to a home with slightly older children who are used to being around dogs. We’re confident this behaviour can be improved with training, but there’s only so much we can achieve in a shelter setting.

Gaston is a very friendly, loving, goofy and sociable dog, and he would make a lovely companion in the right home.

We’re unsure if Gaston has lived in a conventional home setting before, so he will need some patience as he adapts to a new lifestyle, but as he’s so people oriented we’re sure with lots of reassurance he will settle in quickly.

The ideal home for Gaston would be based outside of the city with direct access to a secure garden.

He’d really benefit from some introductory training to improve his manners and build a strong bond with his new family, and he would also love a fairly active lifestyle.

He loves rolling around in the grass at the shelter, napping under the shade of the trees, and digging in the dust, so a family who spend a lot of time outside would be perfect for him.

He is such a silly love bug with a heart of gold, and we’d love to see him find the forever home he deserves.

name: Rex
description:
Rex is a 2 year old male Cross-Breed who was surrendered by his owner after previously living in a home.

We know he lived in a home before, which makes it even more heartbreaking that he has known comfort and a human companion and has now found himself in a cage day in and day out.

It is not unusual for dogs like Rex to find themselves waiting in kennels for months or even years due to their intimidating size. But Rex is the calmest and biggest softy.

Rex is remarkably sweet and affectionate with people. He adores fuss and craves a good cuddle. Having said that, he does not like other dogs, so he needs to be homed as the only dog.

We do not want Rex to lose the best years of his life in a cage. His size should not matter. He is a dog and deserves a home just like the small, cute, fluffy dogs that get adopted so easily. Rex will be a wonderful companion.

Rex can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. He has been tested for infectious diseases, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

His adoption fees are sponsored, so we are only asking for travel costs.

name: Gabriella
description:
Gabriella is a 2 year old female Cross-Breed who is friendly, affectionate, and ready to find her forever home.

Gabriella arrived at the shelter with her brother Gabriel a year ago. They were found together as strays. From the minute they arrived, they were super friendly and loving towards the shelter staff.

For a while, they shared a kennel just the two of them and were very attached. To give them a better chance at adoption, they are now mixing with other dogs and can be adopted separately or together. They will be OK either way.

We think they are approximately 2 years old. They both get on well with other dogs, usually quite aloof and in their own little world. They are well behaved and adore people and lots of cuddles.

Both of them require a home that will take them on exciting walks and preferably have a large garden for them to run around in.

Both Gabriel and Gabriella have been superstars in the shelter. We just hope their situation changes soon. Living their young lives in a small kennel is not what they are here for.

They are here to be adored, and you will get plenty of love and cuddles in return.

Gabriel and Gabriella can be adopted in Cyprus or in the UK. They are both ready to fly. They will be neutered, vaccinated, and have a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

name: Stratos
description:
Meet Stratos, a 2 year old male Pointer Cross currently in Cyprus.

Upon meeting Stratos on a recent trip to Cyprus, I can honestly say this boy broke me. Huddled in a compound with many other dogs, Stratos struggled to be seen.

The dogs rushed the fencing for attention. Poor Stratos tried his best to get to the people, making some fuss. But he missed out, overcome by the crowd. His face was full of sorrow and sadness. The shelter team told me his passion is human interaction but rarely did he get it.

I managed to get him out of the compound for a little one to one time. His little face literally lit up when he saw I’d chosen him to come out.He totally adored the attention, loved being fussed and stroked. He gave the best kisses ever.He pulled at my heartstrings like few dogs do.

The shelter team informed me he had Leishmania, treated without any issues, the remnants of which were still visible on his face, some fur loss that will grow back in time.
